EditReportRequest.description: Request body for `edit-report`. Can target ANY of the team's inbox reports, not just scout-authored ones.

actionability.description:
Optional new actionability call, for when new evidence changed your judgment. Replaces the report's actionability decision and re-runs autostart: `immediately_actionable` can open a draft PR, `requires_human_input` and `not_actionable` stop autostart from opening one. The report's inbox status does not change. Send it with `actionability_explanation`, and with `already_addressed` when the issue is handled, since the three replace the decision as one unit.

* `immediately_actionable` - immediately_actionable
* `requires_human_input` - requires_human_input
* `not_actionable` - not_actionable

actionability_explanation.description: 2-3 sentence evidence-grounded justification for `actionability`. Required when you set it.

already_addressed.description: Whether the issue is already handled: fixed, or with a fix in flight. Part of the actionability decision, so it requires `actionability` and `actionability_explanation` too; omitted means false. Set it when a fix lands or starts, so autostart does not open a duplicate PR.

append_evidence.description: Optional observations to add to the report's evidence rail, each becoming a bound signal attributed to this scout — adds to the report's evidence rather than replacing it. Use this for a new observation a reader should be able to check, and `append_note` for commentary (the owning team knows, a deploy fixed it). The report's signal count and weight move with the appended rows. Emit plus every append share a cap of 50 signals per report.

append_note.description: Optional free-form note to append to the report's work log, attributed to this scout. Prefer it over rewriting a report you did not author: a note is additive and keeps the audit trail.

charts.description: The full set of charts the report should show. Replaces the report's charts rather than adding to them, the way `summary` replaces the summary — so read the report first and send every chart you want kept. Omit the field (or send null) to leave the report's existing charts untouched, and send an empty list to take them all down.

corroboration_only.description: Set only when `append_note` confirms the finding with no new information. The first four confirmations stay in the work log as entries; later ones only raise the report's corroboration count. Other notes always stay in the work log.

expected_reviewers.description: Report reviewer_assignment.state read before selection began. Required when reviewer corrections are enabled.

links.description: Typed, directed links from this report to others, recording how the work relates. Use `depends_on` when you split one finding into a stack and the second report's fix cannot land until the first one's does, so the order is recorded rather than left to a reader of the diffs. Additive: links join what the report already has rather than replacing them, and only this report gets a row, so link from the side the sentence starts at. Links of the same kind must stay acyclic and every report must be in this project.

metrics.description: The report's full impact-metric set, at most 6. Omit it or send null to keep the current set, send an empty list to clear it, or send the complete replacement. Mark one metric `primary` for the key observation and the rest `supporting`, for users, sessions, occurrences, conversion, latency, or revenue. Every metric needs a live `query`: an InsightVizNode wrapping one bounded TrendsQuery built only from EventsNode or ActionsNode sources, with at most 1000 estimated longitudinal points. An affected-users metric counts distinct people through one series with `math: dau`; never sum its buckets. A `value`/`value_at` snapshot is only an optional cached fallback, and a metric without a query is invalid.

priority.description:
Optional new priority (`P0`-`P4`), for when the issue escalated or eased. Replaces the report's priority and re-runs autostart, which needs a priority to open a draft PR. Requires `priority_explanation`.

* `P0` - P0
* `P1` - P1
* `P2` - P2
* `P3` - P3
* `P4` - P4

priority_explanation.description: 2-3 sentence justification for `priority`. Required when `priority` is set.

pull_requests.description: GitHub pull request URLs (`https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<number>`) that fix what this report describes, when you found a fix that a person or another agent already opened. A linked pull request is the report's implementation: the report resolves on its own when every linked pull request is closed or merged and at least one merged, and a merged pull request resolves it at once. Additive: a pull request the report already links is skipped. Linking does not claim the report and does not change the pull request itself (no labels, reviewers, or ready-for-review). Link only a pull request whose diff targets this report's cause. The edit refuses a pull request outside the report's repository, one GitHub cannot read, and one closed without merging. At most 5 per call.

report_id.description: Id of the report to edit (must belong to this project).

repository.description: Optional repository to point the report at, as `owner/repo` — the fix for a report that surfaced against the wrong codebase, so you correct it in place instead of filing a duplicate. It replaces the report's current target and re-runs autostart, so a report that had no repository to open a PR against can now open a draft PR. Omit the field to leave the target as it is, and pass the `NO_REPO` sentinel for a report where nothing under version control could change. The response's `repository` reads the target back from the report, and the call fails when the target you named did not land.

reviewer_outcome.description:
A successful selection, a deliberate empty result, or an unavailable lookup. Defaults to selected when omitted.

* `selected` - Selected
* `no_suitable_owner` - No suitable owner
* `lookup_failed` - Lookup failed

reviewer_outcome_reason.description: Why no suitable owner exists, with `reviewer_outcome: no_suitable_owner`. Required to clear a report that already has suggested reviewers: without it the current reviewers stay and the response carries a warning. The reason is recorded in the report's work log.

source_issues.description: The GitHub issues this report is about, when the finding came from an issue tracker. Pass the issue whenever the report is about one, so the report links back to it: a GitHub issue signal for the same issue then joins this report instead of opening a second one. When the project turned on GitHub issue comments, the issue gets one comment that links the report once its GitHub source ingests the issue. At most 5 per call. Additive: issues join the ones the report already names, and an issue it already names is skipped. Only a newly added issue gets a comment.

suggested_prompts.description: The full set of follow-up prompts (questions or next-step actions) the report should offer above its `Ask AI` box. Replaces the report's prompts rather than adding to them, so send every one you want kept. Omit the field (or send null) to leave them untouched, and send an empty list to take them down, which is what you want once a rewrite has left them pointing at the old report.

suggested_reviewers.description: Optional reviewers to set on the report (each a `github_login` and/or `user_uuid`), replacing any existing list. Use this to route a report that surfaced with no reviewer — it re-runs autostart, so a report that was missing a qualifying reviewer can now open a draft PR. An empty list clears automatic reviewers when correction rules are enabled. Pins, exclusions, and confirmed lists are preserved. Pass expected_reviewers from the report reviewer_assignment.state read before selection.

summary.description: Optional new summary. Markdown is supported (headings, lists, code, links; images are not rendered); lead with one plain declarative sentence — it becomes the inbox card headline. A heading, or a bold label on a line of its own with a blank line above it, marks a section that a threaded Slack delivery splits into its own reply. The pipeline may later re-research and overwrite it.

supersedes_implementation.description: Set this only when your rewrite changes what the fix should be: a different root cause, a different file or layer, a materially wider or narrower scope. More evidence for the same fix is not a reason, because the report's open pull request already implements it: put that in `append_note`. Setting it true records a replacement decision for a ready report. Policy and eligibility checks gate the replacement. The existing pull request closes only after a successful, verified replacement. Technical failures retry automatically; policy blocks wait for a new edit or research trigger. Only honored alongside a `title` or `summary` that actually changes, and only within the first four content revisions, including revisions that did not request replacement. When the flag is not applied, `warnings` says why.

tags.description: The report's full set of slug tags, at most 10. Replaces the report's tags rather than adding to them, so send every tag you want kept. Omit the field (or send null) to leave them untouched, and send an empty list to remove them. Reuse a slug the project already uses before you coin a new one.

title.description: Optional new title. Conventional-commit style (`type(scope): description`) renders with type/scope styling. The pipeline may later re-research and overwrite it.

charts_set.description: How many charts the report now shows, or null if the edit left its charts as they were (the field omitted, or a re-send of what was already stored). 0 means the edit took the report's charts down.

content_revision_count.description: How many times a scout has rewritten this report's title or summary, counting this edit.

corroboration_collapsed.description: Whether your note raised the report's corroboration count instead of landing as its own entry. Only notes marked corroboration_only can collapse; free-form notes remain in the work log.

decision_fields_set.description: Which work decisions the edit replaced (`actionability`, `priority`). Empty when you set none, or re-sent the decisions the report already held.

evidence_appended.description: How many observations this edit added to the report's evidence rail; 0 if none.

is_content_revision.description: Whether this edit actually rewrote the report's title or summary. False for a note, a reviewer change, or a re-send of the text the report already had.

links_appended.description: How many typed report-to-report links this edit wrote; 0 if none.

metrics_set.description: How many impact metrics the report now shows, or null when untouched/unchanged. 0 means the edit removed every metric.

note_appended.description: Whether the edit included a note. True for a collapsed corroboration too, where the report's count moves and no work-log entry is written. Read `corroboration_collapsed` to tell the two apart.

pull_requests_linked.description: How many pull requests this edit linked that the report did not link yet; 0 if none.

quality_hints.description: Quality checks the title or summary matched. A `repair` hint means the stored text differs from what you sent: escape the JSON one time only next time. A `hint` means the text was stored as sent: correct it with edit_report if the hint applies. Empty when no check matched.

report_id.description: Id of the edited report.

repository.description: The repository the report points at now, read back from the report rather than echoed from the request; null when the report has no target. Compare it with the `repository` you sent to confirm the correction landed.

repository_set.description: Whether the report's repository was replaced (true for a cleared target too).

reviewers_set.description: Whether the report's suggested reviewers were replaced.

source_issues_appended.description: How many source issues this edit added that the report did not name yet; 0 if none.

suggested_prompts_set.description: How many prompts the report now suggests, or null if the edit left them as they were (the field omitted, or a re-send of what was already stored). 0 means the edit took the report's suggested prompts down.

supersedes_implementation.description: Whether the edit recorded that the report's pull request should be replaced. False when you did not ask for it, when the edit changed no content, or when the report has already been rewritten too many times.

tags_set.description: How many tags the report now carries, or null if the edit left them as they were (the field omitted, or a re-send of what was already stored). 0 means the edit removed the report's tags.

updated_fields.description: Which presentation fields changed (e.g. `title`, `summary`); empty if only a note was appended.

warnings.description: Request fields the edit did not apply, each with the reason. Empty when every field applied.

field.description: The request field the edit did not apply.

message.description: Why the field was not applied. The rest of the edit landed.

base_version.description: Version number that the changes apply to. Must be the active version of the app, otherwise the request fails with 409 and returns the active version number.

create_files.description: New text files keyed by project-relative path, each value the file's full text (max 1 MB). The path must not exist in the base version.

delete_files.description: Paths of files to remove from the base version. app.py cannot be removed.

file_edits.description: Exact text edits to existing text files. Files that no change touches stay byte-for-byte the same.

count.description: Number of events matching this element chain

elements.description: Parsed elements of the chain, clicked element first

hash.description: Hash of the chain as the server grouped it; combine with type to deduplicate rows across pages

type.description: Event type: $autocapture, $rageclick, or $dead_click

next.description: URL for the next page of results, if any

previous.description: URL for the previous page of results, if any

results.description: Element chains with event counts, ordered by count

name.description: A distinct value of the requested element property

content_id.description: Content ID that the HTML body references as `cid:<content_id>` to show the file inline, such as `logo`. Without `<` or `>`.

content_type.description: MIME type of the file, such as `application/pdf`, with any parameters, such as `text/calendar; charset=utf-8; method=REQUEST`. Without it, the type follows from the file name. A `name` parameter is refused, because the file name comes from `filename`.

filename.description: File name the recipient sees, such as `invoice.pdf`. No path and no line breaks. A file type mailbox providers block, such as `.exe`, is refused.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of a file uploaded through `POST /api/projects/{project_id}/messaging/attachments/uploads/`, as 64 lowercase hex characters.

emails_per_day.description: How many emails this tier allows per day.

emails_sent_last_day.description: Emails sent by this project's workflows in the last 24 hours.

enforced.description: True when these allowances are applied to sends. False while they are only being measured.

max_batch_audience.description: The largest audience this tier allows for a single batch send.

rate_limited_max_batch_audience.description: The largest audience a single email batch may reach when its sending rate limit is slow enough. Null when no rate limit raises max_batch_audience.

EmailSendingRates.description: Bounce/complaint rates over the last 30 days of workflow email, computed on the fly from app metrics.

bounce_rate.description: Hard (permanent) bounces / emails sent over the last 30 days (0-1), matching how AWS counts its bounce rate — transient bounces (greylisting, mailbox full) are excluded. Bounces are counted when the feedback arrives, so the ratio is approximate at the window boundary and capped at 1.

complaint_rate.description: Spam complaints / emails sent over the last 30 days (0-1). Complaints are counted when the feedback arrives, so the ratio is approximate at the window boundary and capped at 1.

emails_sent.description: Emails sent in the last 30 days.

EmailSendingSuspensionStatus.description: Cheap suspension-only read for the persistent scene-wide banner — no reputation computation.

email_sending_suspended.description: True while workflow email sending is suspended for this project to protect deliverability.

email_sending_suspended_at.description: When email sending was suspended; null while sending is enabled.

email_sending_suspension_reason.description: Staff-authored reason shown to customers alongside the suspension notice; empty when not suspended.

reason.description: Why a failed email was not sent, or the bounce type of a bounced email. A failed send has `provider_error`, or `provider_rejected` when the provider refused the email after it accepted the send. A skipped send has `recipient_suppressed`, `recipient_unreachable`, `recipient_opted_out`, `missing_recipient`, `sending_paused`, `sending_suspended` or `frequency_capped`. A run that stopped before the send has `canceled`, `workflow_unavailable` or an error kind such as `timeout`, and more error kinds can be added. A bounce has `hard`, `soft` or `unknown`. Null otherwise.

status.description:
What happened to the email. `queued` means it waits to go out. `sent` means PostHog handed it to the email provider. `failed` means it was not sent, and `reason` says why. A rerun of the send can still move it to `sent`. `delivered` means the recipient's mail server accepted it. `bounced` and `complained` come later from the recipient's mail provider.

* `queued` - Queued
* `failed` - Failed
* `sent` - Sent
* `delivered` - Delivered
* `bounced` - Bounced
* `complained` - Complained

subject.description: Email subject line. Supports Liquid templating. Required in `content` for email-type templates. A `draft_content` may leave it blank until it is published.

text.description: Plain-text fallback body for clients that can't render the email.

email.description: Address to send from instead of the sender's own. Must be on the sender's verified domain. Supports Liquid templating. Leave out or empty to use the sender's address.

EmitEligibility.description: `inventory.emit_eligibility` — whether the calling scout's findings and reports can reach the inbox.

ai_processing_approved.description: Whether the organization has approved AI data processing (an org-level gate on all scout emits).

blocking_reason.description: Which gate blocks the write: `scout_emit_disabled`, `scout_config_missing`, `ai_processing_not_approved`, or `source_disabled`. Null when `can_emit` is True. Matches the `skipped_reason` `emit-report` returns for the same block.

can_emit.description: True only when every gate passes, so this scout's findings and reports (both channels) actually reach the inbox. When False, every write is dropped or refused — quick-close instead of doing throwaway investigation. Read this one value: it accounts for the calling scout's own dry-run posture as well as the team-wide gates, and it is the same gate `emit-report` and `edit-report` apply at write time.

remediation.description: One-line next step to unblock writes when `can_emit` is False; null when writes can flow.

scout_emit_enabled.description: Whether the calling scout's own config can write, as opposed to running in dry-run (`emit=false`), where it investigates but everything it writes is discarded. Null when the read is not from a scout run, so no single scout's config applies.

source_enabled.description: Whether the `signals_scout` signal source is enabled for this team.

EmitFindingRequest.description: Request body for `emit-finding`. Run attribution is taken from the URL path.

description.description: Canonical evidence-bundle prose. Becomes the signal's `description`.

evidence.description: Citations supporting the finding. Capped at 20 entries.

finding_id.description: Stable id for this finding, baked into the signal's source_id for traceability. NOT a dedupe key — re-emitting the same id creates another signal.

hypothesis.description: Optional one-line hypothesis the finding tests.

mcp_trace_id.description: Optional MCP trace id for cross-system debugging.

severity.description:
Optional severity tag — one of P0, P1, P2, P3, P4. Informational only.

* `P0` - P0
* `P1` - P1
* `P2` - P2
* `P3` - P3
* `P4` - P4

tags.description: Optional category tags as lowercase kebab-case slugs (e.g. `cost-spike`, `silent-failure`), max 10. Reuse the vocabulary in your `tags:<domain>:taxonomy` scratchpad entry when a tag fits; coin a new slug when a genuinely new category emerges. Near-miss formats are normalized to slugs; persisted in the signal's `extra.tags` and on the emission row.

time_range.description: Optional time window the finding refers to.

finding_id.description: Stable id for the finding (echoed back from request, or generated).

remediation.description: One-line, actionable next step when `skipped_reason` is set and the block is fixable (e.g. an org admin must approve AI data processing). Null when emitted normally or the skip isn't something the scout can act on.

EmitReportRequest.description:
Request body for the scout `emit-report` action and the inbox report `create` action. A scout run is
taken from the URL path; a person is the authenticated caller.

actionability.description:
The scout's actionability call: `immediately_actionable` -> the report surfaces READY; `requires_human_input` -> PENDING_INPUT; `not_actionable` -> suppressed. A safety-judge failure suppresses the report regardless. A root cause you have not found is not human input: a report that names the evidence, the code surface, or a reproducible failure path is `immediately_actionable`, because investigating it is the action. Reserve `requires_human_input` for a report blocked on a decision only a person can make.

* `immediately_actionable` - immediately_actionable
* `requires_human_input` - requires_human_input
* `not_actionable` - not_actionable

actionability_explanation.description: 2-3 sentence evidence-grounded justification for the actionability call below.

already_addressed.description: Whether the issue is already being handled — fixed in recent changes, or with a fix in flight (an open PR, a recently active branch, an assigned / in-progress issue or agent task). Gates autostart of a scout report, so a wrong `false` opens a duplicate PR. Tracked separately.

charts.description: Optional charts to attach to the report — the inbox renders them inline, so a metric move is something the reader sees rather than a number they take on trust. Attach one whenever the finding rests on a trend, a spike, or a comparison you already queried. Reference a chart from `summary` as `[label](chart:<chart_id>)` to place it in the body; an unreferenced chart renders below the summary.

evidence.description: The observations backing the report — each becomes a bound signal. At least one.

idempotency_key.description: Optional name for this emission, unique within a scout's run or within a person's own reports. Reuse it verbatim to retry a call whose outcome you don't know (a timeout, a dropped connection): the retry returns the report the first call authored, with `idempotent_replay` true, instead of a second report. Omit it and the report's own content is the key, which covers a retry of the identical call — pass one when a retry might reword the report.

links.description: Typed, directed links from the new report to reports that already exist. Send them here, not in a later `edit-report` call, because autostart reads them when the report is created: a `duplicate_of` link to a report that already has a pull request, or a `depends_on` link to a report with no pull request yet, stops a second draft PR. Only the new report gets a row, so link from the side the sentence starts at. Links of the same kind must stay acyclic and every report must be in this project.

metrics.description: Optional typed impact measurements, at most 6. Mark one metric `primary` for the key observation and the rest `supporting`, for users, sessions, occurrences, conversion, latency, or revenue. Every metric needs a live `query`: an InsightVizNode wrapping one bounded TrendsQuery built only from EventsNode or ActionsNode sources, with at most 1000 estimated longitudinal points. An affected-users metric counts distinct people through one series with `math: dau`; never sum its buckets. A `value`/`value_at` snapshot is only an optional cached fallback, and a metric without a query is invalid.

priority.description:
Optional priority (`P0`-`P4`). Required for autostart; pair with `priority_explanation`.

* `P0` - P0
* `P1` - P1
* `P2` - P2
* `P3` - P3
* `P4` - P4

priority_explanation.description: 2-3 sentence justification for `priority`. Required when `priority` is set.

repository.description: Optional repo for opening a draft PR, by autostart of a scout report or by a person from the inbox. Pass `owner/repo` whenever you can say where a fix would land. Nothing selects a repository for you: omit the field when you can't tell, and the report records no repository unless its text links exactly one connected repo, so it cannot autostart a draft PR. Keep the `NO_REPO` sentinel for the rare report where nothing under version control could change, since a skill body, a config file, or a doc still lives in a repo.

source_issues.description: The GitHub issues this report is about, when the finding came from an issue tracker. Pass the issue whenever the report is about one, so the report links back to it: a GitHub issue signal for the same issue then joins this report instead of opening a second one. When the project turned on GitHub issue comments, the issue gets one comment that links the report once its GitHub source ingests the issue. At most 5 per call.

suggested_prompts.description: Optional follow-up prompts to offer above the report's `Ask AI` box: questions to ask, or next-step actions to request (e.g. carrying out the report's recommendation). The reader clicks one to fill the box with it, then sends or edits it. Write the prompts your own research left open, phrased as the reader would send them.

suggested_reviewers.description: Optional reviewers to route the report to (each a `github_login` and/or `user_uuid`). This is the primary way a report reaches a human — the inbox floats a reviewer's own reports to the top of their inbox even when no PR is involved — so set it whenever you can name a plausible owner. On a scout report it also gates autostart: a PR opens only if at least one reviewer clears their autonomy threshold. A report a person files never autostarts.

summary.description: The report body the inbox shows. Markdown is supported (headings, lists, code, links; images are not rendered). Lead with one plain declarative sentence — the inbox card uses your first line verbatim as the headline (~140 chars, emphasis stripped), then renders the full markdown in the detail view. A heading, or a bold label on a line of its own with a blank line above it, marks a section that a threaded Slack delivery splits into its own reply.

tags.description: Optional slug tags that group the report with related ones, at most 10. Write lowercase kebab-case slugs that name the category of the report (`cost-spike`, `tracking-gap`), not the specific entity. Reuse a slug the project already uses before you coin a new one. Near-miss formats are normalized to slugs, and a tag that is empty or longer than 50 characters after normalization is rejected.

title.description: One-line report title the inbox shows. Conventional-commit style (`type(scope): description`, e.g. `fix(insights): missing series color`) renders with type/scope styling.

emitted.description: True when the report actually surfaced in the inbox (READY or PENDING_INPUT).

idempotent_replay.description: True when this call authored nothing because the emission had already landed — the fields above describe that first report. Expected on a retry; treat the report as filed and don't send it again.

quality_hints.description: Quality checks the title or summary matched. A `repair` hint means the stored text differs from what you sent: escape the JSON one time only next time. A `hint` means the text was stored as sent: correct it with edit_report if the hint applies. Empty when no check matched.

remediation.description: One-line, actionable next step when `skipped_reason` is set and the block is fixable (e.g. an org admin must approve AI data processing). Null when the report was authored or the skip isn't something the scout can act on.

report_id.description: The authored report's id (null only when a preflight gate skipped the call). Returned even when suppressed, so you can edit/dedup against it.

report_status.description: Birth status: `ready` | `pending_input` | `suppressed`, or null when gate-skipped.

safety_explanation.description: When the safety judge suppressed the report, why; null when safe.

conclusion.description:
The conclusion of the experiment.

* `won` - won
* `lost` - lost
* `inconclusive` - inconclusive
* `stopped_early` - stopped_early
* `invalid` - invalid

conclusion_comment.description: Optional comment about the experiment conclusion.

open_cleanup_pr.description: When true, open a draft pull request that removes the experiment's feature-flag code from the linked repository. A personal API key needs the task:write scope (403 otherwise). Skipped when the conclusion is empty, or when no connected repository can be resolved.

repository.description: GitHub repository to open the cleanup pull request in, in `organization/repository` format. Only used when open_cleanup_pr is true. It must be one of the team's connected repositories (see the flag_cleanup_target action); it is then saved as the experiment's repository. When omitted, the experiment's saved repository, the team's default cleanup repository, or the team's only connected repository is used.

set_repository_as_team_default.description: When true, also save `repository` as this environment's default cleanup repository, used for experiments that have no repository of their own. Only acts when open_cleanup_pr is true and `repository` is provided and belongs to the team's GitHub installation. Requires project admin access (403 otherwise).

variables.description:
Variables to parameterize the endpoint query. The key is the variable name and the value is the variable value.

For HogQL endpoints:   Keys must match a variable `code_name` defined in the query (referenced as `{variables.code_name}`).   Example: `{"event_name": "$pageview"}`

For non-materialized insight endpoints (e.g. TrendsQuery):   - `date_from` and `date_to` are built-in variables that filter the date range.     Example: `{"date_from": "2024-01-01", "date_to": "2024-01-31"}`

For materialized insight endpoints:   - Use the breakdown property name as the key to filter by breakdown value.     Example: `{"$browser": "Chrome"}`   - `date_from`/`date_to` are not supported on materialized insight endpoints.

Unknown variable names will return a 400 error.

conditions.description: Trigger conditions that filter which events are evaluated. OR between condition sets, AND within each. Each set is {id, rollout_percentage, properties[]} — `rollout_percentage` (0-100, defaults to 100) is the sampling field the dispatcher reads.

source.description: Hog source code. Return a boolean, finite number, or category keys matching output_type. Categorical single selection accepts one key or a one-item list; multiple selection accepts a list, including []. Return null only for allowed N/A. Output settings determine which boolean counts as a failure.

Classify sentiment from user messages in the generation input. The classifier is trained on English, so labels are unreliable for other languages; use an 'llm_judge' evaluation for multilingual agents.

evaluation_type.description:
'llm_judge' uses an LLM to score outputs against a prompt; 'hog' runs deterministic Hog code; 'sentiment' classifies user-message sentiment (trained on English, so use 'llm_judge' for multilingual agents).

* `llm_judge` - LLM as a judge
* `hog` - Hog
* `sentiment` - Sentiment analysis

model_configuration.description: Provider and model for an llm_judge evaluation. Required when creating or switching to llm_judge. To add or replace a model, provide both provider and model. On an existing configured llm_judge, omit this field to keep the current model; null is rejected. When switching an llm_judge to hog or sentiment, set this field to null. Legacy llm_judge evaluations without a model remain editable without adding one. The nested provider_key_id may be null.

name.description: Name of the evaluation.

output_config.description: Output config. For 'boolean' output_type: {allows_na} to permit N/A results, and {true_is_failure} to declare that a true result means the evaluation found a problem. For boolean decision-model judges, decision_threshold is a probability from 0 to 1 (default 0.5). For 'numeric': only min/max/step, allows_na, and passing_rule {operator: 'gte'|'lte', threshold}. For 'categorical': options [{key, label}], selection_mode (single or multiple), allows_na, and optional passing_rule {categories: [key]}. Do not send true_is_failure for numeric or categorical output. For 'sentiment': {}.

allows_na.description: Whether the evaluation can return N/A for non-applicable generations.

decision_threshold.description: Boolean decision-model judges only. Minimum probability of true required for a true result, inclusive. Omit or set null to use 0.5. Applies to new runs; historical results are unchanged.

max.description: Inclusive maximum numeric score. Omit for no upper bound. Required for numeric decision models and must exceed min.

min.description: Inclusive minimum numeric score. Omit for no lower bound. Required for numeric decision models.

options.description: Categorical output options. Keys identify stored results; labels are displayed to users.

key.description: Stable category key.

label.description: Category display label.

passing_rule.description: Optional numeric or categorical passing rule. Null removes the rule; historical results use the current rule.

operator.description: Pass at or above (gte), or at or below (lte), the threshold.

threshold.description: Finite passing threshold within any configured score bounds.

categories.description: Passing category keys. With keys selected, results must be non-empty and contain only these keys. If no passing keys are selected, only an empty result passes.

selection_mode.description: Select one category or multiple categories. Multiple selection allows an empty result. Defaults to single.

step.description: Optional positive input increment. Does not round evaluation results.

true_is_failure.description: Boolean output only. Omit for numeric, categorical, and sentiment output. Whether a true result means the evaluation found a problem. False (the default) suits pass/fail evaluations, where a true result satisfied the criteria. Set it to true for detector-style evaluations, so a true result is counted and labeled as a fail.

output_type.description:
Output format: 'boolean', 'numeric' for a finite score, 'categorical' for category keys, or 'sentiment' for sentiment analysis.

* `boolean` - Boolean (Pass/Fail)
* `numeric` - Numeric
* `categorical` - Categorical
* `sentiment` - Sentiment

status_reason_detail.description: Additional detail for the current system-disabled status. This is only populated when the detail is safe to show in the evaluation UI.

target.description:
What the evaluation runs on. 'generation' evaluates each matching $ai_generation event individually. 'trace' evaluates the whole trace once and 'session' the whole $ai_session_id session once: the first matching generation schedules a run that waits for the unit to settle, then evaluates all of its events together. Condition filters still match individual generations — a unit is evaluated when any of its generations matches, and sampling applies per unit. A 'session' evaluation only fires for generations that carry $ai_session_id. When and how the run fires is controlled by target_config's settle strategy.

* `generation` - Generation
* `trace` - Trace
* `session` - Session

target_config.description: Target-specific config. Send {} or omit it for 'generation'. For 'trace' and 'session' targets: a settle config, either 'fixed_window' {window_seconds} or 'inactivity' {quiet_period_seconds, max_age_seconds}. Omit `strategy` to use the target's default. The server fills in any other field you omit, using per-target defaults, and the accepted bounds also depend on `target`.

max_age_seconds.description: inactivity only. Hard cap in seconds on the total wait from the first matching generation, even if the unit stays active. Must be at least quiet_period_seconds. The accepted range depends on `target`: 60–7200 for 'trace', 60–604800 for 'session'. The default also depends on `target`; see the field-level help_text.

quiet_period_seconds.description: inactivity only. Seconds without new activity before the unit counts as settled. The accepted range depends on `target`: 10–1800 for 'trace', 10–86400 for 'session'. The default also depends on `target`; see the field-level help_text.

strategy.description: 'fixed_window' waits a fixed window after the first matching generation, then evaluates. 'inactivity' evaluates once the unit has had no new activity for the quiet period. Omit it to use the target's default: 'fixed_window' for 'trace', 'inactivity' for 'session'.

window_seconds.description: fixed_window only. Seconds to wait after the first matching generation before evaluating the whole unit. Experiment.description:
Full experiment representation for the detail, create, and update endpoints.

Extends the shared read-side fields in ``ExperimentBaseSerializer`` with the metric
definitions (``metrics``/``metrics_secondary``/``saved_metrics``) and the write-side
fields, and refreshes stale action names while serializing. The list endpoint uses the
leaner ``ExperimentBasicSerializer`` instead.

allow_unknown_events.description: Suppresses the validation that rejects metrics referencing events not yet ingested by this project. REQUIRES explicit user confirmation before being set to true — never flip this silently to retry a failed call. The default validation catches typo'd event names and missing instrumentation. Set this to true only when the user has confirmed the event is intentional (e.g. they are about to instrument it).

archived.description: Whether the experiment is archived.

can_freeze_exposure.description: Whether enrollment can be frozen right now: the experiment must be running (not draft, paused, stopped, or already frozen) and its feature flag must have release conditions that a person cohort can narrow (no group aggregation, no holdout, no early access conditions).

conclusion.description:
Experiment conclusion: won, lost, inconclusive, stopped_early, or invalid.

* `won` - won
* `lost` - lost
* `inconclusive` - inconclusive
* `stopped_early` - stopped_early
* `invalid` - invalid

description.description: Description of the experiment hypothesis and expected outcomes.

excluded_variants.description: Variant keys to exclude from metric result calculations. Excluded variants are still served to users but omitted from statistical analysis. The baseline variant and holdout pseudo-variants cannot be excluded. Canonical home for what historically lived in `parameters.excluded_variants`.

exposure_criteria.description: Exposure configuration including filter test accounts and custom exposure events.

feature_flag_key.description: Unique key for the experiment's feature flag. Letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores only. Search existing flags with the feature-flag-get-all tool first — reuse an existing flag when possible.

feature_flag_rule_id.description: The experiment rule that this experiment runs on, when its feature flag has rules. Null for every other experiment. Set it only on create, together with the feature_flag_key of an existing flag with rules. When that flag has one experiment rule, it can be left out. The experiment then counts exposures on the $experiment_exposure events of this rule, and never changes the flag.

flag_cleanup_task_id.description: ID of the Desktop task opened to remove the experiment's feature-flag code, when one was requested via open_cleanup_pr on end/ship_variant. Read its status via the flag_cleanup_task action.

health.description: Always null. Read the health findings from `GET /api/projects/{project_id}/experiments/{id}/health/`: problems in this experiment's configuration and its feature flag that keep it from producing trustworthy results, each with a fix.

holdout_id.description: ID of a holdout group to exclude from the experiment.

is_legacy.description: Whether the experiment uses any legacy-engine metrics (ExperimentTrendsQuery or ExperimentFunnelsQuery). Used to flag legacy experiments and gate actions that don't support them, such as duplicate and copy-to-project.

metrics.description: Primary experiment metrics. Each metric must have kind='ExperimentMetric' and a metric_type: 'mean' (set source to an EventsNode with an event name), 'funnel' (set series to an array of EventsNode steps), 'ratio' (set numerator and denominator EventsNode entries), 'quantile' (set source to an EventsNode or ActionsNode with math_property, the numeric property to measure, and quantile, the level in [0.01, 0.99], for example 0.9 for p90), or 'retention' (set start_event and completion_event; pass start_event {"kind": "ExperimentExposureNode"} to start retention from the experiment's exposure event). Use the read-data-schema tool with query kind 'events' to find available events in the project.

metrics_secondary.description: Secondary metrics for additional measurements. Same format as primary metrics.

name.description: Name of the experiment.

original_experiment.description: The experiment state as the client last read it, used together with `version` to resolve concurrent edits: metric collections merge per metric uuid, and any other field the update carries merges per field against its base value here (only a same-field double edit fails). Relevant keys are metrics, metrics_secondary, saved_metrics_ids, plus the last-read values of whichever scalar fields the update writes; unknown keys are ignored. Changed fields without a base value — and, without this object, any version mismatch — fail with HTTP 409.

parameters.description: Experiment parameters JSON. Supported keys include `custom_exposure_filter` and `variant_notes` (free-text notes per variant, keyed by variant key). Flag config (variants, rollout, aggregation, payloads, experience continuity) belongs on the `feature_flag` object; send it there. For backward compatibility, config still sent through these deprecated keys is copied onto the linked flag rather than rejected, and reads project the flag's current config back into this field. Excluded variants live on the top-level `excluded_variants` field, not here.

primary_metrics_ordered_uuids.description: Display order of the primary metrics, as metric uuids. This is a display hint only: a metric not in the list renders after the listed ones in stored order, and an entry that matches no metric is ignored. Send it only to reorder metrics. Adding or removing metrics does not need it.

repository.description: GitHub repository holding this experiment's feature-flag code, in `organization/repository` format. Used as the target of the flag-cleanup pull request opened via open_cleanup_pr on end/ship_variant. When not set, cleanup targets the team's only connected repository and is skipped if the team has several.

resolved_exposure_event.description: The event exposures are actually counted on when the experiment doesn't configure a custom one — `$feature_flag_called`, or `$experiment_exposure` once the team is in the rollout and the experiment started at or after the cutoff. Resolved server-side so clients display the same event the results queries read. For a draft, this is what the experiment would resolve to if launched now.

running_time_calculation.description: Running-time calculator state: `minimum_detectable_effect`, `recommended_running_time`, `recommended_sample_size`, and `exposure_estimate_config`. Canonical home for these keys, which historically lived in `parameters`.

saved_metrics_ids.description: IDs of shared saved metrics to attach to this experiment. Each item has 'id' (saved metric ID) and 'metadata' with 'type' (primary or secondary).

secondary_metrics_ordered_uuids.description: Display order of the secondary metrics, as metric uuids. This is a display hint only: a metric not in the list renders after the listed ones in stored order, and an entry that matches no metric is ignored. Send it only to reorder metrics. Adding or removing metrics does not need it.

status.description: Experiment lifecycle state: 'draft' (not yet launched), 'running' (launched with active feature flag), 'paused' (running with feature flag deactivated — virtual state derived from feature_flag.active, not stored), 'exposure_frozen' (running with enrollment frozen to the already-exposed cohort while metrics keep flowing — virtual state derived from the flag's release groups, not stored), 'stopped' (ended).

update_feature_flag_params.description: When true, sync the flag config sent in this request (via the `feature_flag` object) to the linked feature flag. Draft experiments always sync regardless. On a running experiment, `feature_flag` config without this flag is rejected.

user_access_level.description: The effective access level the user has for this object

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency token. Reads return the experiment's current version, bumped on every update. Send the version you last read with an update to detect concurrent edits: a stale update merges concurrent changes where safe — metric collections per metric uuid, other fields per field — using the base values sent in `original_experiment`, and fails with HTTP 409 only when the same metric or field changed on both sides (or no base value was sent for a changed field). Omit to skip the check.

ExperimentBasic.description:
Lightweight, read-only serializer for the experiment list endpoint.

The list view (and the MCP list tool) render only the scalar and feature-flag fields
shared via ``ExperimentBaseSerializer`` — never the metric definitions. Omitting
``metrics``/``metrics_secondary``/``saved_metrics`` lets the list query defer the large
JSON columns and skip the saved-metric prefetch plus per-row fingerprinting; that work
belongs to the detail response served by ``ExperimentSerializer``.

Because the metric fields, the write-side machinery, and the action-name-refreshing
``to_representation`` all live on ``ExperimentSerializer`` rather than the shared base,
this serializer needs no overrides: it gets DRF's default ``get_fields`` (no write-only
``holdout_id`` to configure), default ``to_representation`` (no metrics to normalize), and
a plain ``ListSerializer`` that never touches the deferred columns. See
``EnterpriseExperimentsViewSet.safely_get_queryset``.

Feature-flag filters accepted by the experiment endpoints: the flag's own filters shape,
minus the keys experiments don't apply.

ExperimentFeatureFlagInput.description:
Flag config for experiment create/update, sent through the linked feature flag's own shape.

Validated both as the OpenAPI request field (via ``ExperimentWriteSerializer``) and at runtime
(``ExperimentSerializer._normalize_feature_flag_input`` runs it against the raw feature_flag
object). Echoed read-only flag objects (carrying a non-null id) are handled upstream and never
reach this validation.

ensure_experience_continuity.description: Whether the flag persists variant assignment across authentication steps.

filters.description: Flag config to apply: `multivariate.variants` (2 to 20 variants; the baseline defaults to the variant keyed 'control' when present, else the first variant), `groups` (a single group with `rollout_percentage` only; release conditions are not supported here, edit the feature flag directly), `aggregation_group_type_index`, and `payloads` (JSON-encoded strings keyed by variant key). On update, config this object omits is preserved from the linked flag's current state.

candidates.description: Repositories connected to the team's GitHub integration, to choose a target from.

repository.description: Repository a flag-cleanup pull request would be opened in, or null when none can be determined.

source.description:

* `explicit` - explicit
* `team_default` - team_default
* `single_repo` - single_repo
* `ambiguous` - ambiguous
* `no_integration` - no_integration

name.description: The problem the check looks for, for example 'Metrics not set up'.

reason.description: Why the check did not look, for the statuses not_applicable and not_checked, for example 'Runs after launch'. Null for passed and finding.

rows.description: What the check read per variant, metric or feature flag change, one object each, with the keys and units of `values`. For example, the significance check gives each variant's difference and the smallest difference its sample can detect. A release condition change also gives the conditions as the flag stores them, in before_filters and after_filters. Empty when the check reads no such list.

oneOf.description: A feature flag's release conditions as the flag stores them, in before_filters and after_filters.

rule.description: How the check decides. The same for every experiment and every status. Null for a check without a numeric rule.

status.description:
passed: the check found no problem. finding: the check reported a finding in `findings`. not_applicable: the check does not cover the experiment's current state, for example a check of the changes since launch on a draft. not_checked: the check covers the experiment, but it could not read an input or it failed, so a problem it looks for can be present without a finding.

* `passed` - Passed
* `finding` - Finding
* `not_applicable` - Not Applicable
* `not_checked` - Not Checked

values.description: What the check read on the experiment, for every status, as numbers, strings, booleans or null. Empty when the check read nothing or shows nothing. The suffix of a key gives the unit: _count is a count, _percentage is on the 0-100 scale, _hours is hours and _at is an ISO 8601 time in UTC. A key without a suffix is a setting or a state. A key means the same thing in every check. `rule.value` names the key that decides.

minimum.description: What the check needs before it judges. Null when the check judges from the first value.

test.description:
The statistical test that computes the value, for example chi_squared. Null for a count or a share.

* `chi_squared` - Chi-squared goodness-of-fit test

threshold.description: The threshold, in the unit that the suffix of the key gives.

value.description:
The key in `values` that the check compares with the threshold.

* `exposed_count` - Users or groups exposed since launch, as the exposure criteria count them, including those exposed to multiple variants
* `compared_count` - Exposed users or groups in the variants that the sample ratio test compares, without those exposed to multiple variants
* `multiple_variant_count` - Users or groups exposed to more than one variant
* `multiple_variant_percentage` - multiple_variant_count as a share of exposed_count
* `multiple_variant_handling` - What the results do with users exposed to more than one variant: exclude or first_seen
* `p_value` - P-value of the sample ratio test
* `since_launch_hours` - Hours since launch
* `exposed_without_test_account_filter_count` - Users or groups that the exposure criteria count without the test account filters
* `kept_by_test_account_filter_percentage` - exposed_count as a share of exposed_without_test_account_filter_count
* `unserved_exposed_count` - Users or groups first exposed after the day of the feature flag's last save, in a variant that the flag doesn't serve since that save
* `unserved_exposed_percentage` - unserved_exposed_count as a share of the users or groups first exposed after that day
* `only_count_matured_users` - Whether "Require completed conversion or retention window" is on
* `primary_metric_count` - Primary metrics that the calculation computes
* `waiting_metric_count` - Of the primary metrics, those whose conversion or retention window hasn't passed for any user yet
* `metric_count` - Metrics that the calculation computes
* `completed_metric_count` - Metrics whose result of the latest calculation the page shows
* `failed_metric_count` - Metrics whose latest calculation failed
* `calculated_at` - When the latest calculation of the metrics finished
* `flag_active` - Whether the feature flag is enabled
* `flag_deleted` - Whether the feature flag is deleted
* `flag_rolled_out` - Whether a release condition of the feature flag rolls out to more than 0%
* `shipped_variant` - The key of the variant that the feature flag serves to everyone, or null when it serves more than one
* `flag_last_called_at` - When PostHog last recorded a call of the feature flag
* `since_start_hours` - Hours since the experiment's start date, which can be earlier than the launch
* `daily_calculation_ends_at` - When the daily calculation stops covering the experiment, a fixed number of days after its start date
* `metric_name` - The name of a metric
* `metric_role` - Whether a metric is primary or secondary
* `ratio_side` - The side of a ratio metric, numerator or denominator, or null for the other metric types
* `sample_count` - Users or groups in a metric's results, across the variants
* `planned_sample_count` - Users or groups that the running time estimate needs to detect its minimum detectable effect
* `data_hours` - Hours of data that a metric's latest calculation holds since launch, within the metric's conversion window
* `variant` - The key of a variant
* `difference_percentage` - A variant's difference from the control on the primary metric, relative to the control, with its sign
* `detectable_difference_percentage` - The smallest difference from the control that the variant's sample can reliably detect, relative to the control
* `significant` - Whether a variant's difference from the control is significant
* `forced_condition_count` - Release conditions of the feature flag that serve a fixed variant through a variant override
* `matched_count` - Users or groups that a release condition served since traffic_since_at, without those forced to a variant that has 0% in the split
* `variant_matched_count` - Of matched_count, the users or groups who got the variant. Estimated from the split for those assigned at random
* `forced_count` - Users or groups that a release condition with a variant override served
* `forced_percentage` - forced_count as a share of variant_matched_count
* `traffic_since_at` - The start of the window that matched_count counts: 7 days ago, or the launch or the flag's last save if later
* `changed_at` - When a change of the feature flag was saved
* `before_exposure` - Whether a change of the feature flag was saved before anyone was exposed, so it moved nobody. Null when unknown
* `changed_setting` - The flag setting that a change of the bucketing changed, as the flag page names it
* `before` - What a change of the feature flag changed, as it was before the change, in words
* `after` - What a change of the feature flag changed, as it was after the change, in words
* `before_filters` - The feature flag's release conditions before a change, as the flag stores them: an object with the groups and the aggregation_group_type_index of its filters. Null when they don't fit the size limit of the check's rows. The flag's history shows them in full
* `after_filters` - The feature flag's release conditions after a change, as the flag stores them, like before_filters
* `flag_service_call_percentage` - Of the feature flag's calls since traffic_since_at that returned a variant, the share that the flag service evaluated. Only these calls name the release condition that served them, so local evaluation and bootstrapped values count in no condition
* `event` - The name of an event that the check looked up
* `event_received` - Whether the project has received the event. Null when PostHog keeps no record of the event name
* `invalid_metric_count` - Metrics whose query doesn't compile, so every calculation fails
* `unchecked_metric_count` - Metrics whose query the check couldn't compile, because they read data that the reader can't query or the compile failed for a reason other than the metric
* `flag_split` - The feature flag's variants with their rollout percentages, in words
* `baseline_variant` - The key of the variant that the analysis compares the others with, or null when the analysis picks one
* `other_running_experiment_count` - Other experiments that run on the same feature flag and are not archived
* `assigned_outside_count` - Users or groups who got a variant from a call that the flag service didn't evaluate and that is no local evaluation, such as a bootstrapped value. Read only while a running experiment's feature flag has a 0% rollout
* `other_draft_experiment_count` - Other draft experiments on the same feature flag that are not archived
