archived.description: Whether the experiment is archived.

baseline_variant_key.description: The baseline set in the experiment's settings. Null when unset.

condition_set_traffic.description: The flag's recent calls by condition set. Null unless condition_set_traffic_status is 'read'.

condition_set_traffic_status.description:
Whether the condition-set traffic was read, or why not. The forced-variant check needs it when the experiment is launched and some but not all release conditions pin a variant that has a share of the split and is not excluded from the analysis. The release-condition check needs it when such an override was removed after launch.

* `read` - Read
* `not_needed` - Not Needed
* `no_query_access` - No Query Access
* `denied_properties` - Denied Properties
* `no_flag_version` - No Flag Version
* `unknown` - Unknown

events_received.description: Whether the project has received each event that the metrics and the exposure criteria name, by event name. A name that ingestion keeps no record of is absent.

excluded_variant_keys.description: The variants the analysis leaves out of the results. The forced-variant check ignores pins to them.

exposure_events.description: The events the exposure criteria count. Null when the stored exposure criteria don't parse.

exposures.description: The exposure query's answer that the exposure checks read, from the cache.

flag.description: The experiment's feature flag. Null when it has none.

flag_called.description: Whether PostHog has recorded any call of the flag. The flag traffic check reads it on a draft. Null when the experiment has no flag, or the organization's flag calls are stored where the checks can't read them.

flag_called_after_end.description: Whether PostHog has recorded a call of the flag after the end and within the last 3 days. The flag state check reads it on an ended experiment whose flag is still active with multiple variants. False only once 3 days have passed since the end. Null before the end, before those 3 days are over without a call, or when the organization's flag calls can't be read.

flag_called_during_run.description: Whether PostHog has recorded a call of the flag between launch and the end, or until now. The zero exposures check reads it to say whether the flag is called. Null before launch, after a latest call that came after the end, or when the organization's flag calls can't be read.

flag_history.description: The changes of the flag since launch that can move exposed people. Null when the experiment is not running, is archived, its flag is missing or deleted, or the read failed.

flag_last_called_at.description: The flag's latest recorded call, which a periodic sync of the flag call events sets. Null when the experiment has no flag, or the flag has no recorded call.

has_ended.description: Whether the experiment has an end date.

is_launched.description: Whether the experiment has a start date.

is_running.description: Whether the experiment is launched and not ended.

latest_calculation.description: The latest finished calculation of the metrics, which the metric results check reads. Null before launch, on an archived experiment, or when the read failed.

metric_compiles.description: The compile of each metric's query without running it, as the reader, which the 'Invalid metric definitions' check reads. A metric that compiles is cached per reader for a day, and a failing metric compiles again on every request. Null when the compile itself failed.

primary_metric_count.description: Single-use primary metrics plus shared metrics linked as primary.

project.description: Facts about the project that no check reads yet, from the same providers as the setup context.

reader_access.description: What the reader may read, which decides what the checks can load.

secondary_metric_count.description: Single-use secondary metrics plus shared metrics linked as secondary.

condition_set.description: The number of the release condition, from 1.

people.description: The people whose latest call this condition served.

calls.description: The flag's calls in the window, of any flag version.

filters_test_accounts.description: Whether the counts leave out the calls that the project's filter for internal and test users excludes, because the experiment applies that filter.

people_assigned_outside.description: The people who got a variant from a call without a flag version that is no local evaluation in a server SDK, from an hour after the start of the window: a bootstrap or the caller's own assignment. With a 0% rollout, 10 or more of them turn `running_but_no_rollout` into `assigned_outside_flag_service`.

people_by_set.description: People by the release condition that served their latest call of the flag's version.

remotely_evaluated_calls.description: The calls that the flag service evaluated. Only those name a condition set. Local evaluation in a server SDK and a bootstrapped value name none.

since.description: The start of the window: the latest of launch, the flag's last save and 7 days ago.

team_timezone.description: The project's time zone, which the finding uses for times.

exposed.description: Whether anyone was exposed between the first and the last counted change of this kind. Asked only when the last sets back what the first changed. Null when not asked or unknown.

kind.description:
The kind of change. A bucketing change is a change of a setting that decides the variant draw.

* `split` - Split
* `bucketing` - Bucketing
* `release_conditions` - Release-condition

question.description: What was asked, as the staff view names it.

activation.description: The event, or the action's name, that has to follow a user's flag call before the user counts. Null without an activation.

custom_event.description: The event the exposure criteria count in place of the flag calls. Null for flag calls or an action.

required_flag_key.description: The flag key the exposure query requires on the flag call events. Null for a custom event or an action.

variant_property.description: The event property that holds the variant.

hours_since_launch.description: Hours from launch to the computation of the answer, as the checks read them.

multiple_variant_handling.description: How the analysis treats people in several variants: 'exclude' or 'first_seen'.

sample_ratio_mismatch_p_value.description: The p-value of the sample ratio test. Null when there was too little data.

total_exposures.description: Exposed people by variant. '$multiple' counts the people exposed to more than one variant.

error.description: Why the query or its last background calculation failed. Set for 'failed', and for 'stale' when the recalculation failed.

findings.description: The findings of the exposure checks on this answer: zero exposures, SRM and bias risk.

status.description:
Whether a cached answer was read. 'calculating' means no answer is cached and a calculation runs in the background, so a later request reads a fresh answer. 'stale' means the cached answer is past its age: a recalculation runs in the background, or the last one failed and 'error' says why. After a failed calculation, no new one starts for 20 minutes.

* `ready` - Ready
* `stale` - Stale
* `calculating` - Calculating
* `not_launched` - Not Launched
* `no_query_access` - No Query Access
* `failed` - Failed

totals.description: What the exposure checks read. Null without an answer.

deleted.description: Whether the flag is deleted.

release_conditions.description: The flag's release conditions, in evaluation order.

split_text.description: The split as text, in the form of a change's before and after, such as 'control 50%, test 50%'.

variants.description: The flag's variants and their split.

after.description: The value after the change, in the same form.

before.description: The value before the change as text, such as 'control 50%, test 50%' or 'device_id'. 'none' when unset.

changed.description: What changed, as the staff view names it, such as 'Split' or 'Key'.

counted.description: Whether the checks count this change: every change counts from the first change, of any kind, with an exposure before it, or an unknown answer. False for every change when not checked.

kind.description:
The kind of change. A bucketing change is a change of a setting that decides the variant draw.

* `split` - Split
* `bucketing` - Bucketing
* `release_conditions` - Release-condition

changes.description: Every change since launch that can move exposed people, of every kind, in time order. A bucketing change is one per setting and save. A rollout change alone is no release-condition change. Empty for 'no_history_access', which does not read them.

checked.description: Whether the changes were compared with the exposures. False when not_checked_reason is set.

exposed_before_first.description: Whether anyone was exposed before the first counted change. Null when unknown or not checked.

exposed_between.description: One entry for each kind of change with a counted change, in the order of the kinds.

not_checked_reason.description: Why the changes were not compared with the exposures: 'no_history_access', 'no_query_access', 'exposure_filters', 'exposure_action', 'exposure_criteria', 'too_many_saves' or 'too_many_conditions'. Null when they were.

start_date.description: The experiment's start date. The flag history counts changes from it, as the results count exposures from it.

team_timezone.description: The project's time zone, which the findings use for times.

failures.description: The metrics whose latest calculation failed, with the error that the results page shows.

finished_at.description: When the latest calculation that the results page shows finished. Null when none has finished.

hours_of_data.description: The hours from launch to the end of the data of this calculation. Null when none has finished.

zero_metrics.description: The metrics that read zero in every variant in this calculation.

error_type.description: The class that the calculation stored for the error, such as 'timeout' or 'rate_limited'. Null for a failure stored without a class.

message.description: The stored message as the results page shows it, without the names that HogQL suggests and the list of a scope's fields. Null when it can hold evaluation rules that the AI evaluation markers keep out of the browser.

name.description: The metric's name as the experiment shows it.

retriable.description: Whether the results page shows a button to try the metric again, which it does for a retriable error.

step.description: The step of the calculation that failed, such as 'calculation'. Null when the failure names none.

kind.description:
Who rejected the query: 'rejected' is a validation of the query builder, 'syntax' and 'query' come from HogQL, 'definition' means the stored definition doesn't parse into a metric.

* `rejected` - Rejected
* `syntax` - Syntax
* `query` - Query
* `definition` - Definition

message.description: The compiler's message, without the list of a scope's fields. Null when it can hold the evaluation rules that the AI evaluation markers keep out of the browser.

name.description: The metric's name as the experiment shows it.

exposure_query_fails.description: Whether the exposure query alone doesn't compile. Every metric then fails for that reason, so no failure is listed.

failures.description: The metrics whose query doesn't compile, with the compiler's message.

metric_count.description: The metrics that the experiment calculates, one per uuid.

no_access_count.description: The metrics that read a warehouse table or view that the reader may not query, so they aren't checked.

unknown_count.description: The metrics whose compile raised an error that names no problem of the metric, such as a defect.

sdk_profile.description: Which SDKs call feature flags and where flags are evaluated, across the whole project. Skipped for a reader who may not query events.

can_query_events.description: Whether the reader may query events, which the flag-change and forced-variant checks need.

can_read_flag_history.description: Whether the reader may read the flag's history, which the flag-change checks need.

denied_event_properties.description: Event properties the reader is denied. The forced-variant and release-condition checks skip their scan when one of them is a flag call property it reads.

number.description: The condition's position in the flag, from 1, as the flag page labels it ('Set 2').

pinned_variant.description: The variant that the condition's override serves. Null when the condition is not reachable, has no override, or its override names no variant of the flag.

property_count.description: The number of property filters. Null when the flag stores no list.

reachable.description: Whether the condition can serve a request. A condition after one that matches everyone never does.

rollout_percentage.description: The condition's rollout, in percent. Null when the flag stores no number.

ExperimentHealthInputsTrafficStatusEnum.description:
* `read` - Read
* `not_needed` - Not Needed
* `no_query_access` - No Query Access
* `denied_properties` - Denied Properties
* `no_flag_version` - No Flag Version
* `unknown` - Unknown

key.description: The variant key. Null when the flag stores no string key.

rollout_percentage.description: The variant's share of the split, in percent. Null when the flag stores no number.

exposures.description: The persons or groups of the result, across the variants.

name.description: The name of the metric, as the results page shows it.

ratio_side.description: The side of a ratio that reads zero. Each side that reads zero has its own entry. Null for the other metric types.

role.description: Whether the metric is a primary or a secondary metric of the experiment.

stopped_events.description: The events of the metric that the project last received before launch.

aggregation_group_type_index.description: The group type the condition set assigns variants by: its own, or the flag's when it sets none. Null when it assigns them by user.

property_count.description: The number of filters a user must match, such as properties and cohorts. 0 matches all users.

rollout_percentage.description: The share of the users matching the condition set's filters who get the flag, from 0 to 100.

threshold.description: The value that the key must reach. Below it, the check reports no finding.

value.description:
The key in `values` that must reach the threshold before the check judges.

* `exposed_count` - Users or groups exposed since launch, as the exposure criteria count them, including those exposed to multiple variants
* `compared_count` - Exposed users or groups in the variants that the sample ratio test compares, without those exposed to multiple variants
* `multiple_variant_count` - Users or groups exposed to more than one variant
* `multiple_variant_percentage` - multiple_variant_count as a share of exposed_count
* `multiple_variant_handling` - What the results do with users exposed to more than one variant: exclude or first_seen
* `p_value` - P-value of the sample ratio test
* `since_launch_hours` - Hours since launch
* `exposed_without_test_account_filter_count` - Users or groups that the exposure criteria count without the test account filters
* `kept_by_test_account_filter_percentage` - exposed_count as a share of exposed_without_test_account_filter_count
* `unserved_exposed_count` - Users or groups first exposed after the day of the feature flag's last save, in a variant that the flag doesn't serve since that save
* `unserved_exposed_percentage` - unserved_exposed_count as a share of the users or groups first exposed after that day
* `only_count_matured_users` - Whether "Require completed conversion or retention window" is on
* `primary_metric_count` - Primary metrics that the calculation computes
* `waiting_metric_count` - Of the primary metrics, those whose conversion or retention window hasn't passed for any user yet
* `metric_count` - Metrics that the calculation computes
* `completed_metric_count` - Metrics whose result of the latest calculation the page shows
* `failed_metric_count` - Metrics whose latest calculation failed
* `calculated_at` - When the latest calculation of the metrics finished
* `flag_active` - Whether the feature flag is enabled
* `flag_deleted` - Whether the feature flag is deleted
* `flag_rolled_out` - Whether a release condition of the feature flag rolls out to more than 0%
* `shipped_variant` - The key of the variant that the feature flag serves to everyone, or null when it serves more than one
* `flag_last_called_at` - When PostHog last recorded a call of the feature flag
* `since_start_hours` - Hours since the experiment's start date, which can be earlier than the launch
* `daily_calculation_ends_at` - When the daily calculation stops covering the experiment, a fixed number of days after its start date
* `metric_name` - The name of a metric
* `metric_role` - Whether a metric is primary or secondary
* `ratio_side` - The side of a ratio metric, numerator or denominator, or null for the other metric types
* `sample_count` - Users or groups in a metric's results, across the variants
* `planned_sample_count` - Users or groups that the running time estimate needs to detect its minimum detectable effect
* `data_hours` - Hours of data that a metric's latest calculation holds since launch, within the metric's conversion window
* `variant` - The key of a variant
* `difference_percentage` - A variant's difference from the control on the primary metric, relative to the control, with its sign
* `detectable_difference_percentage` - The smallest difference from the control that the variant's sample can reliably detect, relative to the control
* `significant` - Whether a variant's difference from the control is significant
* `forced_condition_count` - Release conditions of the feature flag that serve a fixed variant through a variant override
* `matched_count` - Users or groups that a release condition served since traffic_since_at, without those forced to a variant that has 0% in the split
* `variant_matched_count` - Of matched_count, the users or groups who got the variant. Estimated from the split for those assigned at random
* `forced_count` - Users or groups that a release condition with a variant override served
* `forced_percentage` - forced_count as a share of variant_matched_count
* `traffic_since_at` - The start of the window that matched_count counts: 7 days ago, or the launch or the flag's last save if later
* `changed_at` - When a change of the feature flag was saved
* `before_exposure` - Whether a change of the feature flag was saved before anyone was exposed, so it moved nobody. Null when unknown
* `changed_setting` - The flag setting that a change of the bucketing changed, as the flag page names it
* `before` - What a change of the feature flag changed, as it was before the change, in words
* `after` - What a change of the feature flag changed, as it was after the change, in words
* `before_filters` - The feature flag's release conditions before a change, as the flag stores them: an object with the groups and the aggregation_group_type_index of its filters. Null when they don't fit the size limit of the check's rows. The flag's history shows them in full
* `after_filters` - The feature flag's release conditions after a change, as the flag stores them, like before_filters
* `flag_service_call_percentage` - Of the feature flag's calls since traffic_since_at that returned a variant, the share that the flag service evaluated. Only these calls name the release condition that served them, so local evaluation and bootstrapped values count in no condition
* `event` - The name of an event that the check looked up
* `event_received` - Whether the project has received the event. Null when PostHog keeps no record of the event name
* `invalid_metric_count` - Metrics whose query doesn't compile, so every calculation fails
* `unchecked_metric_count` - Metrics whose query the check couldn't compile, because they read data that the reader can't query or the compile failed for a reason other than the metric
* `flag_split` - The feature flag's variants with their rollout percentages, in words
* `baseline_variant` - The key of the variant that the analysis compares the others with, or null when the analysis picks one
* `other_running_experiment_count` - Other experiments that run on the same feature flag and are not archived
* `assigned_outside_count` - Users or groups who got a variant from a call that the flag service didn't evaluate and that is no local evaluation, such as a bootstrapped value. Read only while a running experiment's feature flag has a 0% rollout
* `other_draft_experiment_count` - Other draft experiments on the same feature flag that are not archived

ExperimentHealthRuleSideEnum.description:
* `above` - Finding above the threshold
* `below` - Finding below the threshold

aggregation_group_type_index.description: The flag's own group type, which the exposure counts and the results use. A condition set can override it. Null for users.

bucketing_identifier.description:
The flag's `bucketing_identifier`. Null on the flag reads as distinct_id.

* `distinct_id` - User ID (default)
* `device_id` - Device ID

early_exit.description: Whether the flag stops at the first condition set whose filters match, also when its rollout leaves the user out. Otherwise such a user goes on to the next set.

ensure_experience_continuity.description: The flag's 'Persist flag across authentication steps' setting.

evaluation_contexts.description: The names of the flag's evaluation contexts. When PostHog evaluates the flag, an SDK that sends evaluation contexts gets it only when it sends one of these, and an SDK that sends none gets it. Empty when the flag has none.

evaluation_runtime.description:
The flag's `evaluation_runtime`. Null on the flag reads as all.

* `server` - Server
* `client` - Client
* `all` - All

release_conditions.description: The flag's condition sets as stored, in the order the flag evaluates them. Whether a set can serve a request depends on the sets before it and on `early_exit`.

ExperimentHoldout.description: A holdout group — a stable slice of users excluded from experiment exposure.

description.description: Optional description of what this holdout reserves and why.

filters.description: Non-empty list of release-condition groups defining the held-out population, using the same shape as feature-flag release conditions. Each element's `rollout_percentage` (0–100, may be fractional) is the **exclusion** percentage — the share of users held back from all experiments that reference this holdout. `properties` optionally narrows the group by person/group properties. Do not set `variant`: the server normalizes it to `holdout-{id}`. Note that only the first element's `rollout_percentage` is embedded into each linked experiment's feature flag, and this population is shared across every experiment using the holdout.

name.description: Human-readable name for the holdout group.

user_access_level.description: The effective access level the user has for this object
Read-only, server-computed effective access level; absent on a not-yet-created holdout.

ExperimentInSessionExposure.description: How the recordings tab's in-session exposure scope reads on this experiment.

available.description: Whether the in-session exposure scope can answer for this experiment. Mirrors the recordings query, which refuses `experiment_exposure.in_session` exactly when this is false.

unavailable_reason.description: Why the in-session scope can't answer for this experiment, worded for display next to the disabled option. Null when available.

uses_stamped_fallback.description: True when in-session evidence is the stamped `$feature/<flag_key>` property, which means the flag was active in the session, rather than the exposure event itself being captured there. Copy must not claim the exposure was captured in the session when this is set.

ids.description: IDs of all experiments matching the current list filters that the user can edit.

total.description: Number of matching editable experiments.

lower_bound_percentile.description: Winsorization lower percentile bound, as a fraction in [0, 1] (e.g. 0.01 for the 1st percentile).
lower_bound_percentile.title: Lower Bound Percentile

threshold.description: When set, reports the percentage of users whose per-user summed/counted value reaches or exceeds this threshold. Only meaningful for sum/count math types.
threshold.title: Threshold

upper_bound_percentile.description: Winsorization upper percentile bound, as a fraction in [0, 1] (e.g. 0.99 for the 99th percentile).
upper_bound_percentile.title: Upper Bound Percentile

value_format.description: How results show the value of the metric. Metrics that report a share of users (funnel, retention, mean with a threshold) ignore it.

version.description: version of the node, used for schema migrations
version.title: Version

lower_bound_percentile.title: Lower Bound Percentile

upper_bound_percentile.description: Winsorization upper percentile bound, as a fraction in [0, 1] (e.g. 0.99 for the 99th percentile).
upper_bound_percentile.title: Upper Bound Percentile

ExperimentMetricsRecalculationJob.description: POST response: the job just queued, or the one already active. It carries no results or live progress yet.

completed_at.description: When processing completed

completed_metrics.description: Number of metrics with a COMPLETED result row that did not fail in this run (derived, not stored)

experiment_id.description: ID of the experiment being recalculated

failed_metrics.description: Number of failed metrics in this run (derived): metrics with a FAILED result row or a metric_errors entry. A metric that fails keeps its earlier completed result, so it can count here and still have a completed row in results. The error of a rejected run counts only for a metric without a row

id.description: Unique identifier for this recalculation job

is_existing.description: True if returning an existing job rather than a newly created one

metric_errors.description: Terminal failure per metric_uuid: {step, message, error_type, retriable, timestamp, exposures_path}. retriable is true when a transient error exhausted its attempts, so a heal_latest_run or manual_retry can succeed; false when the metric config, the data, or a resource limit must change first. exposures_path is where the query read the exposures, and is missing when the query failed before it was built

query_to.description: Upper time bound the metrics in this run were calculated against (the data freshness cutoff). Shared by every metric in the run; null until processing starts

started_at.description: When processing started

status.description:
Current status of the recalculation job

* `pending` - Pending
* `in_progress` - In Progress
* `completed` - Completed
* `failed` - Failed

total_metrics.description: Total number of metrics to recalculate

active_run.description: Run currently executing for this experiment, if any; poll it by id for live progress

completed_at.description: When processing completed

completed_metrics.description: Number of metrics with a COMPLETED result row that did not fail in this run (derived, not stored)

estimated_rows_total.description: ClickHouse's total_rows_approx across running queries plus the final read_rows of finished ones. A soft ceiling revised mid-scan, so it can exceed or trail rows_read; treat rows_read as the reliable signal

exceeds_recalculation_age_limit.description: True when the experiment started too long ago for its metrics to be recalculated. A recalculation request then returns a rejected run with the recalculation_window_too_long error, and the saved results stay as they are

experiment_id.description: ID of the experiment being recalculated

failed_metrics.description: Number of failed metrics in this run (derived): metrics with a FAILED result row or a metric_errors entry. metric_retries.description: Transient retry state per metric_uuid: {attempt, max_attempts, error_type, message, next_retry_at}. message is a user-safe description of the error that triggered the retry. Present only while a metric is between failed attempts; cleared when it succeeds or fails terminally, so treat entries for metrics that already have a result as stale.

query_to.description: Upper time bound the metrics in this run were calculated against (the data freshness cutoff). Shared by every metric in the run; null until processing starts

result_source.description:
Where these results came from: 'recalculation' for a real metrics-recalculation run, 'timeseries_fallback' for a cold-start placeholder built from the latest daily timeseries data.

* `recalculation` - recalculation
* `timeseries_fallback` - timeseries_fallback

results.description: Per-metric results of this run, scoped by the run's recalc fingerprint. When a metric fails, its earlier completed result at the same window stays here and the failure is in metric_errors

rows_read.description: Rows read by the run's metric queries so far, both finished and currently running. Cumulative and roughly monotonic across the run; the primary live progress signal

started_at.description: When processing started

status.description:
Current status of the recalculation job

* `pending` - Pending
* `in_progress` - In Progress
* `completed` - Completed
* `failed` - Failed

total_metrics.description: Total number of metrics to recalculate

metric_retries.description: Transient retry state per metric_uuid: {attempt, max_attempts, error_type, message, next_retry_at}. message is a user-safe description of the error that triggered the retry. Present only while a metric is between failed attempts; cleared when it succeeds or fails terminally, so treat entries for metrics that already have a result as stale.

query_to.description: Upper time bound the metrics in this run were calculated against (the data freshness cutoff). Shared by every metric in the run; null until processing starts

results.description: Per-metric results of this run, scoped by the run's recalc fingerprint. When a metric fails, its earlier completed result at the same window stays here and the failure is in metric_errors

rows_read.description: Rows read by the run's metric queries so far, both finished and currently running. Cumulative and roughly monotonic across the run; the primary live progress signal

started_at.description: When processing started

ExperimentSavedMetric.description: Mixin for serializers to add user access control fields

description.description: Short description of what the metric measures.

linked_experiments.description: Experiments using this shared metric (soft-deleted experiments excluded). Populated only on single-metric retrieve; always an empty list in list responses.

name.description: Name of the shared metric. Must be unique within the project (case-insensitive).

query.description: ExperimentMetric JSON. Must have kind='ExperimentMetric' and a metric_type: 'mean' (set source to an EventsNode with an event name), 'funnel' (set series to an array of EventsNode steps), 'ratio' (set numerator and denominator EventsNode entries), 'quantile' (set source to an EventsNode or ActionsNode with math_property, the numeric property to measure, and quantile, the level in [0.01, 0.99], for example 0.9 for p90), or 'retention' (set start_event and completion_event). Legacy kinds (ExperimentTrendsQuery, ExperimentFunnelsQuery) are rejected for new shared metrics.

user_access_level.description: The effective access level the user has for this object

is_running.description: True when the experiment is launched and not yet stopped.

name.description: Experiment name.

ExperimentSessionBucketExcludedMetric.description: One requested metric the bucket could not be computed over.

reason.description: Why the metric can't be matched to recordings: a data-warehouse-only source, a retention window, or events only ever captured server-side.

ExperimentSessionBucketMetric.description: One metric the bucket was computed over.

metric_name.description: Display name of the metric, or an event-derived title (matching the experiment UI) when unnamed.

ExperimentSessionBucketRequest.description: Request body for the session-bucket endpoint.

bucket.description:
Which question the returned session set answers. 'fired_any': the session fired at least one event of any listed metric (an OR the recordings query itself can't express). 'no_metric_activity': the session fired none of them. 'funnel_dropoff': the session saw an exposure event but never fired the funnel metric's last step; the exposure is the funnel's implicit first step, the same as in the experiment analysis. All three are session-scoped and goal-free: they say what happened in the session, not whether it helped or hurt the metric.

* `fired_any` - fired_any
* `no_metric_activity` - no_metric_activity
* `funnel_dropoff` - funnel_dropoff

limit.description: Maximum session IDs to return, at most 100. The most recently active matching sessions win.

metric_uuids.description: Metrics the bucket is computed over. Exactly one funnel metric for 'funnel_dropoff'. Omit for the other buckets to use every metric of the experiment that can be matched to recordings.

items.description: UUID of one of the experiment's metrics.

variant.description: Restrict to sessions that saw this variant. Omit for every variant. A session that saw more than one variant matches each variant it saw.

ExperimentSessionBucketResponse.description: Session recordings of an experiment matching a bucket.

considered_metrics.description: The metrics the bucket was actually computed over. Load-bearing for 'no_metric_activity': 'fired nothing' only means something next to the list of metrics it was evaluated against.

date_from.description: Start of the window scanned, never before the experiment started. At most 30 days before date_to when the scan found an exposure to anchor on. When it found none, how far back the search for one reached, which the project's recording retention bounds. Matches outside the window are not returned.

date_to.description: End of the window scanned: 24 hours after the latest exposure captured in a session, capped at the experiment's end date or now. The pad covers the metric events a session fires after its exposure. The scan ends at the experiment's end date, or now while it runs, when that exposure can't be located, so an experiment whose exposures stopped long ago is still scanned where its sessions are.

excluded_metrics.description: Requested metrics left out of the bucket because they can never match a recording, with the reason. They are reported rather than silently producing an empty result.

filter_test_accounts.description: Whether the project's test-account filters were applied, following the experiment's exposure criteria, the same rule the experiment's recordings list uses.

session_ids.description: IDs of matching sessions that have a recording, most recently active first. Feed these to a recordings query as session_ids; they are a subset of the experiment's exposed sessions, so the exposure filter can stay in place alongside them.

truncated.description: True when more sessions matched than the limit returned. Older matches were dropped first.

used_exposure_fallback.description: True when the exposed population was matched on the stamped $feature/<flag key> event property instead of the exposure event, because the default exposure event has only ever been captured server-side and can never match a session. The sessions then mean 'the flag was active in this session', not 'the exposure moment was captured'. The variant comes from the flag's value on each event, so a returning user can appear under a variant they were re-bucketed into later.

ExperimentSessionContextItem.description: One experiment whose feature flag a session recording saw.

experiment_end_date.description: When the experiment ended. Null while the experiment is still running.

experiment_id.description: ID of the experiment whose feature flag the session saw.

first_exposure_timestamp.description: Timestamp of the first event in the session matching the experiment's exposure criteria — the default exposure event ($feature_flag_called), or the configured custom event/action. Null when no event in the session matched the criteria; the variant is then known from flag evaluations or stamped $feature/<key> properties. Session-scoped: the experiment analysis counts exposure per person across the whole run window, so the person's counted first exposure may lie in an earlier session.

flag_key.description: Key of the experiment's feature flag.

metrics_in_session.description: This experiment's metrics with at least one matching event in the session, sorted by first occurrence. Empty when none of the experiment's metric events fired during the session.

multiple_variants.description: True when the session saw more than one variant of this flag.

variant.description: Variant the session saw. Taken from the earliest event matching the experiment's exposure criteria when one exists, otherwise from the earliest flag evaluation in the session, otherwise from the $feature/<key> property stamped on the session's events.

variants_seen.description: All distinct variant values observed for this flag during the session, sorted alphabetically. Only the flag's defined variant keys count; non-enrollment responses (false) are ignored. More than one value means the session saw multiple variants — a signal of multi-exposure bias.

ExperimentSessionContextResponse.description: Experiment/variant context for a session recording.

results.description: Experiments (and variants) the session saw, sorted by experiment name. Empty when no launched experiment's run window overlaps the recording or no flag data was observed in the session.

session_id.description: ID of the session recording the context was resolved for.

ExperimentSessionContextsRequest.description: Request body for the batch session-context endpoint.

session_ids.description: IDs of the session recordings to resolve experiment context for, at most 20 per request. Duplicates are ignored.

items.description: ID of one session recording.

ExperimentSessionContextsResponse.description: Experiment/variant context for a batch of session recordings.

results.description: Per-session experiment context, in the order the session IDs were requested. Sessions whose recording metadata doesn't exist yet (still ingesting, or unknown to this project) are omitted, as are recordings you don't have access to and sessions beyond the batch's recording-day budget (only the most recent days are computed). Fetch omitted sessions individually via the single-session endpoint.

ExperimentSessionEventDeltaResponse.description:
The recordings worth watching for this experiment, grouped into cards.

Descriptive, never a result: cards say where behavior visibly differed and hand over the
recordings, while the experiment's results measure its metrics over the whole run window and
state the magnitudes. Nothing here says a variant is winning.

cards.description: The shelf, strongest comparison first, then the variant's own rendering, then metric shortcuts. Events the variants can't be told apart on get no card at all rather than a weak one, so an empty shelf means no difference was big enough to be sure of, not that nothing was measured. Empty also takes the metric shortcuts with it: a shelf of shortcuts and no finding restates what the experiment's results already answer while reading as a finding, so it is withheld. Read empty_reason and say what it reports instead of presenting an empty shelf. Group by kind before presenting: a 'variant_only' card outranks every real difference by construction, and reading the shelf in order would report it as the headline.

date_from.description: When the earliest compared person was first exposed. The comparison takes the most recently exposed people, newest first, until it has as many as one comparison covers or their first sessions span 14 days of events, so on a busy experiment this is hours rather than days before date_to, and on an experiment that stopped enrolling it can be long before the experiment's end. Display this, not the experiment's own dates. Equal to date_to when nobody has been exposed yet.

date_to.description: One minute past the newest compared person's first exposure. Nobody first exposed between date_from and date_to was passed over, so the pair is a stretch of enrollment rather than a hull around scattered people. It bounds who was selected, not who was read: variants[].persons counts only those who then had a session. While an experiment runs this sits about an hour before now, because the newest hour of enrollment is held back until those people's first sessions have finished rather than read half-way through. Sessions reach past it, up to 24 hours after each person's own exposure, so this is not the end of the events that were read.

dropped_duplicate_cards.description: How many cards were removed because their recordings were already another card's on the same shelf. Nothing was lost: the recordings are all reachable through the cards that stayed.

empty_reason.description:
Why cards is empty, and null whenever cards is not empty. Report which of the four happened rather than reporting an empty shelf, because they ask different things of the reader. 'too_early': fewer than two variants have min_variant_persons exposed people, so nothing was compared yet. The answer can still change unless sessions_truncated is true, in which case only the people exposed between date_from and date_to were compared and more time helps only if more people are exposed within a stretch that long; a rollout split that changed during the run lands here too, and the experiment's exposure chart is where that shows. 'no_separation': the variants were compared and no event told them apart, which is a result rather than a failure. 'no_recordings': events did tell the variants apart, but no recording behind them can be opened, so the project's session replay sampling and retention are what decide whether this surface can ever show anything. 'no_session_linked_exposures': the people exposed between date_from and date_to had no session we can see since being exposed, looking up to 24 hours after each exposure, so there was nothing to compare. Two things reach this state, and they ask for different answers: no browser or mobile SDK is capturing events, because sessions exist nowhere else, or the exposed people have not come back. While the experiment runs the read stops at the time of the request, so people exposed less than a day ago are judged on less than a day and can still return. Check which one before telling anyone to check back, because more exposures captured the same way yield more of the same. Never fill an empty shelf with the experiment's metrics: shortcut cards to those metrics' events are withheld here for exactly that reason.

* `too_early` - too_early
* `no_separation` - no_separation
* `no_recordings` - no_recordings
* `no_session_linked_exposures` - no_session_linked_exposures

events_truncated.description: True when the project has more distinct event names in the window than one comparison can rank, so some were never considered.

filter_test_accounts.description: Whether the project's test-account filters were applied, following the experiment's exposure criteria, the same rule the experiment's recordings list uses.

max_card_recordings.description: The most recordings one card can carry. A card whose recording_count equals this hit the ceiling, so report it as 'at least this many' rather than as a count.

metric_events.description: The events the experiment's own metrics count. A card on one of these carries metric_name and must be read as pointing at the experiment's results, which measure the same event over the whole run window with the statistics that go with a result. Cards state no magnitude for exactly this reason, so never turn one into a claim about how the metric moved.

min_variant_persons.description: How many exposed people a variant needs before it can be compared at all. Below it a variant's cards would be noise whatever the evidence bar allows.

multiple_variant_handling.description:
How the experiment handles someone who saw more than one variant, followed here so the cards split their people the same way the analysis does.

* `exclude` - exclude
* `first_seen` - first_seen

multiple_variant_persons.description: People who saw more than one variant and were left out of every card. Always 0 when the experiment attributes such users to the variant they saw first.

sessions_truncated.description: True when more people were exposed than one comparison covers, so the most recently exposed were used and people exposed before date_from were left out. Every variant is still covered over the same stretch of enrollment. Named for the session ceiling it used to report; the name is kept for existing readers.

too_early.description: True when fewer than two variants have min_variant_persons exposed people, so no comparison exists and cards is empty. Show the variants' counts alongside it: an empty shelf presented without them would read as 'the variants behaved identically'. Read empty_reason and sessions_truncated before telling anyone to check back: this is also true when the variants are empty because the people exposed have no sessions we can see, which empty_reason reports as 'no_session_linked_exposures' and which more time fixes only while those people were exposed less than a day ago. And when sessions_truncated is true, only people exposed between date_from and date_to were compared, so more time helps only if more people are exposed within a stretch that long.

used_exposure_fallback.description: Always false. The compared population is the exposed population the experiment's results count, matched to sessions by person, so no stamped-property fallback exists any more. The field stays for compatibility with existing readers.

variants.description: Every variant the analysis compares, with its population, in the flag's variant order. A variant the experiment excludes never appears here, because the analysis does not count it either, so read a missing key as excluded rather than as zero people.

ExperimentSessionMetricHit.description: One experiment metric with at least one matching event in a session recording.

event_count.description: Total number of events in the session matching any of the metric's event/action sources.

first_timestamp.description: Timestamp of the first event in the session matching the metric.

metric_name.description: Display name of the metric, or an event-derived title (matching the experiment UI) when unnamed.

metric_uuid.description: UUID of the experiment metric (inline primary/secondary or saved) whose events fired.

sources.description: Which of the metric's sources fired, so a hit reads as 'step 2 of 3' or 'the start event of a retention metric' rather than an unqualified 'this metric happened'. Sources with no matching event are omitted, as is the whole breakdown for metrics beyond the scan's aggregate ceiling. A retention metric whose start and completion are the same event contributes only the start source: the completion would match the identical events and render a duplicate.

timestamps.description: Ascending timestamps of the metric's matching events in the session, capped at the first 50. event_count is the true total, so this list may be shorter — treat these as seek points, not a count.

ExperimentSessionMetricSourceHit.description: One event/action source of a metric with at least one matching event in a session recording.

event_count.description: Number of events in the session matching this source.

first_timestamp.description: Timestamp of the first event in the session matching this source.

source_index.description: 0-based position of this source among all the metric's sources, data-warehouse ones included — so a funnel step keeps its real step number even when an earlier step has no session events.

source_name.description: Display name of the source event or action.

source_role.description:
What this source means to its metric: 'source' (a mean metric's single event), 'step' (a funnel step, numbered by source_index), 'numerator'/'denominator' (a ratio metric's two sides), or 'retention_start'/'retention_completion' (a retention metric's start event and return visit). A hit on one source is not a hit on the metric as the analysis counts it.

* `source` - source
* `step` - step
* `numerator` - numerator
* `denominator` - denominator
* `retention_start` - retention_start
* `retention_completion` - retention_completion

source_total.description: Total number of sources the metric is defined over.

timestamps.description: Ascending timestamps of this source's matching events in the session, capped at the first 50. event_count is the true total, so this list may be shorter — treat these as seek points, not a count.

computed_at.description: When the numbers were computed. They are cached for an hour.

conversion_rate.description: persons_converted divided by persons_reached. Null without target_event.

event_volume.description: Metric events in the window, with metric_properties applied. 0 means the event did not occur under those filters, so check the event name before you trust a conversion_rate of 0.

funnel_baseline_stats.description: Pass as baseline_stats to experiment-calculate-running-time with metric_type 'funnel'. Null without target_event.

mean_count_baseline_stats.description: Pass as baseline_stats to experiment-calculate-running-time with metric_type 'mean_count'. It counts metric events in the whole window, not only after the first target event, so it can overstate the baseline. Null without target_event.

metric_properties.description: The property filters that were applied to the metric event. Empty when none were passed.

note.description: What the mean count baseline counts.

persons_converted.description: Persons who sent the metric event at or after their first target event. Null without target_event.

persons_reached.description: Persons who sent the target event. Null without target_event.

source_event.description: The metric event that was counted.

target_event.description: The target event the baseline starts from, or null when none was passed.

test_accounts_filtered.description: Whether test accounts were left out. It follows the default a new experiment gets, so the baseline matches the population that experiment analyzes. False when the project defines no test-account filters.

unique_persons.description: Persons who sent the metric event, with metric_properties applied.

window_days.description: Days of events read, ending now.

data.description: Baseline of the candidate metric. Skipped without metric_event.

status.description:
'ok' when data holds the section. 'skipped' when an input the section needs was not passed. 'timed_out' when the query was too expensive to finish. 'error' when the read failed. Every status other than 'ok' leaves data null, and the other sections are still valid.

* `ok` - Ok
* `skipped` - Skipped
* `timed_out` - Timed Out
* `error` - Error

ExperimentSetupContextInput.description:
What the caller plans to test. Every field is optional; a section that needs a missing input
comes back with status 'skipped'.

metric_event.description: Event of the candidate primary metric. With target_event, candidate_metric returns a baseline. Without it, candidate_metric returns only the event's volume. Also marks the shared metrics that count this event.

metric_properties.description: Event or person property filters that narrow the metric event, for the metric that counts only some of its occurrences. At most 10 filters, and each needs type 'event' or 'person'. Needs metric_event.

previous_experiments_limit.description: How many experiments to return, most recently launched first, then drafts, 1 to 25.

shared_metrics_limit.description: How many shared metrics to return, most reused first, 1 to 25.

target_event.description: Event that marks a visit to the surface under test, for example '$pageview' or '$screen'. Needed for target_surface and for the baseline in candidate_metric.

target_properties.description: Event or person property filters that narrow the target event, for example an exact $host and $pathname for one page. At most 10 filters, and each needs type 'event' or 'person'. Needs target_event. Combines with target_url_contains.

target_url_contains.description: Only counts target events whose $current_url contains this text, ignoring case. Needs target_event to be '$pageview'.

ExperimentSetupContextResponse.description:
Facts about the project that decide how to configure a new experiment. Facts only, no
recommendations.

candidate_metric.description: Traffic and baseline of the candidate primary metric.

sdk_profile.description: Which SDKs call feature flags and where flags are evaluated.

target_surface.description: Traffic on the surface under test.

step_counts.description: One entry: the persons who converted.

distinct_ids.description: Distinct ids that sent those events.

events.description: Events this SDK sent in the window, of any kind.

lib.description: The $lib value of the SDK, for example 'web'.

anonymous_share.description: Among this SDK's distinct ids that report whether they are identified, the share that was anonymous. Null when no target event from this SDK reported it.

device_id_share.description: Share of this SDK's target events that carry a $device_id. 0 when it never sends one.

lib.description: The $lib value that sent the target events.

unique_persons.description: Persons who sent the target event from this SDK.

sum.description: Metric events those persons sent in the whole window.

sum_squares.description: Sum over persons of their metric event count squared.

analyzed_exposures.description: metric_samples, but only where the metric type makes it the analyzed population: 'funnel' and 'mean'. Users seen in several variants are left out under the default handling, so it can be lower than exposures. Null for 'retention', whose samples are the units that did the start event, and for 'ratio', whose samples are not exposures either. Also null when the result stores no sample counts, which is not the same as analyzing nobody.

any_variant_significant.description: Whether any variant was significant on that metric in that result.

control_baseline_value.description: What control measured: a conversion rate for 'funnel', an average per unit for 'mean'. Compare it with the rate on the surface itself to see whether the exposure was diluted by users who never reached the surface. Null for other metric types and when control analyzed no units.

metric_samples.description: Units the result counted across all variants. What a unit is depends on metric_type, so read analyzed_exposures where you need exposures. Null when the result stores no sample counts.

metric_type.description: metric_type of the metric this outcome describes: 'funnel', 'mean', 'ratio', 'retention' or 'quantile'.

result_data_through.description: The last moment the result covers. A backfill writes an older day with a recent completed_at, so this says how current the numbers are.

activation_action_id.description: Action used for activation instead of an event, or null.

activation_event.description: Event a user must send after their first exposure event before they count as exposed, or null. This is activation mode, which sits on top of the default exposure event.

bucketing_identifier.description: What the flag buckets users on: 'distinct_id' (default) or 'device_id'. Read from the flag as it stands now.

conclusion.description: The recorded conclusion, for example 'won' or 'inconclusive', or null.

custom_exposure_action_id.description: Action used as the custom exposure, or null.

custom_exposure_event.description: An exposure event other than the default one, or null. A default event narrowed by exposure_property_filters is still the default event, so it stays null here.

end_date.description: When it ended. Null unless stopped.

ensure_experience_continuity.description: Whether the flag keeps a user's variant across authentication steps, read from the flag as it stands now.

evaluation_runtime.description: Where the flag may be evaluated: 'server', 'client' or 'all'. Read from the flag as it stands now.

exposure_property_filters.description: Property filters the exposure is narrowed by, whichever event it counts. An experiment that counts exposure only where $pathname is '/' is the precedent for a new test on that page. Any filter type can appear, cohorts included. Empty when the exposure is not narrowed.

feature_flag_key.description: Key of the feature flag the experiment runs on.

filter_test_accounts.description: Whether exposures leave out test accounts.

group_aggregation.description: Whether the flag buckets groups instead of persons.

has_holdout.description: Whether the experiment uses a holdout group.

minimum_detectable_effect.description: Minimum detectable effect saved from the running time calculator, or null.

multiple_variant_handling.description:
How users seen in several variants are analyzed, with the default resolved.

* `exclude` - exclude
* `first_seen` - first_seen

multiple_variant_handling_set.description: Whether the experiment sets multiple_variant_handling itself instead of using the default.

name.description: Experiment name.

outcome.description: From the completed result that covers the latest data under the experiment's current configuration. A funnel or a mean primary metric is chosen over a retention or a ratio one, because only its samples are the analyzed population. Null when no result exists for that configuration, for example after a relaunch or a settings edit until the results are recalculated, and for older metric definitions that results are never stored for.

primary_metric_events.description: Event names the primary metrics count.

primary_metric_types.description: metric_type of each primary metric, for example 'mean', 'funnel', 'ratio', 'retention' or 'quantile'.

rollout_percentage.description: Rollout percentage of the flag's first release condition, read from the flag as it stands now.

serving_single_variant.description: The one variant the flag now serves to everyone it matches, or null. Shipping a variant rewrites the flag this way, so the split the experiment ran with cannot be read from the flag any more. Only a launched experiment can be shipped, so a draft at 100/0 reports its split as it stands.

shared_metric_count.description: Shared metrics attached to the experiment.

split_even.description: Whether variants split traffic evenly, read from the flag as it stands now. 34/33/33 counts as even. Null on a boolean flag, which has no variants, and null when serving_single_variant is set.

start_date.description: When it launched. Null for drafts.

state.description:
'draft', 'running', 'paused' (running with its flag turned off), 'exposure_frozen' (running with enrollment closed to the already-exposed users) or 'stopped'.

* `draft` - Draft
* `running` - Running
* `paused` - Paused
* `exposure_frozen` - Exposure Frozen
* `stopped` - Stopped

variant_count.description: Variants on the flag, control included.

experiments.description: Most recently launched first, then drafts. Archived experiments are included, deleted ones are not.

summary.description: Counts over the listed experiments.

data.description: How the project's recent experiments were set up and how they went.

status.description:

ExperimentWatchCard.description:
One group of recordings worth opening, and the sentence that justifies it.

Deliberately no rate, no ratio and no person count: a precise number next to an event name is
an effect size, and the experiment's results publish those for everything it measures, computed
over a different window and a different unit. The only number here is how many recordings the
card can actually show.

event.description: The event behind the card.

highlights.description: Which of the card's recordings to open first, at most 3, ranked by how much each one carries: recordings showing several kinds of signal at once come before recordings showing more of a single kind. Offer these before the full list: the recordings list orders by its own sort, so session_ids order never reaches the viewer, and twenty recordings that share an event are otherwise indistinguishable in it. Empty when no recording the viewer can open carries a signal, which is worth saying rather than hiding.

kind.description:
What the card is: 'behavior' for an event this variant did clearly more than the other variants together, 'friction' for the same finding on an error or rage signal, 'variant_only' for an event no other variant fired at all, and 'metric' for a shortcut to recordings around one of the experiment's own metric events. A 'variant_only' card shows the variant rendering its own change rather than a behavior difference, so present it as confirmation the change is live and never as a finding. Metric cards claim nothing about how the metric moved: that is the experiment results' answer.

* `behavior` - behavior
* `friction` - friction
* `variant_only` - variant_only
* `metric` - metric

metric_name.description: The metric this card's event belongs to, on a comparison card as well as on a shortcut card. When set, the experiment's results measure this event over the whole run window with the statistics that go with a result, so say the card points there and never present the card as a second answer about that metric. Null when no metric counts the event.

recording_count.description: How many recordings the card carries, at most max_card_recordings (20). Every card is backed by recordings that actually exist: a finding whose sessions were never recorded is dropped rather than promised. A count sitting on the ceiling means at least that many, so say 'at least' and never compare two such counts: how often the event happened is the experiment's results, and this only counts what replay kept.

session_ids.description: The recordings themselves, most recent first, ready to hand to the recordings list as-is.

strength.description:
How far apart this variant and the rest are, as a band rather than a number: 'only' when nobody in the other variants did it at all among the people compared, then 'far_more', 'more' and 'slightly_more'. Read off the conservative end of the difference, so a card that clears the bar only because the sample is large reports as slight. Null on metric cards, which compare nothing. Present a band as a comparison ('far more common in test'), never convert it into a multiple.

* `only` - only
* `far_more` - far_more
* `more` - more
* `slightly_more` - slightly_more

variant.description: The variant whose recordings these are: for comparison cards, the one that did the event more.

ExperimentWatchHighlight.description: One recording a card names first, and the phrase that says why.

reason.description: Everything this recording carries that earned it the place, ready to render as-is, for example '6 rage clicks, 6 errors' or '1 error, did this 4 times'. Every signal the session shows is listed, so the phrase is the whole picture rather than the single strongest part of it. Friction counts run from the moment the person was exposed to the end of the session, so friction before they met the variant is left out; 'did this N times' counts the card's own event. Not a comparison and not a reason the card exists.

session_id.description: The recording to open. Always one of the card's own session_ids.

key.description: The variant key.

persons.description: Exposed people the comparison read for this variant: the most recently exposed people, each read from their first session after being exposed. Someone selected who had no session in that horizon is not counted here, so this sits at or below the variant's enrollment between date_from and date_to. People rather than sessions because a variant can change how often the flag is evaluated again later, which moves a variant's session count without anyone behaving differently. One session each, from the moment of exposure on, so every variant gets the same amount of behavior per person.

sessions.description: Sessions those people had within 24 hours of being exposed, and before the experiment ended or this request was made, which is more than the comparison reads: it says how much recorded material sits behind the variant.

ExperimentWrite.description: Experiment write payload. Identical to Experiment, plus the writable `feature_flag` config input.

allow_unknown_events.description: Suppresses the validation that rejects metrics referencing events not yet ingested by this project. REQUIRES explicit user confirmation before being set to true — never flip this silently to retry a failed call. The default validation catches typo'd event names and missing instrumentation. Set this to true only when the user has confirmed the event is intentional (e.g. they are about to instrument it).

archived.description: Whether the experiment is archived.

can_freeze_exposure.description: Whether enrollment can be frozen right now: the experiment must be running (not draft, paused, stopped, or already frozen) and its feature flag must have release conditions that a person cohort can narrow (no group aggregation, no holdout, no early access conditions).

conclusion.description:
Experiment conclusion: won, lost, inconclusive, stopped_early, or invalid.

* `won` - won
* `lost` - lost
* `inconclusive` - inconclusive
* `stopped_early` - stopped_early
* `invalid` - invalid

description.description: Description of the experiment hypothesis and expected outcomes.

excluded_variants.description: Variant keys to exclude from metric result calculations. Excluded variants are still served to users but omitted from statistical analysis. The baseline variant and holdout pseudo-variants cannot be excluded. Canonical home for what historically lived in `parameters.excluded_variants`.

exposure_criteria.description: Exposure configuration including filter test accounts and custom exposure events.

feature_flag.description: Feature-flag config for the experiment, in the flag's own filters shape. The linked flag is the source of truth for variants, rollout, aggregation, payloads, and experience continuity: send config here instead of the deprecated `parameters` keys. On a running experiment, also send `update_feature_flag_params=true`. Cannot be combined with the key of a pre-existing feature flag on create (the experiment links to it as-is).

feature_flag_key.description: Unique key for the experiment's feature flag. Letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores only. Search existing flags with the feature-flag-get-all tool first — reuse an existing flag when possible.

feature_flag_rule_id.description: The experiment rule that this experiment runs on, when its feature flag has rules. Null for every other experiment. Set it only on create, together with the feature_flag_key of an existing flag with rules. When that flag has one experiment rule, it can be left out. The experiment then counts exposures on the $experiment_exposure events of this rule, and never changes the flag.

flag_cleanup_task_id.description: ID of the Desktop task opened to remove the experiment's feature-flag code, when one was requested via open_cleanup_pr on end/ship_variant. Read its status via the flag_cleanup_task action.

health.description: Always null. Read the health findings from `GET /api/projects/{project_id}/experiments/{id}/health/`: problems in this experiment's configuration and its feature flag that keep it from producing trustworthy results, each with a fix.

holdout_id.description: ID of a holdout group to exclude from the experiment.

is_legacy.description: Whether the experiment uses any legacy-engine metrics (ExperimentTrendsQuery or ExperimentFunnelsQuery). Used to flag legacy experiments and gate actions that don't support them, such as duplicate and copy-to-project.

metrics.description: Primary experiment metrics. Each metric must have kind='ExperimentMetric' and a metric_type: 'mean' (set source to an EventsNode with an event name), 'funnel' (set series to an array of EventsNode steps), 'ratio' (set numerator and denominator EventsNode entries), 'quantile' (set source to an EventsNode or ActionsNode with math_property, the numeric property to measure, and quantile, the level in [0.01, 0.99], for example 0.9 for p90), or 'retention' (set start_event and completion_event; pass start_event {"kind": "ExperimentExposureNode"} to start retention from the experiment's exposure event). Use the read-data-schema tool with query kind 'events' to find available events in the project.

metrics_secondary.description: Secondary metrics for additional measurements. Same format as primary metrics.

name.description: Name of the experiment.

original_experiment.description: The experiment state as the client last read it, used together with `version` to resolve concurrent edits: metric collections merge per metric uuid, and any other field the update carries merges per field against its base value here (only a same-field double edit fails). Relevant keys are metrics, metrics_secondary, saved_metrics_ids, plus the last-read values of whichever scalar fields the update writes; unknown keys are ignored. Changed fields without a base value — and, without this object, any version mismatch — fail with HTTP 409.

parameters.description: Experiment parameters JSON. Supported keys include `custom_exposure_filter` and `variant_notes` (free-text notes per variant, keyed by variant key). Flag config (variants, rollout, aggregation, payloads, experience continuity) belongs on the `feature_flag` object; send it there. For backward compatibility, config still sent through these deprecated keys is copied onto the linked flag rather than rejected, and reads project the flag's current config back into this field. Excluded variants live on the top-level `excluded_variants` field, not here.

primary_metrics_ordered_uuids.description: Display order of the primary metrics, as metric uuids. This is a display hint only: a metric not in the list renders after the listed ones in stored order, and an entry that matches no metric is ignored. Send it only to reorder metrics. Adding or removing metrics does not need it.

repository.description: GitHub repository holding this experiment's feature-flag code, in `organization/repository` format. Used as the target of the flag-cleanup pull request opened via open_cleanup_pr on end/ship_variant. When not set, cleanup targets the team's only connected repository and is skipped if the team has several.

resolved_exposure_event.description: The event exposures are actually counted on when the experiment doesn't configure a custom one — `$feature_flag_called`, or `$experiment_exposure` once the team is in the rollout and the experiment started at or after the cutoff. Resolved server-side so clients display the same event the results queries read. For a draft, this is what the experiment would resolve to if launched now.

running_time_calculation.description: Running-time calculator state: `minimum_detectable_effect`, `recommended_running_time`, `recommended_sample_size`, and `exposure_estimate_config`. Canonical home for these keys, which historically lived in `parameters`.

saved_metrics_ids.description: IDs of shared saved metrics to attach to this experiment. Each item has 'id' (saved metric ID) and 'metadata' with 'type' (primary or secondary).

secondary_metrics_ordered_uuids.description: Display order of the secondary metrics, as metric uuids. This is a display hint only: a metric not in the list renders after the listed ones in stored order, and an entry that matches no metric is ignored. Send it only to reorder metrics. Adding or removing metrics does not need it.

status.description: Experiment lifecycle state: 'draft' (not yet launched), 'running' (launched with active feature flag), 'paused' (running with feature flag deactivated — virtual state derived from feature_flag.active, not stored), 'exposure_frozen' (running with enrollment frozen to the already-exposed cohort while metrics keep flowing — virtual state derived from the flag's release groups, not stored), 'stopped' (ended).

tags.description: Organizational tags for this experiment (up to 100, 255 characters each).

type.description:
Experiment type: web for frontend UI changes, product for backend/API changes.

* `web` - web
* `product` - product

update_feature_flag_params.description: When true, sync the flag config sent in this request (via the `feature_flag` object) to the linked feature flag. Draft experiments always sync regardless. On a running experiment, `feature_flag` config without this flag is rejected.

user_access_level.description: The effective access level the user has for this object

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency token. Reads return the experiment's current version, bumped on every update. Send the version you last read with an update to detect concurrent edits: a stale update merges concurrent changes where safe — metric collections per metric uuid, other fields per field — using the base values sent in `original_experiment`, and fails with HTTP 409 only when the same metric or field changed on both sides (or no base value was sent for a changed field). Omit to skip the check.

live.description: Whether tiles of this type self-update in real time after load. Live tiles show a fixed real-time window and cannot apply test-account filtering to the stream, so their config takes neither dateRange nor filterTestAccounts.
