ProjectProfile.description:
Wire shape for the project profile returned by `signals-scout-harness-project-profile-list`.

Read this once at the start of a run (after `skill-get`) to orient on the team. Cache
is per-team with a soft TTL (`PROFILE_TTL`). The internal scout token gets a fresh
profile, built on a stale cache or `force_refresh=true`. Other callers get the newest
stored profile, with `stale=true` when it is past `expires_at`.

`summary` leads the response and `payload` trails it: the inventory runs to tens of
kilobytes, so a client that truncates a long tool result would otherwise cut off the emit
gate the scout has to read before doing any work.

computed_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the profile was built.

expires_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp after which the profile is considered stale.

payload.description: Structured profile content. v1 has `inventory` only. Omitted when `summary_only=true`.

source_version.description: Schema version of the inventory builder. Bumps invalidate older cached rows.

stale.description: True when the profile is past `expires_at`. Only read-only callers get a stale profile. Read `computed_at` to see how old it is, and verify a detail live when its age matters.

summary.description: Compact envelope repeating the emit gate and the inbox report counts from `payload.inventory`. Declared first so it survives a truncated response.

ProjectProfileInventory.description:
The deterministic inventory layer of a project profile.

Read this to orient on the team's product mix, integrations, warehouse sources, signal
coverage, and existing inbox surface in one tool call. Distinct from `SignalScratchpad`:
profile is ground truth from authoritative tables; memory is agent inference.

emit_eligibility.description: Whether scout findings can actually reach the inbox for this team — the org-level AI data-processing consent gate and the `signals_scout` source toggle, plus a one-line remediation pointer. Read at cold start to quick-close before doing throwaway work.

existing_inbox_reports.description: Counts of reports already in the inbox, grouped by status.

integrations.description: Connected integrations (kind + connection time only — config never surfaced).

product_intents.description: Products the team signaled intent to use; useful for spotting stuck onboardings.

products_in_use.description: Product keys this team has completed onboarding for, sorted alphabetically.

project_context.description: Free-form orientation: human-set product description + registered app URLs.

recent_actions.description: Action orientation: total + the 5 most recently updated actions — useful to anchor agent reasoning about what the team treats as a meaningful interaction.

recent_activity.description: Per-scope counts off the activity log over the recent-activity window — cross-cutting orientation across every entity type (surveys, feature flags, experiments, dashboards, insights, cohorts, notebooks, actions, etc.). Each scope reports `edits` (total log entries), `users` (distinct user count), and `last_edit` (ISO-8601). Use to triage which scope a team has been working in lately before drilling down via the per-entity readers or `advanced-activity-logs-list`.

recent_alerts.description: Alert orientation: total + enabled count, plus the 5 most recently created alerts with their state and threshold metadata.

recent_cohorts.description: Cohort orientation: total + the 5 most recently created cohorts on the team.

recent_dashboards.description: Up to 20 dashboards on this team sorted by `last_accessed_at` desc — what the team is currently looking at, not necessarily the most-trafficked. We don't have per-dashboard view counts in Postgres, only the timestamp of the most recent access.

recent_experiments.description: Experiment orientation: total + running count, plus the 5 most recently updated experiments. The feature_flag_key on each row lets the scout correlate experiments with the `recent_feature_flags` section.

recent_feature_flags.description: Feature flag orientation: total + active count, plus the 5 most recently updated non-deleted flags with id, key, name, active, and updated_at.

recent_hog_flows.description: Hog flow orientation: total + non-archived count, plus the 5 most recently updated automation flows.

recent_hog_functions.description: Hog function orientation: total + enabled count, plus the 5 most recently updated destinations / transformations the team has wired up via the CDP pipelines.

recent_notebooks.description: Notebook orientation: total + the 5 most recently modified notebooks — useful signal for what the team has been investigating.

recent_reviewer_corrections.description: Recent human edits to report reviewer lists (before/after GitHub logins). The strongest ownership precedent available — check it before setting `suggested_reviewers` and fold what it shows into `reviewer:` memory keys.

recent_surveys.description: Surveys orientation: total + active count, plus the 5 most recently updated surveys with id, name, type, status (draft / running / stopped / archived), and updated_at.

scout_fleet.description: The other scouts configured on this project, split into enabled / disabled, each with its cadence, dry-run posture, last run, and last emit. Read it to see who else is watching this project before investigating a surface a sibling already covers.

signal_source_configs.description: Signal source configs split into enabled / disabled buckets.

top_events.description: Top ~50 events by count over a recent rolling window (each row carries `window_days`), with first/last seen timestamps within that window. These are WINDOWED counts, not lifetime totals: a capture gap can collapse a real, high-volume project's counts to near-zero here, so rule out an ingestion gap (compare against a trailing baseline via a direct `execute-sql`) before reading thinness as a genuinely low-volume project. `null` if the underlying ClickHouse query failed or timed out (distinct from `[]`, which means the team has no captures in the window). Use the gap between `first_seen_in_window` and `now` to spot new event types or recent bursts.

ProjectProfilePayload.description:
Top-level `payload` shape on a `SignalProjectProfile` row.

Carries `inventory` only.

inventory.description: Deterministic snapshot of what's true about the project.

ProjectProfileSummary.description:
The compact envelope returned ahead of the verbose `payload`.

Both sections are repeated from `payload.inventory`. They lead the response because a
client that truncates a long tool result keeps the prefix, and these are the two things a
scout has to know before it does anything: whether its output can reach the inbox at all,
and what is already there. Read `summary` rather than digging for the same keys inside
`payload.inventory`, because it is the same data and it is guaranteed to be in the part you
received.

emit_eligibility.description: The delivery gate: whether scout findings can reach the inbox for this team, with a one-line `remediation` when they cannot. Check `can_emit` before investigating anything, because when it is False every emit is silently dropped. Null only for a stored profile built before this section existed, which the caller should treat as unknown rather than as permission to emit.

existing_inbox_reports.description: Counts of reports already in the inbox, grouped by status, which is what a new finding would be deduped against. Null for a stored profile built before this section existed.

ai_credential.description: Value the AI gateway stamps as $ai_credential on generations made with this key, so gateway spend can be grouped by key. Derived from the key's hash, so it changes when the key is rolled.

scopes.description: Project-wide API scopes granted to this key. Project secret API keys do not honor object-level access controls, so a scope can access resources of that type even when per-resource RBAC would hide them from an individual user.

name.description: The counter's display name.

usage.description: The project's usage of the counter so far this billing period.

usage_key.description: The usage counter, as the usage series names it.

billing_period.description: The period the usage covers. Null when the organization has no billing period yet, and the usage then covers the current calendar month in UTC.

results.description: One entry per usage counter the project reported.

expires_at.description: When the quarantine lifts itself, as an ISO 8601 datetime. Through MCP an omitted or later expiry becomes 30 days from now; anywhere else omitting it means no expiry.

notify_owners.description: Post the quarantine to the Slack channel of the team that owns the story, naming the user who quarantined it. Only Storybook snapshots have an owning team. Best effort: skipped when the story has no owning team or the project has no Slack integration.

reason.description: Why this snapshot is being quarantined.

source_run_id.description: Optional pointer to the run whose failing snapshot prompted this quarantine — used to surface a 'view the failing run' link later.

QuarantineLifecycleEnum.description:
* `active` - Active
* `expiring_soon` - Expiring Soon
* `in_grace` - In Grace
* `overdue` - Overdue

detail.description: The latest verification outcome, in plain words.

expected_hash.description: Content hash a default-branch run must render, against a baseline entry with the same hash, for the lift to apply.

lifted_at_sha.description: Commit of the default-branch run that proved the fix and lifted the quarantine. A branch that does not contain it still treats the snapshot as quarantined.

merge_commit_sha.description: Merge commit of the pull request. Set when the lift applies.

pr_number.description: Pull request whose merge the lift waits for.

quarantine_id.description: UUID of the quarantine event this request lifts. A later quarantine of the same snapshot is a different event.

requested_by.description: User who requested the lift, or on whose behalf an agent did.

resolved_at.description: When the request left `pending`. Null while it waits.

run_type.description: Run type of the quarantine, for example storybook.

source.description: Who requested the lift: `human` for a person in the UI, `agent` for an agent through MCP.

source_run_id.description: Run the lift was requested from. Null after that run is deleted.

state.description:
`pending` waits for the merge and a matching default-branch run. `applied` lifted the quarantine. `cancelled` was withdrawn, or the pull request closed without merging into the run's branch. `superseded` means the quarantine ended some other way, or another request lifted it.

* `pending` - pending
* `applied` - applied
* `cancelled` - cancelled
* `superseded` - superseded

updated_at.description: When the request last changed.

expires.description: ISO date the quarantine expires (at most 30 days out). Defaults to 14 days from today. Ignored by remove.

issue.description: Existing tracking issue URL, carried forward on extend and remove. Ignored by quarantine, which files a fresh issue.

mode.description:
'run' (the test still executes but cannot fail the suite) or 'skip' (not run at all). Defaults to 'run'.

* `run` - Run
* `skip` - Skip

operation.description:
What to do: 'quarantine' (add or replace an entry and file a tracking issue), 'extend' (re-stamp an existing entry's expiry, reusing its issue), or 'remove' (delete the entry). All three open a pull request.

* `quarantine` - Quarantine
* `extend` - Extend
* `remove` - Remove

owner.description: GitHub team or user handle responsible for the fix, e.g. '@PostHog/team-x'. Required for quarantine and extend.

reason.description: Why the test is quarantined. Required for quarantine and extend; ignored by remove.

repo.description: Optional 'owner/name' repository override; defaults to the team's most active repo.

runner.description:
Test runner the selector targets: 'pytest', 'jest', or 'playwright'. Existing entries and Jest file extensions are inferred for older clients that omit it; other selectors default to 'pytest'.

* `pytest` - Pytest
* `jest` - Jest
* `playwright` - Playwright

selector.description: Test selector to act on: an exact test id, a file, a directory, a class prefix, or 'product:<dashed-name>'.

branch.description: Branch the pull request was opened from.

issue_url.description: URL of the tracking issue filed for a new quarantine; empty for extend and remove.

pr_url.description: URL of the opened pull request that edits the quarantine file.

lift_reason.description: Why visual review lifted this quarantine by itself, for example after 500 clean default-branch runs. Empty when a person, an agent, a merged fix, or the expiry ended it, and while it is active.

source_run.description: Run whose failing snapshot prompted this quarantine. Null when quarantine was created without run context.

name.description: Name of the query, preferably unique. For example web_analytics_vitals

presetId.description: Short id of the saved Web analytics filter preset this query was run under, if any.

productKey.description: Product responsible for this query. Use string, there's no need to churn the Schema when we add a new product *

scene.description: Scene where this query is shown in the UI. Use string, there's no need to churn the Schema when we add a new Scene *
scene.title: Scene

client_query_id.description: Client provided query ID. Can be used to retrieve the status or cancel the query.
client_query_id.title: Client Query Id

limit_context.description: Limit context for the query. Only 'posthog_ai' is allowed as a client-provided value.

name.description: Name given to a query. It's used to identify the query in the UI. Up to 128 characters for a name.
name.title: Name

query.description:
Submit a JSON string representing a query for PostHog data analysis, for example a HogQL query.

Example payload:

```

{"query": {"kind": "HogQLQuery", "query": "select * from events limit 100"}}

```

For more details on HogQL queries, see the [PostHog HogQL documentation](/docs/hogql#api-access).
query.title: Query

refresh.description:
Whether results should be calculated sync or async, and how much to rely on the cache:
- `'blocking'` - calculate synchronously (returning only when the query is done), UNLESS there are very fresh results in the cache
- `'async'` - kick off background calculation (returning immediately with a query status), UNLESS there are very fresh results in the cache
- `'lazy_async'` - kick off background calculation, UNLESS there are somewhat fresh results in the cache
- `'force_blocking'` - calculate synchronously, even if fresh results are already cached
- `'force_async'` - kick off background calculation, even if fresh results are already cached
- `'force_cache'` - return cached data or a cache miss; always completes immediately as it never calculates Background calculation can be tracked using the `query_status` response field.

assistant_prompt.description: The message the Fix with AI button sends to the assistant. Absent when no finding can be fixed in the query.
assistant_prompt.title: Assistant Prompt

findings.description: Every finding, fixable or not. Empty when the analysis found none.
findings.title: Findings

project_share.description: How much of all the project's events the query read, 0 to 1.
project_share.title: Project Share

range_share.description: How much of the project's events in the query's date range the query read, 0 to 1.
range_share.title: Range Share

analysis.description: The stored analysis, put on the response when it is served. Absent while the analysis runs, and when none was requested.

analysis_requested.description: True when the run asked for an analysis, or found one stored. While `analysis` is absent, poll `GET /query/scan/{cache_key}` for it.
analysis_requested.title: Analysis Requested

duration_ms.description: ClickHouse time for the last fresh run, summed over its ClickHouse queries.
duration_ms.title: Duration Ms

killed.description: True when ClickHouse stopped the run instead of finishing it.
killed.title: Killed

rows_read.description: Rows ClickHouse read for the last fresh run, all tables included.
rows_read.title: Rows Read

actionable.description: Whether the person can change the query so it reads less and still answers the same question. Surfaces show the full advice and "Fix with AI" only when a finding is actionable.
actionable.title: Actionable

by_design.description: True when the query reads this much on purpose, so reading less would change the answer. Absent means no.
by_design.title: By Design

cause.description: A label for what in the query text kept the read wide, such as `in_or`. Only analytics and the assistant read it, and the labels can change.
cause.title: Cause

evidence.description: The one fact the finding rests on.
evidence.title: Evidence

fix.description: What "Fix with AI" and the assistant are told to do.
fix.title: Fix

fix_location.description: Where the change goes. Absent means the query itself.

message.description: Shown to the person: what happened and what to do.
message.title: Message

cache_key.description: Cache key of the run that failed, so clients can ask for its query scan.
cache_key.title: Cache Key

complete.description: Whether the query is still running. Will be true if the query is complete, even if it errored. Either result or error will be set.
complete.title: Complete

end_time.description: When did the query execution task finish (whether successfully or not).
end_time.title: End Time

error.description: If the query failed, this will be set to true. More information can be found in the error_message field.
error.title: Error

error_code.description: Stable machine-readable code for the error, when known: the DRF exception code, the ClickHouse error name, the HogQL error code, or `unhandled_<exception class>` for a failure that no handler classified.
error_code.title: Error Code

pickup_time.description: When was the query execution task picked up by a worker.
pickup_time.title: Pickup Time

start_time.description: When was query execution task enqueued.
start_time.title: Start Time

k.description: Key. Shortened to 'k' to save on data.
k.title: K

t.description: Time in seconds. Shortened to 't' to save on data.
t.title: T

code_usage_billing_active.description: Whether the team's organization pays for PostHog Desktop usage: billing grants the `posthog_code_usage` product feature only on the Desktop usage product's paid plan, synced into the organization's available features. Consumers gate paid-tier Desktop behavior on this; an org unknown to billing reads as not paying. Always false for deactivated organizations.

limited.description: Per-resource limit state for every `QuotaResource` value, e.g. `ai_credits`, `posthog_code_credits`. Also carries the informational Desktop component resources (`posthog_code_token_credits`, `sandbox_compute_credits`, `sandbox_compute_cpu_millicore_seconds`, `sandbox_compute_memory_mib_seconds`) with usage in their native units, a null limit, and `limited` always false — they are never quota-enforced; only the combined `posthog_code_credits` is.

limit.description: The organization's limit for this resource in the same unit. Null when unlimited or unknown.

limited.description: True when the team is currently over its quota for this resource and limits are in effect. A deactivated organization additionally reads as limited on the two credit buckets `ai_credits` and `posthog_code_credits`, regardless of usage.

usage.description: Units of this resource the organization has used so far this billing period, in the resource's native unit (credits for credit buckets). Null when billing hasn't synced usage for the resource.

base_rate.description: The outcome's base rate: a report's lift is its probability divided by this value. Null when the served model has no saved base rate for the outcome.

cohort.description: Name of the report set the outcome was trained on. Null when the served model did not save it.

description.description: What the outcome predicts, in one sentence.

horizon_days.description: Days after scoring within which the outcome counts. Null when the served model did not save it.

label.description: Short label the inbox shows for the outcome.

outcome.description:
Name of the outcome in the `ranking` field's predictions.

* `open` - Open
* `action` - Action
* `fix` - Fix

readable.description: True when the training run could read the outcome's holdout AUC. Treat other outcomes with caution.

model.description: Key of the served model, as `<model_name>@<model_version>`, from the project's latest score.

outcomes.description: One entry per public outcome, in the inbox order.

status.description:
scored: the served model has scored reports in this project. unscored: no readable score yet. not_available: you cannot see the ranking model's output.

* `scored` - scored
* `unscored` - unscored
* `not_available` - not_available

limit.description: The audience limit with a rate limit of max_emails_per_hour. A slower rate allows fewer people.

max_days.description: The most days a rate-limited send may take to reach everyone.

max_emails_per_hour.description: The fastest email sending rate limit that raises the audience limit. A faster rate keeps the normal limit.

event_count.description: Number of events with this raw value in the window

raw_utm_source.description: A raw utm_source value matching no integration

suggested_integration.description: Integration suggested by token match, if any

bucket_start.description: Bucket start, aligned to ready_to_merge_series_granularity (top of hour, midnight, or Monday).

p50_seconds.description: Median per-PR ready_to_merge_seconds (merged_at minus the last observed ready-for-review transition) over PRs merged in this bucket, bots and drafts excluded. Null when nothing merged with an observed value (a gap, never zero).

before_first_approval_share.description: Share (0 to 1) of all ready-to-merge hours spent before the first approval, summed over the pull requests, so long pull requests weigh more.

first_approval_to_merge_seconds.description: Median seconds from the first approval to merge. The two approval medians do not add up to the ready-to-merge median.

merged_pr_count.description: Pull requests merged in the window, bots and drafts excluded.

ready_to_first_approval_seconds.description: Median seconds from ready to the first approval, over the pull requests with an approval. Null when nothing was measured.

ready_to_merge_seconds.description: Median seconds from the last ready_for_review to merge. Null when nothing was measured.

name.description: Name of the realtime cohort.

id.description: The realtime cohort the audience sends to.

name.description: The cohort's name.

percent_complete.description: How far the calculation has come, while the cohort is not ready.

state.description:
'ready' when the cohort's membership is calculated. 'building' or 'rebuilding' while it is still calculating, when a send waits for it. 'needs_attention' when its calculation is stuck.

* `ready` - Ready
* `building` - Building
* `rebuilding` - Rebuilding
* `needs_attention` - Needs attention

Where this project stands in joining the realtime cohorts beta. `serving`: the project has realtime cohorts. `setting_up`: a join is in progress. `available`: a POST to `join` starts one. `not_open`: this region takes no new projects. `refused`: the project cannot join by itself, and support can turn realtime cohorts on for it. `failed`: the last join did not finish, and a join an hour later tries again.

* `serving` - Serving
* `setting_up` - Setting up
* `available` - Available
* `not_open` - Not open
* `refused` - Refused
* `failed` - Failed

RealtimeCohortsJoinStateEnum.description:
* `serving` - Serving
* `setting_up` - Setting up
* `available` - Available
* `not_open` - Not open
* `refused` - Refused
* `failed` - Failed

ReasoningEffortEnum.description:
* `low` - low
* `medium` - medium
* `high` - high
* `xhigh` - xhigh
* `max` - max
* `ultracode` - ultracode

RecalculateMetricsRequest.description: Request body for triggering a metrics recalculation.

trigger.description:
What triggered this recalculation (manual is the default for user-initiated runs). Only client triggers are accepted; agent_mcp, timeseries_sync and scheduled are set by the server.

* `manual` - Manual
* `manual_retry` - Manual Retry
* `cold_run` - Cold Run
* `stale_refresh` - Stale Refresh
* `heal_latest_run` - Heal Latest Run
* `experiment_config_change` - Experiment Config Change
* `metric_config_change` - Metric Config Change

detail.description: Supporting sentence for the highlight.

title.description: Short headline for the highlight, e.g. 'Rising star page'.

value.description: The standout value, e.g. a page path or visitor count.

blurb.description: One-line explanation of why this persona was assigned this week.

color.description: Hex accent color for rendering the persona card.

id.description: Stable persona identifier. One of: just_getting_started, conversion_machine, traffic_magnet, crowd_favorite, search_hog, word_of_mouth, loyal_following, rising_star, steady_hog.

RecordCheckResultRequest.description: Request body for `scout-check-record-result`: the verdict on one dispatched report check.

check_id.description: The check this run was dispatched to answer, as given in the run note.

explanation.description: One or two sentences on what you looked at and what it showed. This is what a person reads on the report, so write it for them, with the numbers or entities you checked.

observed_value.description: The number you measured, when the check came down to one. Leave it out otherwise.

outcome.description:
`passed` when the evidence meets the check's stated bar and the expectation holds, `failed` when the evidence meets the bar and the expectation does not hold. `inconclusive` when your tools worked but the evidence cannot settle the question; give a `reason`. `errored` only when a tool, query, or model call failed. Reserve `failed` for a conclusion, not a suspicion.

* `passed` - Passed
* `failed` - Failed
* `errored` - Errored
* `inconclusive` - Inconclusive

reason.description:
Required with `inconclusive`, and refused with any other outcome. `awaiting_data`: the data can still arrive (a rollout lag, a soak not complete, too few samples so far). `unmeasurable`: the data the check needs is not captured. `needs_manual_verification`: only a person or another environment can verify it. `no_fix_to_measure`: nothing was changed to fix the claim, so no window after a fix exists. A report resolved without a pull request still has a window that starts when it resolved.

* `awaiting_data` - Awaiting Data
* `unmeasurable` - Unmeasurable
* `needs_manual_verification` - Needs Manual Verification
* `no_fix_to_measure` - No Fix To Measure

check_status.description: The check's status after the verdict. `active` means a recurring check re-armed for its next run; anything else is terminal.

outcome.description: The verdict that was recorded.

runs_remaining.description: Evaluations the check still owes after this one.

interaction_kind.description:
Which interaction counter to increment: 'data' (slicing/filtering the dashboard) or 'recording' (opening a session recording).

* `data` - data
* `recording` - recording

recorded.description: True once the interaction has been counted for the user.

RecordIteration.description: Input for recording one training iteration. Validated against the recipe allowlist.

agent_confidence.description: Agent's self-assessed confidence (0-1) that this iteration helps.

agent_description.description: Agent's plain-English rationale for this iteration. Max 2000 characters.

headline.description: A short title for people, at most 60 characters, on what this experiment tried. Use plain words, with no column names, SQL or model jargon. Longer text is cut, not rejected.

holdout_score.description: Held-out AUC for this iteration (0-1). Used to pick the champion at completion.

iteration_number.description: Zero-based index of this iteration within the run. Re-sending the same number updates that iteration (idempotent).

model_spec.description: model_class and model_params tried this iteration. Any class is accepted here; the sklearn/xgboost allowlist applies at completion, to a run that uploaded no bundle.

model_class.description: Dotted path of the estimator class.

model_params.description: Keyword arguments for the estimator's constructor; null or absent means the defaults.

parent_suggestion.description: UUID of the steering suggestion this iteration was spawned from, if any. Set it whenever the iteration acts on a pending suggestion — it links the iteration back to the suggestion for attribution and advances the suggestion to 'acted_on'.

recipe_snapshot.description: Compact recipe for this iteration: feature_sql (HogQL SELECT keyed on person_id) and transforms.

example.feature_sql: SELECT a.person_id AS distinct_id, countIf(e.event = '$pageview') AS pageviews FROM {anchors} a LEFT JOIN events e ON e.person_id = a.person_id AND e.timestamp < a.cutoff_ts GROUP BY a.person_id, a.cutoff_ts

feature_sql.description: A read-only HogQL SELECT from {anchors}, one row per person, keyed on person_id.

feature_transforms.description: Transforms the bundle applies to the feature columns; null or absent means none, and the in-process path accepts none.

status.description:
'kept' if this iteration improved on the best score, 'discarded' otherwise, 'crashed' on failure.

* `kept` - kept
* `discarded` - discarded
* `crashed` - crashed

summary.description: One plain sentence for people on what this experiment tried and what happened. Max 300 characters.

RecordStructuredOutputRequest.description: Request body for `scout-record-output`: a batch of schema-validated records.

records.description: Records to record, each validated against the scout config's `structured_output_schema`. All-or-nothing: if any record fails validation, nothing is written and the error names the failing records. Capped at 100 per call; batch per-entity judgments rather than calling once per record.

record_ids.description: Deterministic event ids of the recorded `$scout_structured_output` events, in submission order. Stable across a resubmission of the identical batch, which is what makes retrying a failed delivery safe.

recorded_count.description: How many records were recorded (all of them, or none).

recorded.description: True once today's visit row exists for the user.

complete.description: False when the scan could not read the whole workspace. Tools it did not find are then kept.

program.description: The wizard program that scanned, such as `posthog-integration` or `warehouse-source`.

scanned_at.description: When the wizard scanned the codebase.

session_id.description: The wizard run that made the scan.

tools.description: Every tool the scan found. An empty list is a scan that found nothing.

wizard_version.description: Version of the wizard that made the scan.

workspace_fingerprint.description: sha256 hex digest that identifies the scanned repository without naming it.

offset.description: The finding's time in the recording, as MM:SS.

seek_seconds.description: Where the player starts, in seconds from the recording start. Null without an offset.

session_id.description: The recording's session id.

start_at.description: Where the player starts, a few seconds before the finding.

after.description: Cursor for pagination. Contains the ordering value and session_id from the last record of the previous page.
after.title: After

event_match_scope.description: Where a filter that is evaluated against events must match. 'session' (default) matches an event anywhere in the session, including before the recording started or after it ended. 'recording' only matches events from one minute before the recording starts until one minute after it ends. This applies to every filter the events table answers: events, actions, event properties, and, when the project resolves them on events, person, group, and cohort properties.

experiment_exposure.description: Only sessions of persons exposed to this experiment, each ending at or after the person's first exposure as the experiment's exposure criteria count it. Resolved server-side from the experiment, so it links sessions even when the exposure events themselves carry no session id (e.g. server-side SDKs). Composes with the query's date range like any other filter, so set date_from to the experiment's start (or earlier) to cover the full run: the default window only reaches back a few days.

hide_viewed_recordings.description: Exclude recordings already viewed by the current user ('current-user'), by any team member ('any-user'), or none (default). Applied server-side so pagination and the result cursor operate on the filtered set.

modifiers.description: Modifiers used when performing the query

order_direction.description: Replay originally had all ordering as descending by specifying the field name, this runs counter to Django behavior where the field name specifies ascending sorting (e.g. the_field_name) and -the_field_name would indicate descending order to avoid invalidating or migrating all existing filters we keep DESC as the default or allow specification of an explicit order direction here

session_recording_id.description: If provided, this recording will be fetched and prepended to the results, even if it doesn't match the filters
session_recording_id.title: Session Recording Id

version.description: version of the node, used for schema migrations
version.title: Version

experiment_id.description: Experiment whose exposed persons' sessions to show. Must belong to the environment the query runs in.
experiment_id.title: Experiment Id

in_session.description: Only sessions carrying in-session exposure evidence: an event matching the experiment's exposure criteria inside the session (with the stamped `$feature/<flag_key>` property standing in when the exposure event was never captured with a session id). Defaults to all exposed persons' sessions from first exposure onward.
in_session.title: In Session

variant.description: Narrow to persons exposed to this variant. Defaults to all of the experiment's variants.
variant.title: Variant

variants.description: Narrow to persons exposed to any of these variants. Defaults to all of the experiment's variants. Do not combine with `variant`, the single-variant form that predates this field.
variants.title: Variants

error.description: Query error. Returned only if 'explain' or `modifiers.debug` is true. Throws an error otherwise.
error.title: Error

modifiers.description: Modifiers used when performing the query

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page. Contains the ordering value and session_id from the last record.
next_cursor.title: Next Cursor

query_status.description: Query status indicates whether next to the provided data, a query is still running.

resolved_compare_date_range.description: The resolved previous/comparison period date range, when comparing against another period

resolved_date_range.description: The date range used for the query

timings.description: Measured timings for different parts of the query generation process
timings.title: Timings

used_data_warehouse_sources.description: Connector-synced data warehouse sources referenced by this query, if any.
used_data_warehouse_sources.title: Used Data Warehouse Sources

warehouse_suggestions.description: Open warehouse suggestions about views this query read. Set only on fresh runs for agent callers; absent when not evaluated, empty when evaluated and none apply.
warehouse_suggestions.title: Warehouse Suggestions

warnings.description: Warnings about data warehouse sources referenced by the query whose latest sync failed, is paused, hit a billing limit, or is otherwise stale. Results may not reflect current source data. Accumulated across every HogQL execution that contributes to this response — so insights backed by warehouse tables (Trends, Funnels, etc.) receive the same warnings as raw HogQL queries. Also carries access control warnings when a system-table query filters out objects the user can't access, and a breakdown warning when the query ran without its requested breakdown.
warnings.title: Warnings

rejection_reason.description: Why the proposal is rejected. Persisted so it is never re-proposed.

RelayedMcpServer.description: One desktop-only MCP server relayed into the run — a name only, never configuration.

broadcasts.description: ID, name and status of each linked broadcast the caller can see. Deleted broadcasts are left out.

has_hidden_flags.description: True when the release links flags the caller cannot see. Their IDs are left out of feature_flag_ids.

insights.description: ID, short ID, name and dates of each linked insight the caller can see, including deleted ones.

metric_goals.description: Target for each metric that has one. Metrics without a goal are left out.

metric_insight_ids.description: IDs of the insights that are the release's metrics. The first is the primary metric.

surveys.description: ID, name, dates, targeting flag and archived state of each linked survey the caller can see.

ReleaseGoalDirectionEnum.description:
* `at_least` - At least the target
* `at_most` - At most the target

name.description: Name of the release.

matched_terms.description: Words the flag shares with the release's name, description or linked flags.

name.description: Name of the release.

content.description: Markdown to write. Future prompts read it verbatim and people read it directly, so structured Markdown (headings, bullets, inline code for ids) is easier to skim than a wall of prose.

expires_at.description: Optional ISO-8601 expiry for a memory that's only true for a while (a cooldown, a window you're watching). After this time the entry drops out of searches, so you don't have to come back and forget it. Omit for a durable memory — every write sets the whole entry, so omitting it on a later write clears an expiry set earlier. Best-effort — a value that can't be parsed or is already in the past is dropped (the memory stays durable), not rejected, so the memory write is never lost.

key.description: Short stable ID for what you're tracking, e.g. `noise:<fingerprint>`; max 300 chars, the note goes in `content`. Unique per team; re-using a key overwrites the entry. Never embed a date, timestamp, or run id (that mints a new row every run). For run state, use one fixed key and keep the timestamp in `content`.

run_id.description: Run that authored this memory; persisted as `created_by_run_id` for lineage. Best-effort — a `run_id` that is unparseable, or that isn't a run on this project, is dropped rather than rejected, so the memory write is never lost. Omit it and the lineage still lands: a write from a scout sandbox is attributed to that sandbox's own run. A report-pipeline caller is attributed by its stage and does not pass one.

cron_expression.description: For a recurring reminder: a 5-field cron expression (e.g. '0 9 * * 1' = Mondays 9am). May fire at most 4 times per day. Mutually exclusive with recurrence_interval.

end_date.description: Optional: recurring reminders stop (status=completed) after this time.

message.description: Optional longer body for the notification.

organization.description: ID of the organization this reminder belongs to. You must be a member of it.

recurrence_interval.description:
For a recurring reminder: daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly.

* `daily` - Daily
* `weekly` - Weekly
* `monthly` - Monthly
* `yearly` - Yearly

resource_id.description: ID of the referenced resource; must exist in the chosen project.

resource_type.description: Optional PostHog resource this reminder is about. One of: dashboard, insight, experiment, feature_flag, survey, notebook, replay, error_tracking. Resources are project-scoped, so a team must be set when this is provided.

scheduled_at.description: For a one-off reminder: when it should fire (ISO 8601, future).

team.description: Optional ID of the project this reminder is scoped to. Required when targeting a specific resource. Must belong to the chosen organization.

timezone.description: IANA timezone the schedule resolves in (e.g. 'America/New_York'). Defaults to the project timezone when a team is set, otherwise UTC.

title.description: Short text shown as the notification title when the reminder fires.

category_key.description: Optional message category key. If omitted, the recipient is opted back in to all marketing messages.

identifier.description: The recipient identifier to opt back in (e.g. email address).

confirm_complaints.description: Set to true to remove addresses that are suppressed because the recipient reported a message as spam. Mailing them again can hurt your sender reputation. Without it, a request that includes one removes nothing and returns 400.

layout.description:
How to size tiles when reordering. 'preserve' (default) keeps each tile's existing width and height and only repacks positions in the new order. Use the other modes only when every tile should use the same size: 'two_column' makes every tile 6-wide × 5-tall, 'three_column' makes every tile 4-wide × 5-tall, and 'full_width' makes every tile 12-wide × 5-tall.

* `preserve` - preserve
* `two_column` - two_column
* `three_column` - three_column
* `full_width` - full_width

tile_order.description: Array of tile IDs in the desired display order (top to bottom, left to right).

backfill_id.description: Backfill that dispatched this observation; null for live, on-demand, and retry triggers.

distinct_id.description: Distinct id of the person in the recorded session (the subject being watched); null if unknown.

error_reason.description: Populated on terminal non-success statuses; formatted as `kind:human-readable message`. For `ineligible`, kind is one of no_recording / too_short / too_inactive / too_long / no_events / no_snapshots / too_large / not_exposed / experiment_unresolved. For `failed`, kind is one of provider_transient / provider_rejected / rasterization_failed / validation_failed / infra_transient / internal_error / orphaned / pii_detected.

label.description: The team's shared label on this observation (correct/incorrect + feedback), or null if unlabeled.

media.description: Frames illustrating this observation, in order. Empty until the media render finishes.

next_observation_id.description: Id of the following sibling observation for the same scanner (prev/next nav), honoring any list filters and ordering passed to retrieve; only set on retrieve, null at the end of the set.

previous_observation_id.description: Id of the preceding sibling observation for the same scanner (prev/next nav), honoring any list filters and ordering passed to retrieve; only set on retrieve, null at the start of the set.

prompt_question.description: The scanner's prompt condensed into the one question it answers about a session. Null when the prompt has changed since this observation was scanned, since the question then describes a different prompt; read `scanner_snapshot.scanner_config.prompt` instead.

prompt_valence.description: For a monitor or scorer: `good` when a yes or a high score is good news for the team, `bad` when it is a problem, `neutral` when neither. Judged by AI from the prompt. Null for other scanner types, when not judged, or when the prompt has changed since this observation was scanned.

recording_subject_email.description: Email of the person in the recorded session (the subject being watched, not the user who triggered the observation), captured at scan time. Null when the session had no identified person.

scanner_id.description: The scanner that produced this observation.

scanner_origin.description:
Where the producing scanner came from. `configured` scanners are saved, named, and have a detail page; `inline` ones are throwaways minted for a one-off scan and are not addressable, so callers must not link to them.

* `configured` - Configured
* `inline` - Inline

scanner_result.description: Result data persisted on success; null until the observation succeeds.

scanner_snapshot.description: Frozen view of the scanner at run time; scanner edits do not retroactively mutate this observation.

session_id.description: Session recording id this scanner was applied to.

status.description:
Observation status (pending, running, succeeded, failed, ineligible).

* `pending` - Pending
* `running` - Running
* `succeeded` - Succeeded
* `failed` - Failed
* `ineligible` - Ineligible

summary_line.description: One line of plain text saying what the scanner found: its verdict, score, tags or title, then its own words, with markdown flattened and the text truncated. An observation that produced no result carries the reason instead, and one still in flight carries an empty string. Read this in place of `scanner_result` when you scan a list of observations.

triggered_by.description:
Whether this observation came from the schedule, an on-demand request, a retry of a failed or ineligible observation, or a historical backfill.

* `schedule` - Schedule
* `on_demand` - On demand
* `retry` - Retry
* `backfill` - Backfill

triggered_by_user.description: User who triggered an on-demand observation; null for scheduled observations.

viewed.description: Whether the calling user has opened this observation.

workflow_id.description: Temporal workflow id for progress queries and debugging. Empty until the workflow starts.

ReplayObservationLabel.description: The team's shared judgement on whether the scanner scored this session correctly.

feedback.description: Optional written context on the rating, for thumbs-up and thumbs-down alike: what the scanner got right or wrong, or what it should have concluded.

is_correct.description: True if the scanner scored this session correctly, false if not.

asset_id.description: Export asset holding the bytes; fetch it from the export content endpoint.

kind.description:
`thumbnail` for the single frame that illustrates the observation, `chapter` for the frame of one summary chapter.

* `thumbnail` - Thumbnail
* `chapter` - Chapter

position.description: Order among media of the same kind. For a `chapter` frame, the index into `model_output.chapters`.

video_start_ms.description: Where this media starts in the analysis video, in milliseconds.

ReplayScanner.description: A Replay Vision scanner: its type, targeting query, and AI configuration.

created_by.description: User who created the scanner.

creation_method.description:
How the creator built this scanner: from an AI draft, from a template, or from scratch. Reported to product analytics at creation and not stored on the scanner. Independent of any experiment the creator is in, since a person offered the AI flow can still fill the form by hand. Only the app can answer this, so a request from anywhere else reports the calling surface instead of whatever it sends here. Ignored on update.

* `ai` - AI draft
* `template` - Template
* `scratch` - From scratch

credit_limit.description: Optional cap on this scanner's own credit spend per billing period. Null means no scanner-level cap. When reached, this scanner stops scanning until the period resets. It stays enabled and does not scan the sessions it skipped.

credits_per_observation.description: Credits one observation by this scanner costs (1 credit = $0.01), derived from `model`.

credits_this_month.description: Credits billed for this scanner's observations created in the current billing period (1 credit = $0.01), each at the price frozen when it succeeded. Deleted observations still count.

credits_used_against_limit.description: Credits counted against `credit_limit` for the current billing period: settled receipts plus in-flight observations, priced from their frozen snapshot model. This is what the limit gate measures, so it includes work still in progress. It is not the same as `credits_this_month`, which counts only succeeded observations. For a `free_only` scanner bound by the organization's free credits, this is the organization's usage, not the scanner's own.

dashboard_id.description: Dashboard created for this scanner with the create_dashboard action. Null when none was created or the user deleted it.

dashboard_suggested.description: Whether to offer the user a dashboard for this scanner: true when the scanner has no dashboard and at least 20 succeeded observations to chart. Offer it once and do not repeat the offer if the user declines.

description.description: Free-form description shown in the scanner management UI.

disabled_reason.description:
Why the scanner is off, or null when it is on or was created off. `manual`: a person turned it off. `free_credits_used`: a `free_only` scanner stopped when the free credits ran out. `no_ai_consent`: the organization has not approved AI data processing. `creator_lost_access`: the creator can no longer view recordings, which the sweep reads as them, so turning the scanner on requires `take_over_as_creator`. `experiment_deleted`: its experiment was deleted.

* `manual` - Turned off by a person
* `free_credits_used` - Free credits used
* `no_ai_consent` - No AI consent
* `creator_lost_access` - Creator lost access
* `experiment_deleted` - Experiment deleted

emits_signals.description: When true, the prompt is augmented with the Signal side mission and the scanner emits PostHog Signals.

enabled.description: When false, the reconciler removes the scanner's Temporal schedule. On-demand triggers still work.

entry_point.description: The app surface the creator started from, such as `replay_filters`. Reported to product analytics at creation so a scanner can be attributed to its entry point, and not stored on the scanner. Only the app's value is kept: any other caller is reported as its own source, such as `mcp`. Ignored on update.

estimated_at.description: When `estimated_monthly_observations` was last computed. Null means the estimate is being recomputed after a config change or has never run, so the stored number may be stale.

estimated_monthly_credits.description: `estimated_monthly_observations` priced at `credits_per_observation`, capped at `credit_limit` when one is set. Null until the estimate is first computed.

estimated_monthly_observations.description: Latest projected observations/month for this scanner. Null until first computed.

experiment_targeting.description: The experiment this scanner's targeting watches, if any. Set null when the experiment targeting is removed.

filter_error.description: Why the scanner's recording filter cannot run, from the last sweep or estimate that tried it. Cleared when the filter changes or a sweep runs it.

free_only.description: Run only while the organization has free credits left this billing period, so the scanner never adds spend. When they run out it turns off with `disabled_reason` `free_credits_used`.

goal.description: The goal an AI draft was built from, in the creator's own words, so the scanner keeps what it was meant to find. Set on create only and ignored on update.

last_swept_at.description: Watermark for the scanner's last scheduled fire. Mirrors Temporal schedule state for recovery.

limit_from_free_credits.description: True when the organization's free credits bind this `free_only` scanner rather than its own `credit_limit`. `credits_used_against_limit` is then the organization's usage, measured against its free credits.

limit_reached.description: Whether this scanner has stopped because of its own credit limit, or, for a `free_only` scanner, because the organization has used its free credits. True when the budget left cannot cover one more observation, which is the same test the scanner's enforcement gates apply. Always false when no limit is set and `free_only` is false.

model.description:
Concrete model to use for this scanner.

* `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` - Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite
* `gemini-3-flash-preview` - Gemini 3 Flash
* `gemini-3.8-flash` - Gemini 3.8 Flash

name.description: Human-readable scanner name. Unique within the team.

observations_this_month.description: Billed observations this scanner created in the current billing period, including deleted ones.

prompt_question.description: The current prompt condensed by AI into the one question the scanner answers about a session. Falls back to the prompt's first line when no question matches the current prompt.

provider.description:
LLM provider. v1 is Google-only.

* `google` - Google

query.description: Persisted `RecordingsQuery` shape used to pick candidate sessions. `date_from`/`date_to` are stripped on save — the schedule controls time, not the user.

sampling_rate.description: 0..1 random downsample applied after the query matches. Defaults to 1.0 (no downsampling). Use exactly 0 to pause scanning; non-zero rates below 0.0001 (0.01%) are rejected as below the sampling precision.

scanner_config.description: Type-specific configuration. All scanner types require `prompt`; monitors add optional `allow_inconclusive`, classifiers add `tags`, scorers add `scale`, summarizers add optional `length`.

scanner_type.description:
What the scanner does: monitor, classifier, scorer, or summarizer.

* `monitor` - Monitor
* `classifier` - Classifier
* `scorer` - Scorer
* `summarizer` - Summarizer
* `experiment` - Experiment

scanner_version.description: Increments on every config-changing save. Observations snapshot this value.

sweep_interval_minutes.description: How often, in minutes, the scheduled sweep checks this scanner for new recordings. Null when the scanner is off or its sweep is paused because it cannot scan. Scanners that rarely find recordings, or read a lot of data, are checked less often. Scanners created or edited in the last day, or with an enabled alert, are checked as often as their read budget allows.

sweep_throttle_factor.description: How much the scheduled sweep is slowed to keep this scanner inside its daily ClickHouse read budget. 1 means it checks for new recordings on the normal schedule; N means it checks once every N schedule intervals. Expensive filters raise it.

tags.description: Organizational tags for this scanner. Distinct from a classifier's categories in scanner_config. Tags cannot contain commas.

take_over_as_creator.description: Set with `enabled: true` to turn on a scanner whose creator can no longer view recordings. The caller becomes the scanner's creator, and scheduled scans then run as the caller. Without it, that request fails with code `scanner_creator_lost_access`.

user_access_level.description: The effective access level the user has for this object

credits_per_observation.description: Per-observation credit price frozen at creation from the snapshot model.

failed_count.description: Observations from this backfill that failed.

finished_at.description: When the backfill reached a terminal status (completed or cancelled).

in_flight_count.description: Observations from this backfill still pending or running.

ineligible_count.description: Sessions that turned out ineligible (too short, expired recording, ...).

skipped_count.description: Candidates the walk stepped over because this scanner had already tried them. Counted at creation but never dispatched, so progress and remaining spend both have to account for them.

succeeded_count.description: Observations from this backfill that succeeded.

total_count.description: Unobserved candidates enumerated at creation; the ceiling is total_count x credits_per_observation.

window_end.description: Exclusive upper bound of the window; clamped to now at creation.

window_start.description: Inclusive lower bound of the historical window to scan.

ReplayVisionError.description: The shape every Replay Vision error response uses, so generated clients read one key.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation of why the request was refused.

billable_minutes.description: Billable (self-hosted) job minutes in the window; null when the job-level source isn't synced.

billable_minutes_prev.description: Billable minutes over the previous window; null when the job-level source isn't synced.

cost_per_merge_usd.description: estimated_cost_usd divided by merged_pr_count: the window's CI cost per merged PR. Null when the job-level source isn't synced or nothing merged.

cost_per_merge_usd_prev.description: The same ratio over the previous window. Null when the job-level source isn't synced or nothing merged.

cost_series.description: CI cost per merged PR across the window, oldest first, zero-filled, bucketed by cost_series_granularity. Empty when the job-level source isn't synced or include_series=false.

cost_series_granularity.description: Bucket width of the cost_series trend, chosen to fit the window: 'hour', 'day', or 'week'.

default_branch.description: 'master' or 'main', picked by observed run volume in the window.

delivery_pipeline.description: Where a change's wall-clock time goes on the way to production, over PRs merged in the window with bots and drafts excluded.

depot_ci_billable_minutes.description: Slice of billable_minutes from jobs that ran on the Depot CI engine; null when the job-level source isn't synced.

depot_ci_billable_minutes_prev.description: Depot CI billable minutes over the previous window; null when the job-level source isn't synced.

estimated_cost_usd.description: Estimated CI cost in USD (billable minutes x runner-tier rate); null when the job-level source isn't synced.

estimated_cost_usd_prev.description: Estimated cost over the previous window; null when the job-level source isn't synced.

jobs_available.description: Whether the job-level source is synced (cost and queue figures exist).

median_open_to_merge_seconds.description: Median merged_at - created_at over PRs merged in the window, bots and drafts excluded. Coarse by design: draft and ready-for-review time are fused. Null when nothing merged.

median_open_to_merge_seconds_prev.description: The same median over the previous window. Null when nothing merged.

median_ready_to_merge_seconds.description: Median per-PR ready_to_merge_seconds (the true cycle time: merged_at minus the last observed ready-for-review transition) over PRs merged in the window, bots and drafts excluded. Null when the issue-events table isn't synced or no merged PR has an observed value; fall back to median_open_to_merge_seconds and label it open-to-merge.

median_ready_to_merge_seconds_prev.description: The same median over the previous window. Null when not observed.

median_time_to_green_seconds.description: Median wall clock for a PR push round to settle fully green over the window: the window-level twin of time_to_green_series, same population and exclusions. Null when no fully green rounds.

median_time_to_green_seconds_prev.description: The same median over the previous window. Null when no fully green rounds.

merge_queue_avg_attempts_per_merge.description: Mean distinct gate attempts (distinct gate branches, flake-bisection branches collapsed) per queue-landed merge. Null when no queue-landed merges.

merge_queue_avg_attempts_per_merge_prev.description: The same mean over the previous window. Null when no queue-landed merges.

merge_queue_billable_minutes.description: Slice of billable_minutes spent on merge-queue batch branches (trunk-merge/**); null when the job-level source isn't synced.

merge_queue_billable_minutes_prev.description: Merge-queue billable minutes over the previous window; null when the job-level source isn't synced.

merge_queue_failed_gate_merge_share.description: Fraction (0-1) of queue-landed merges with at least one failed gate run before merging. Derived from CI run conclusions, not the queue's own eviction records. Null when no queue-landed merges.

merge_queue_failed_gate_merge_share_prev.description: The same fraction over the previous window. Null when no queue-landed merges.

merge_queue_failed_or_cancelled_share.description: Fraction (0-1) of concluded queue entries (merged, failed, or cancelled) that ended failed or cancelled, from the queue's own records. Windowed on each entry's last state change. Null when the Trunk source isn't synced or nothing concluded.

merge_queue_failed_or_cancelled_share_pr.description: The same fraction over the previous window. Null when the Trunk source isn't synced or nothing concluded.

merge_queue_median_first_gate_to_merge_s.description: Median seconds from a PR's first observed merge-queue gate run starting to the PR merging. Pending time before gate testing starts is not included. Null when no queue-landed merges.
The same median over the previous window. Null when no queue-landed merges.

merge_queue_merged_pr_count.description: PRs merged in the window with at least one corroborated merge-queue gate run: the population behind every merge_queue_* landing stat. All authors, bots included.

merge_queue_merged_pr_count_prev.description: Queue-landed merges over the previous window.

merge_queue_multi_attempt_merge_share.description: Fraction (0-1) of queue-landed merges that needed more than one gate attempt. Null when no queue-landed merges.

merge_queue_multi_attempt_merge_share_pr.description: The same fraction over the previous window. Null when no queue-landed merges.

merge_queue_p90_first_gate_to_merge_seco.description: p90 of the same first-gate-run-to-merge measure: the tail, where queue pain concentrates. Null when no queue-landed merges.
The same p90 over the previous window. Null when no queue-landed merges.

merge_queue_p95_first_gate_to_merge_seco.description: p95 of the same first-gate-run-to-merge measure. Null when no queue-landed merges.
The same p95 over the previous window. Null when no queue-landed merges.

merge_queue_p99_first_gate_to_merge_seco.description: p99 of the same first-gate-run-to-merge measure. Null when no queue-landed merges.
The same p99 over the previous window. Null when no queue-landed merges.

merge_queue_skip_the_line_count.description: Queue entries flagged skip-the-line (prioritized past the queue order) in the window, whatever state they reached. Null when the Trunk source isn't synced.

merge_queue_skip_the_line_count_prev.description: Skip-the-line entries over the previous window. Null when the Trunk source isn't synced.

merge_queue_trunk_available.description: Whether the team's TrunkIo warehouse source has the opt-in merge-queue endpoint synced and readable by the requesting user. When false, every merge_queue_failed_or_cancelled_* and merge_queue_skip_the_line_* field is null; fall back to merge_queue_failed_gate_merge_share.

merged_pr_count.description: PRs merged in the window, all authors and bots included. billable_minutes and estimated_cost_usd cover every run in the window, including default-branch and unmerged PR runs, so dividing them by this count spreads all CI spend over the merges.

merged_pr_count_prev.description: Merged-PR count over the previous window.

open_to_merge_series.description: Median time-to-merge (p50 open_to_merge_seconds, bots/drafts excluded) per bucket across the window, oldest first, bucketed by open_to_merge_series_granularity. Empty buckets carry null; the whole series is empty when include_series=false.

open_to_merge_series_granularity.description: Bucket width of the open_to_merge_series trend: 'hour', 'day', or 'week'.

ready_to_merge_series.description: Median cycle time (p50 per-PR ready_to_merge_seconds, bots/drafts excluded) per bucket across the window, oldest first, bucketed by ready_to_merge_series_granularity. Empty buckets carry null; the whole series is empty when the issue-events table isn't synced or include_series=false, so fall back to open_to_merge_series.

ready_to_merge_series_granularity.description: Bucket width of the ready_to_merge_series trend: 'hour', 'day', or 'week'.

rerun_cycles.description: Runs in the window that were a 2nd+ attempt (attempt > 1).

rerun_cycles_prev.description: Re-run cycles over the previous window.

revert_share.description: reverting_pr_count divided by merged_pr_count: the share of merges that undid an earlier merge. The guardrail to watch when review requirements are loosened. Null when nothing merged.

revert_share_prev.description: The same share over the previous window. Null when nothing merged.

revert_share_series.description: Reverting merges over all merges (all authors, bots included) per bucket across the window, oldest first, zero-filled, bucketed by revert_share_series_granularity. Empty buckets carry a null share; the whole series is empty when include_series=false.

revert_share_series_granularity.description: Bucket width of the revert_share_series trend: 'hour', 'day', or 'week'.

reverting_pr_count.description: PRs merged in the window whose title names a revert: GitHub's 'Revert "..."' or a conventional-commit 'revert: ...' / 'revert(scope): ...' title. Counts the revert when it merges, not the change it undid, which may have merged in an earlier window. Same population as merged_pr_count.

reverting_pr_count_prev.description: Reverting-PR count over the previous window.

run_count.description: Workflow runs started in the window, all branches and workflows.

run_count_prev.description: Same count over the equal-length window immediately before date_from: the delta baseline.

success_rate.description: Fraction of conclusive runs that succeeded (0-1) in the window. Skipped, cancelled, neutral, and action_required runs are excluded. Null if no run reached a verdict.

success_rate_prev.description: Conclusive-run success rate over the previous window. Null if no run reached a verdict.

success_rate_series.description: CI pass rate (conclusive runs that succeeded, all branches) per bucket across the window, oldest first, bucketed by success_rate_series_granularity. Skipped, cancelled, neutral, and action_required runs are excluded. Empty buckets carry null; the whole series is empty when include_series=false.

success_rate_series_granularity.description: Bucket width of the success_rate_series trend: 'hour', 'day', or 'week'.

time_to_green_series.description: Median time-to-green (p50 wall clock for a PR push round to settle fully green) per bucket across the window, oldest first, bucketed by time_to_green_series_granularity. Empty buckets carry null; the whole series is empty when include_series=false.

time_to_green_series_granularity.description: Bucket width of the time_to_green_series trend: 'hour', 'day', or 'week'.

name.description: Repository name.

owner.description: Repository owner or organization.

provider.description: Code host provider, e.g. 'github'.

created_by.description: Who created the rule, from the UI or the Slack commands. Null when that user was deleted.

repository.description: Target repository as owner/repo, e.g. 'posthog/posthog.com'.

rule_text.description: Plain-text description of the requests that should route to the repository, e.g. 'anything about the internal dashboard'. At most 300 characters.

reason.description: The reason stored with the value by whoever set it. Null when none was stored.

set_at.description: When the current value was set.

value.description: `immediately_actionable`, `requires_human_input`, or `not_actionable`: whether the report can be acted on now, needs a person's input first, or needs no action.

reason.description: The reason stored with the value by whoever set it. Null when none was stored.

set_at.description: When the current value was set.

value.description: Whether the issue is already fixed, or has a fix in flight that someone else is working on.

ReportChart.description: One chart attached to a report — rendered in the inbox and referenceable from the summary.

caption.description: Optional one-line note on what to look at in the chart.

chart_id.description: Stable slug for this chart within the report (lowercase letters, numbers, underscores, hyphens; must start with a letter or number). Reference it from `summary` as a markdown link with a `chart:` target — `[Daily signups](chart:signups-drop)` — to place the chart at that point in the body. A chart you don't reference still renders, below the summary.

query.description: The query node to render. `kind` must be `InsightVizNode` (an ad-hoc product analytics chart), `DataVisualizationNode` (a SQL series — a `HogQLQuery` source plus a `display`), or `SavedInsightNode` (an existing insight by `shortId`). Pin the window to absolute dates where the node supports it, so the reader sees the data you wrote about rather than whatever a relative range resolves to when they open the report.

size.description:
How much height the chart gets: `small` for a single number or a short series, `medium` for an ordinary graph, `large` when there are rows or a grid to read (retention, paths, a wide breakdown). Leave it out unless the default looks wrong — the inbox sizes a chart from its query, and two charts referenced from the same paragraph sit side by side.

* `small` - small
* `medium` - medium
* `large` - large

title.description: Short heading shown above the chart.

agent.description: External agent client name when kind is `agent`, otherwise null.

kind.description:
Who set the value. `user`: a person in PostHog. `agent`: a person's external coding agent. `task`: a PostHog agent task, such as report research. `system`: the pipeline, or an older row with no recorded attribution.

* `user` - User
* `task` - Task
* `agent` - Agent
* `system` - System

task_id.description: PostHog task that set the value when kind is `task`.

user.description: The person who set the value, or whose external agent did. Null for task and system writes.

actionability.description: From the latest actionability_judgment artefact. Null when there is none.

already_addressed.description: From the latest actionability_judgment artefact, so it shares the reason and the setter with actionability. Null when there is none.

priority.description: From the latest priority_judgment artefact. Null when there is none.

repository.description: From the latest repo_selection artefact. Null when there is none.

ReportEvidence.description: One observation backing an authored report — becomes a bound signal row on the report.

description.description: Prose for this observation. Embedded and rendered to the safety/research surfaces.

source_id.description: Stable id for this observation within the report (lets a later edit address it).

impact.description: The clauses that state the problem or its cause in the impact sentence.

lead.description: The clauses that state the problem or its cause in the lead.

proposal.description: The clause that states the fix in the proposal.

ReportLinkKindEnum.description:
* `depends_on` - Depends on
* `part_of` - Part of
* `follow_up_of` - Follow-up of
* `duplicate_of` - Duplicate of
* `recurrence_of` - Recurrence of

ReportLinkWrite.description: One typed, directed link to write on the report being emitted or edited.

kind.description:
How this report relates to `report_id`. `depends_on` for work that cannot land until the other report's fix does, `part_of` for one piece of a larger report, `follow_up_of` for work the other report left behind, `duplicate_of` for the same problem filed twice, and `recurrence_of` for a problem a resolved report already covered.

* `depends_on` - Depends on
* `part_of` - Part of
* `follow_up_of` - Follow-up of
* `duplicate_of` - Duplicate of
* `recurrence_of` - Recurrence of

reason.description: Optional one-line note on why the reports are linked this way.

report_id.description: Id of the report to link to. Must be another report in this project.

ReportMetric.description: One impact measurement shown on a report.

caption.description: Optional context the tile cannot show, such as a filter that narrows the count or a caveat on the data. Omit it rather than restate the title, unit, or window.

decision_window_days.description: Suggested days after release before assessing impact, not a monitoring schedule.

goal_direction.description:
Whether success means at most or at least goal_value.

* `at_most` - at_most
* `at_least` - at_least

goal_grain.description:
Whether the goal compares with the whole query window or each chart bucket.

* `whole_window` - whole_window
* `per_interval` - per_interval

goal_value.description: Proposed threshold after release. Informational only; does not schedule a check.

kind.description:
What the value measures, independent of how it is formatted or drawn.

* `affected_users` - affected_users
* `affected_sessions` - affected_sessions
* `occurrences` - occurrences
* `conversion_rate` - conversion_rate
* `error_rate` - error_rate
* `duration` - duration
* `revenue` - revenue
* `custom` - custom

metric_id.description: Stable slug for this metric within the report: lowercase letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens, starting with a letter or number.

minimum_data_points.description: Optional number of qualifying observations before assessing impact.

query.description: Required when authoring: a live InsightVizNode wrapping one bounded TrendsQuery. Consumers derive a BoldNumber execution for the whole-window aggregate and an ActionsBar execution for longitudinal buckets. The query must produce exactly one output series and no more than 1000 estimated longitudinal points; one formula may combine up to ten event or action source series. An affected_users metric uses exactly one source with `math: dau`; never sum its per-bucket unique-user values. A response omits this on list or redacts it to null on detail when the viewer lacks access to the definition.

role.description:
`primary` for the report's key observation, otherwise `supporting`.

* `primary` - primary
* `supporting` - supporting

series.description: Trailing per-bucket values of the live query, oldest first, saved with the value snapshot so a list row can draw the trend without running the query; at most 14 points. Null when no snapshot series is available to this viewer.

series_buckets.description: The Trends bucket label of each `series` point, oldest first, such as `2026-11-09` or `2026-11-09 10:00:00` in the project's timezone. Null when the snapshot did not record them or `series` is null for this viewer.

title.description: Short human-readable label for the measurement.

unit.description: Optional short suffix or currency code, such as `users`, `ms`, or `USD`.

value.description: Latest saved snapshot, initially observed during authoring and replaced when a person opens the inbox or the report. Null means no snapshot is available to this viewer; it never means zero. The required live query remains the source of truth.

value_at.description: When the visible snapshot value was measured; null when value is null.

value_format.description:
How to format the numeric value; semantic meaning remains in kind. `percentage` uses percentage points, so 34 renders as 34%; `percentage_scaled` uses a 0–1 ratio, so 0.34 renders as 34%. Sessions and occurrences use count; duration uses duration with an ms/s unit; revenue uses currency with an ISO currency unit.

* `number` - number
* `count` - count
* `percentage` - percentage
* `percentage_scaled` - percentage_scaled
* `duration` - duration
* `currency` - currency

label.description: Short context for the comparison, such as `Previous period`.

value.description: Baseline or previous value, formatted like the current value.

disposition.description:
Why the turn did not post the finding. `old_code`: a follow-up turn's finding on code that did not change since the last reviewed head. An automatic follow-up (run 2 and later) drops P2 and P3 findings this way, a requested review drops only P3, and a first review drops none. `dedup_prior`: repeats an earlier turn's finding. `dedup_comment`: repeats a PR comment. `dedup_anchor`: repeats a main-review finding at the same spot. `dedup_sibling`: repeats another finding from the same session or lens. `cap`: ranked below the per-review finding limit.

* `old_code` - On unchanged code
* `dedup_prior` - Repeat of an earlier review
* `dedup_comment` - Already in a PR comment

method.description:
The signal that decided `outcome`. `judge_confirmed` gives `addressed`. `comment_reply`, `comment_reply_agent` and `comment_reaction` give `reacted`. `judge_rejected` (the lines changed but the judge found no fix), `no_signal` (nothing touched the lines), `judge_budget_exhausted` and `judge_failed` (the judge did not rule) give `ignored`.

* `judge_rejected` - A judge found no fix
* `comment_reply` - A person replied
* `comment_reply_agent` - An agent replied
* `comment_reaction` - A person reacted
* `no_signal` - No signal
* `judge_budget_exhausted` - Not judged
* `judge_failed` - The judge failed

outcome.description:
What happened to the published finding by the time its pull request merged. `reacted`: a person or another agent replied to or reacted on its comment. `addressed`: a later commit changed the finding's lines and a judge confirmed that the change fixes it. `ignored`: neither.

* `reacted` - Reacted
* `ignored` - Ignored
