RunningTimeBaselineStats.description:
Raw control-group statistics the calculator uses to derive a baseline value and variance.

Supply this when you want the server to compute the baseline value and (for ratio/retention)
the delta-method variance, instead of passing `baseline_value`/`variance` directly.

denominator_sum.description: Sum of the denominator values. Required for ratio/retention metrics.

denominator_sum_squares.description: Sum of squared denominator values (ratio/retention variance).

numerator_denominator_sum_product.description: Sum of numerator×denominator products, used for the delta-method covariance term.

step_counts.description: Per-step counts for funnel metrics; the last entry is the final-step count.

sum.description: Sum of the metric values across the control group (for funnels, the numerator/conversions).

sum_squares.description: Sum of squared metric values. Mean metrics read their variance from it, and ratio/retention metrics need it. Without it, a mean metric's variance is approximated from the baseline value.

RunningTimeCalculationInput.description: Inputs for estimating the recommended sample size and running time of an experiment.

baseline_stats.description: Raw control-group statistics. When provided, the server derives baseline_value and variance.

baseline_value.description: Baseline metric value: conversion rate as a fraction 0-1 (funnel), average per user (mean), or the ratio (ratio/retention). Provide this or baseline_stats.

exposure_rate_per_day.description: Expected exposures per day. When provided, the response includes the recommended running time.

metric_type.description:
Metric type to size for. 'funnel' for conversion rates, 'mean_count' for event counts per user, 'mean_sum_or_avg' for summed property values per user, 'ratio' and 'retention' for ratio-style metrics (both require baseline_stats or an explicit variance).

* `funnel` - funnel
* `mean_count` - mean_count
* `mean_sum_or_avg` - mean_sum_or_avg
* `ratio` - ratio
* `retention` - retention

minimum_detectable_effect.description: Smallest relative change to detect, as a percentage (e.g. 5 means a 5% lift). Must be > 0.

number_of_variants.description: Total number of variants including control (default 2, at most 100).

variance.description: Pre-computed variance per user. Provide this or baseline_stats when metric_type is ratio/retention and baseline_value is given directly. When given, it replaces the variance the calculator derives for any metric type, including p(1-p) for funnels.

RunningTimeCalculationResult.description: Estimated sample size and running time for the given inputs.

baseline_value.description: Baseline metric value used in the calculation (echoed or derived from stats).

recommended_running_time_days.description: Estimated days to reach the recommended sample size. Null when exposure_rate_per_day is omitted.

recommended_sample_size.description: Total recommended sample size across all variants. Null if inputs are insufficient.

variance.description: Variance used in the calculation; null for funnel metrics (implicit in p(1-p)).

RunningTimeOutlook.description: What the experiment can detect over time, at its exposure rate so far.

days_since_launch.description: Days since the experiment launched, with fractions.

detectable_effect_now.description: The smallest relative change, as a percentage, that the exposures so far can detect.

exposures_per_day.description: Exposures that count toward the target, per day from launch to the end of the window the current results cover.

reachable_effect.description: The smallest relative change, as a percentage, that the experiment can detect within four weeks from today. A target for a smaller change is out of reach.

upcoming_checkpoints.description: Up to three week marks after today, out of weeks 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 26 and 52, with the change each can detect at the exposure rate so far.

RunningTimeTarget.description: The target sample of the experiment's running time estimate.

current_sample_size.description: Exposures so far that count toward the target: the control's and those of the variants that get traffic. A variant at 0% does not count. Null in manual mode, and when no result can size the target.

minimum_detectable_effect.description: The relative change, as a percentage, that the target sample is sized to detect.

outlook.description: What the experiment can detect over time, on the same curve the target is sized on. Null in manual mode, before launch, when the current results cover less than 0.1 days, and when no result can size the target.

recommended_sample_size.description: Exposures needed across the analyzed variants, so that the comparison of each variant with the control can detect the minimum detectable effect at the analysis's confidence level and 80% power. In manual running time mode, the saved target. Otherwise sized from the first primary metric's current result, with the variance the analysis uses and the flag's traffic split. Null when no result can size it yet. The variances come from the result and don't depend on the effect, so the sample scales with 1 / effect²: the target for another effect is recommended_sample_size × (minimum_detectable_effect / effect)².

Typed configuration for an S3-compatible batch-export destination (Cloudflare R2,
DigitalOcean Spaces, etc.).

Mirrors the non-credential fields of `S3CompatibleBatchExportInputs` in
`products/batch_exports/backend/service.py`.

compression.description:
Optional compression codec applied to exported files. Valid codecs depend on file_format.

* `brotli` - brotli
* `gzip` - gzip
* `lz4` - lz4
* `snappy` - snappy
* `zstd` - zstd

File format used for exported objects.

* `Parquet` - Parquet
* `JSONLines` - JSONLines

legacy_parquet_extension.description: Whether Parquet files keep the compression codec in their extension, for example '.parquet.zst' rather than '.parquet'. Parquet records its codec inside the file, so new exports leave it out. An export that already wrote Parquet files before this setting existed keeps it, so that pipelines matching on the old names do not break. Has no effect on JSON Lines, which always carries the codec in its extension.

max_file_size_mb.description: If set, rolls to a new file once the current file exceeds this size in MB.

prefix.description: Object key prefix applied to every exported file.

use_virtual_style_addressing.description: Use virtual-hosted-style addressing rather than path-style.

ScannerScoutCreate.description:
A scout to stand up for this scanner. The scanner comes from the URL, never the body: it is
what the caller's access is checked against, and what the scout is recorded as belonging to.

Inherits the Signals scout definition so a scout created here clears the same name and prompt-size
bars as one created through the generic endpoint.

At most 200 characters; blank means the scout has no name of its own and is labelled from its skill name instead.

Omit it and one is generated from `display_name` (`My APM scout` becomes `my-apm-scout`), with a numeric suffix when that name is taken. Pass it to pick the identifier yourself, or to keep a client written before display names working unchanged. The `signals-scout-` prefix is optional.

payload.description: The change to apply. Must include an 'operation' key and a 'value' key. count.description: Total immutable versions for this scorer.

next.description: URL of the next page, or null on the last page.

next_cursor.description: Continuation cursor, or null on the last page.

previous.description: URL of the previous page, or null on the first page and on lists that page forward only.

results.description: Versions on this page, newest first.

scale.description: The configured score bounds, or null when the evaluation sets none.

buckets.description: One bucket per integer on a small integer scale, else ten equal buckets across the scale.
buckets.title: Buckets

score.description: Null when the current period scored nothing.

counts.description: Observation count per bucket; same length as `labels`.

labels.description: Bucket labels (one per histogram bar) spanning the scanner's configured scale.

histogram.description: Score histogram; null when no observations have been scored.

summary.description: Score quantile summary; null when no observations have been scored.

count.description: Number of scored observations summarized.

task_id.description: The created chat task. Open it on the task detail page to continue.

chat_type.description:
Which scout chat to start: `author_scout` (guided scout authoring), `fleet_overview` (health of the scout fleet), or `recent_signals` (walk through recently emitted signals). The prompt template is owned server-side.

* `author_scout` - author_scout
* `fleet_overview` - fleet_overview
* `recent_signals` - recent_signals

suggestion_id.description: Optional id of a suggestion from this project's scout suggestion batch. The chat then opens on that draft instead of scanning from scratch. `author_scout` only.

user_prompt.description: Optional description, in the user's own words, of what the new scout should watch. The chat then opens on this request instead of asking from scratch. `author_scout` only, and not together with `suggestion_id`.

ScoutCheckSummary.description: One check as a scout run reads it back.

dispatched_at.description: When the coordinator last dispatched a run for the check. Null when no run waits.

dispatched_run_id.description: The scout run the coordinator dispatched for the check, once it started. Null while queued.

kind.description: `metric_threshold` (the coordinator measures it) or `agent` (a run does).

last_outcome.description: Verdict of the most recent run; null before the first.

last_outcome_reason.description: Why the most recent run was `inconclusive`: `awaiting_data`, `unmeasurable`, `needs_manual_verification`, or `no_fix_to_measure`. Null on any other outcome.

next_run_at.description: When the check next runs. Provisional while it is `pending`.

report_id.description: The report it is attached to.

run_state.description: Where the check is in its run cycle. `waiting_on_report`: pending, no fix to measure yet. `paused`: active, but its report is suppressed or its horizon passed, so nothing runs it. `scheduled`: active, not due yet. `due`: due now, so a run on the check's scout may record the verdict. `queued`: a run was dispatched and has not started. `running`: the dispatched run started and has time left. `stale`: the dispatched run recorded nothing in its window, so the coordinator dispatches again. Any other value is the terminal status.

status.description: `pending` while the check waits for the report to resolve, `active` while it still runs; every other value is terminal.

title.description: The expectation the check states.

waiting_on_run.description: True while an `agent` check waits on a dispatched run to record its verdict.

ScoutDeprecation.description: What PostHog has said about retiring this scout, for the chip and the banner to render.

phase.description:
How far the retirement has got: `announced` while the scout still runs, `retired` once its sunset has passed. A retired scout is paused and does not run again.

* `announced` - announced
* `retired` - retired

reason.description: Why PostHog is retiring the scout, written to be shown to a person as-is.

sunset_at.description: When the scout stops running. Null means the next fleet reconcile retires it.

superseded_by.description: Skill name of the scout that takes over, or blank when nothing replaces it.

ScoutEmissionReportLink.description:
One finding the run emitted, paired with the inbox report (if any) its signal grouped into.

Best-effort reverse of the report -> signals link: `report` is null when the finding hasn't
grouped into a report yet, was de-duplicated away, or its signal was deleted.

finding_id.description: Stable id the finding was emitted under.

report.description: The inbox report this finding linked to, or null if none could be resolved.

source_id.description: Deterministic `run:<run_id>:finding:<finding_id>` join key into the signal store.

ScoutFleet.description: `inventory.scout_fleet` — the other scouts running on this project, split by enablement.

disabled.description: Scouts that do not run, each carrying a `not_running_reason` — turned off, or left on with a skill that can't dispatch. Different from a surface no scout ever covered.

emitted_lookback_days.description: The window `last_emitted_at` was resolved over, so a null reads as 'quiet', not 'never'.

enabled.description: Scouts that actually run on this team: enabled, with a live skill the coordinator dispatches.

ScoutFleetEntry.description: One scout in either bucket of `inventory.scout_fleet`.

emit.description: Whether this scout's findings actually reach the inbox. False means dry-run: it runs and logs but emits nothing, so its silence says nothing about the surface it watches.

last_emitted_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp this scout last produced output on either channel (a finding, or an authored/edited report), within `emitted_lookback_days`. Null means quiet for at least that window, not never.

last_run_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the coordinator last dispatched this scout, or null if it has never run.

not_running_reason.description: Why this scout is in the `disabled` bucket: `turned_off` (a person or seed posture set it off), `auto_paused` (the system paused it), or `skill_unavailable` (left on, but its skill was deleted, superseded, or withheld, so it never dispatches). Null for scouts that actually run.

pause_reason.description: The cause behind an `auto_paused` entry: `no_output`, `ignored`, or `repeated_failures`. Null for every other entry.

run_cron_schedule.description: Optional cron expression, evaluated in the project timezone. Takes precedence over the interval.

run_interval_minutes.description: Minutes between runs when no cron schedule is set (default 1440, every 24 hours).

skill_name.description: The skill this config schedules as a scout.

ScoutLimits.description:
A team's enforced scout caps and current usage.

These are the values the coordinator actually applies at dispatch (resolved per-team override →
fleet-wide default → code constant), so the UI can show the real throttle rather than what a
user thinks they configured.

max_enabled_scouts.description: Most scouts the project can have switched on at once. Enabling another past this is rejected.

max_runs_per_day.description: Most scout runs the team can start per rolling 24 hours, or null when uncapped.

max_runs_per_tick.description: Most scout runs the team can start in a single 30-minute coordinator tick.

runs_remaining_today.description: Runs still allowed in the trailing 24h window (max_runs_per_day − runs_today), or null when uncapped.

runs_today.description: Scout runs the team has started in the trailing 24 hours.

ScoutMember.description: One project member's routing identity, for picking a `suggested_reviewers` entry on a report.

activity.description: What the member worked on recently. Use it as context to check against the report, not as proof: general activity is not evidence that the member owns the affected work. Filled only when the call passes `search` or `team` and returns at most 10 members. Null when the member has no ready summary, or when activity summaries are not available for this project.

email.description: The member's email — use to match a finding's owner by name/email.

first_name.description: The member's first name (may be empty).

github_login.description: The member's resolved GitHub login (lowercased), already resolved server-side. Null when the member has no linked GitHub account, which does not stop you routing to them: pass their `user_uuid` in `suggested_reviewers` and the report reaches them. A null login only means no draft PR can be opened as that person.

last_name.description: The member's last name (may be empty).

teams.description: The teams this member is on, from the project's synced team roster. Empty when no roster is synced, or when the member has no linked GitHub account, since the roster is keyed on that login. The roster is a periodic snapshot, so it can lag the live team.

user_uuid.description: The member's stable PostHog user UUID — the same id that appears as `created_by.uuid` on entities they own. A durable handle for this person across runs.

ScoutMemberActivity.description: What one member worked on recently, from their activity summary.

headline.description: One line about the member's recent work.

owned.description: Up to 5 objects the member created or changed, the most edited first.

stale.description: True when the summary waits for a rebuild in a newer format. Give a stale summary less weight.

themes.description: The labels of the main threads of the member's recent work.

watched.description: Up to 5 objects the member opened on several days, the most opened first. A member who only reads the work shows up here. A specific object here can support a reviewer pick when the pick's `reason` names it.

name.description: The latest name of the object.

type.description: The object type in snake case, such as `dashboard` or `feature_flag`.

ScoutMemberTeam.description: One team a member belongs to, from the project's synced team roster.

is_maintainer.description: True when this member maintains the team. Prefer maintainers when you pick reviewers for a team, and treat false as 'not known to maintain it': some rosters sync without roles.

name.description: The team's display name. For example `Team Desktop`.

provider.description: Where the team is defined, for example `github`. Today every team comes from GitHub.

slug.description: The team's slug, lowercased. For example `team-desktop`.

ScoutMetadata.description:
Team-scoped scout metadata for the inbox / Code-app UIs: enrollment, the alpha banner, and
the enforced limits. Sourced from the `signals-scout` flag payload so the banner and caps can
change without a deploy to either app.

banner_message.description: Free-form announcement banner to show above the scout UI (e.g. alpha run-limit notice), or null when unset.

enrolled.description: Whether this project runs scouts. True when the project is in the signals-scout flag's enrollment set — either listed explicitly in guaranteed_team_ids or covered by the "*" wildcard (every project that turns scouts on) — and not in skip_team_ids.

limits.description: The team's enforced scout run caps and current usage.

content.description: The note's prose, read verbatim by the run that picks it up.

created_by_name.description: Display name of the user who left the note, or null when unavailable.

expires_at.description: ISO-8601 expiry, or null for a note that stays active until deleted.

id.description: Note UUID. Pass to `scout-notes-delete` to retire the note.

origin.description: Where the note came from. `human`: left directly through this API. `report_note`: left through this API with `report_id` set, about the report its content names. `report_dismissal`: the note someone typed when they dismissed, snoozed, or restored one or more inbox reports. `report_discussion`: the question someone asked when they opened a discussion on a report. `report_feedback`: the note someone left when they rated a report useful or not. `report_reviewer_correction`: someone added or removed a suggested reviewer on a report, or a person or their agent claimed a report. The `scout-notes-list` tool description says how a scout reads each origin.

skill_name.description: Who the note is addressed to: a configured scout's skill name, a pipeline audience (`pipeline:*`, e.g. `pipeline:report-research`), or blank for a general note every scout sees.

content.description: The note's prose — feedback, a pointer, or a nudge for the scout(s) to weigh on their next runs (e.g. 'we shipped a new checkout on Tuesday, watch conversion closely', 'stop flagging the staging traffic spike'). Write it in Markdown; the run reads it verbatim.

expires_at.description: Optional ISO-8601 expiry. After this time the note drops out of the default list view, so time-boxed steering ('watch closely this week') retires itself. Omit for a note that stays active until deleted. Best-effort — a value that can't be parsed or is already in the past is dropped (the note stays active), not rejected, so the note is never lost.

report_id.description: Optional id of the inbox report this note is about. The note then names the report so a scout can fetch it, and the report's activity log records that the note was left. Requires edit access to inbox reports, and the report must belong to this project. The report reference shares the note's character budget, so `content` is capped at 9938 characters when this is set.

skill_name.description: Address the note to one scout by its skill name (exact match against a configured scout on the project — check `scout-config-list` for the roster), or to one stage of the report pipeline by its reserved audience (`pipeline:report-research`); any other `pipeline:*` value is rejected. Use a pipeline audience for guidance about how reports get researched, judged, and routed rather than about what the scouts watch, so it reaches that stage and no scout. Omit or leave blank for a general note every scout sees.

* `no_rows` - No Rows
* `false_value` - False Value
* `query_error` - Query Error

ScoutReport.description:
One report a scanner's scout filed. Enough to read it in Replay Vision; the inbox owns the
full record (status, priority, reviewers, run trail).

charts.description: Charts the scout attached. The summary places one inline with a `[label](chart:<chart_id>)` link; any it does not place render after the body.

filed_at.description: When the run that filed this report started. Later edits do not move it.

report_id.description: The report's id, as used by the Signals inbox.

skill_name.description: The scout that filed it, as its skill name.

summary.description: The report body, as markdown. Empty when the scout left it unset.

title.description: The report's title. Empty when the scout left it unset.

ScoutReportDiscussion.description: One discussion a person opened on a report your scout emitted or edited.

active_at.description: When the discussion last changed, for example when a run wrote its summary. Rows sort by it, newest first.

involvement.description:
`authored` when your scout emitted the report, `edited` when it only edited it.

* `authored` - Authored
* `edited` - Edited

question.description: For a `slack` discussion, the message that started it, in the person's own words. Null when that person may not steer scouts on this project, or started a later Slack discussion on the same report. Always null for an `inbox` discussion, because a scout note carried its question.

report_id.description: The report the discussion is about.

source.description:
`inbox` when the discussion started from Ask AI in the inbox, `slack` when it started from a reply in the report's Slack thread.

* `inbox` - Inbox
* `slack` - Slack

status.description: Status of the discussion's latest run, for example `in_progress` or `completed`. Null before it runs.

task_id.description: The discussion task.

task_summary.description: The latest run's summary of the conversation and its outcome. Null when no run has written one yet, or when the summary could have been written by someone who may not steer scouts on this project. For a `slack` discussion, other people in the public thread can shape the summary, so it is returned when the person who started the discussion may steer scouts.

applicability.description: When this criterion applies or cannot be assessed.

description.description: What this criterion measures.

enabled.description: Whether future evaluations should use this criterion.

pass_condition.description: The evidence needed to pass this criterion.

* `custom` - Custom

config_id.description: Scout config that owns this rubric.

criteria.description: Saved criteria, or enabled defaults before the first save.

reference_context.description: Governing source explicitly adopted for the saved rubric.

reference_generation_id.description: Generation whose governing source was adopted for the saved rubric.

revision.description: Saved rubric revision. Zero means it has not been saved.

skill_name.description: Scout skill name.

context.description: Optional priorities for this generation. Suggestions still cover the scout's full job.

completed_at.description: When generation completed or failed.

context.description: Optional priorities supplied for this generation only.

error.description: Failure message and suggested next step.

status.description:

suggestions.description: Draft criteria awaiting review and explicit saving.

summary.description: Investigation summary and limitations.

task_run_id.description: Task run performing the investigation, once created.

description.description: Scout description captured for this reference.

instructions.description: Saved scout instructions used for judging.

instructions_truncated.description: Whether the saved instructions were truncated.

report_disposition_instructions.description: Report-disposition rules captured for this reference.

schema_version.description: Version of the saved reference-context format.

skill_name.description: Name of the skill used for generation.

truncated_files.description: Paths of files truncated in the saved reference.

ScoutRunIdsBatchRequest.description:
Request body for the batched emissions / emission-reports lookups: the set of run UUIDs to
resolve in one call. Collapses the findings UI's old per-run fan-out (one request — and for the

status.description:
Status of the batch run. waiting: the audience's cohort is still calculating. queued and active: the run is enrolling its audience. completed: the whole audience was enrolled. When every enrolled person's run has ended, or a day after the run completed, PostHog checks for errored sends. A completed run stays completed when no send errored, becomes partially_failed when some sends errored, and becomes failed when every send errored. failed also means the run could not enroll its audience. cancelled: someone stopped the run. A send errors when its step throws, for example on a template that does not render. Provider failures such as bounces are not errored sends; read them from the run's metrics.

* `waiting` - Waiting
* `queued` - Queued
* `active` - Active
* `completed` - Completed
* `partially_failed` - Partially failed
* `cancelled` - Cancelled
* `failed` - Failed

The whole email can be at most 40 MB after Base64 encoding, about 29 MB of files. File types mailbox providers block, such as `.exe`, are refused. Doesn't apply to a send with `template_id`, which refuses any file here.

bcc.description: Addresses that get a hidden copy of the email your code rendered: one address, or a list of up to 10. Each is a bare address such as `jane@example.com`, with no name. Doesn't apply to a send with `template_id`, which refuses any address here.

capture_engagement.description: Deprecated: use `tracking.engagement`. Whether the engagement events (sent, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced) of the email your code rendered are captured as analytics events of the recipient. Defaults to true. A send with `tracking` can't also carry this field. A project whose admin turned engagement capture off captures nothing, whatever the send says.

cc.description: Addresses that get a visible copy of the email your code rendered: one address, or a list of up to 10. Each is a bare address such as `jane@example.com`, with no name. Doesn't apply to a send with `template_id`, which refuses any address here.

distinct_id.description: Distinct ID the email's engagement events (sent, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced) are captured under. Defaults to the recipient's email address. The events join the person who has this ID, or start a new person when nobody has it. No events are captured when the project's engagement events setting is off, or when `tracking` or `capture_engagement` turns engagement off for a send with `template_key`. The template can't read the person's properties, so pass everything it needs in `message_data`.

from.description: Sender of the email your code rendered, as `security@example.com` or `Example <security@example.com>`, on a verified domain of the project. Without it, the email goes out from the project's default sender, or from its only verified sender when it has no default.

html.description: HTML body of the email your code rendered, at most 5 MiB as UTF-8.

message_data.description: Data for the template's Liquid placeholders, available as `variables`. For example `{"reset_link": "https://..."}` fills `{{ variables.reset_link }}`.

reply_to.description: Addresses replies to the email your code rendered go to.

sensitive.description: Mark the email as sensitive when it carries login links, reset tokens, or codes. Sensitive emails keep their links unchanged unless `tracking` turns clicks on, leave the subject off engagement events, and keep the content out of logs. Defaults to the matched template's setting, or true when no template matches. It can't be false when the matched template is sensitive.

subject.description: Subject of the email your code rendered.

template_id.description: ID of the email template to send. The template must be made transactional first. Send either `template_id` or `template_key`.

template_key.description: Names an email whose content your code rendered, such as `order-shipped`, so its metrics, logs and status group under it. Letters, numbers, hyphens (-) and underscores (_) only, at most 256 characters. Send it with `subject` and `html` or `text`. PostHog sends the content as is and never stores it as a template.

text.description: Plain text body of the email your code rendered, at most 5 MiB as UTF-8. Without it, PostHog derives the text from `html`.

tracking.description: What PostHog tracks for the email your code rendered. `true` tracks opens and clicks and captures engagement events. `false` turns off all of it, now and for any kind of tracking added later. An object sets each kind on its own, and a kind it leaves out keeps its default. Without this field, PostHog tracks opens and captures engagement events, and tracks clicks only when the email isn't sensitive (see `sensitive`). Turn on `clicks` for a sensitive email only when its links are safe to send through a redirect. A link with `data-ph-no-track` keeps its own address either way. Click tracking needs open tracking. A project whose admin turned engagement capture off captures nothing, whatever the send says. The object form needs a JSON body.

clicks.description: Whether the email's links go through a redirect that counts clicks. Defaults to true when the email isn't sensitive and false when it is. Needs `opens`. A link with `data-ph-no-track` keeps its own address.

engagement.description: Whether the email's engagement events (sent, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced) are captured as analytics events of the recipient. Defaults to true.

opens.description: Whether PostHog adds its open pixel to the email. Defaults to true.

identifiers.description: Who the email is for, used to attribute engagement events.

message_data.description: Data for the template's Liquid placeholders, available as `variables`. For example `{"reset_link": "https://..."}` fills `{{ variables.reset_link }}`.

message_id.description: ID of the queued send. Delivery and engagement are reported against the template asynchronously.

replayed.description: True when an earlier request with the same `Idempotency-Key` already queued this email. No new email was sent, and `message_id` is the earlier send's ID.

refund_ineligibility_reason.description: Why refunding this report's PR would be rejected right now, or null when a refund would be accepted (see the field's schema for the reason values).

repo_slug.description: `organization/repository` the report's work targets, from the latest repo-selection artefact (when present). Lets list cards show repository context without a per-card fetch.

research_context.description: Evidence available to the latest research pass. Null for legacy reports.

reviewer_assignment.description: Reviewer control and state token for preparing an automatic proposal.

scout_name.description: skill_name slug of the scout that authored this report, when scout-authored (from ClickHouse); null otherwise.

source_issues.description: URLs of the external issues this report is about, as recorded by the scout or person that filed it, oldest first. source_products.description: Distinct source products contributing signals to this report (from ClickHouse).

source_suggestion.description: A product the team does not use that would have given this report better evidence, from the latest source suggestion artefact. startup_failure.description: Startup failure from the latest failed research attempt, when available.

status.description: Current report status. Monitoring reads as resolved when its rollout is disabled.

suggested_prompts.description: Follow-up prompts the report's author suggests sending about it (questions to ask, or next-step actions to request), in the order they were written. The inbox offers them above the `Ask AI` box; clicking one fills the box with it.

Null unless status is suppressed. `dismissed`: a person or agent dismissed it, it was merged into another report, or its pull request closed without merging; dismissal_reason says which when one was given. `safety_judge`: the safety judge marked it unsafe. `not_actionable`: the actionability judge marked it not actionable. `system`: suppressed by the pipeline for another reason. Every value except `dismissed` is a verdict nobody has reviewed, listed by the `held_back` inbox view.

SignalReportArtefactLogCreate.description:
Body for appending an artefact to a report.

Everything is append-only: log artefacts accumulate, status artefacts supersede the previous
version (latest-wins). The `content` shape depends on `artefact_type` and is validated
against the type's schema (see `products/signals/backend/artefact_schemas.py`).

artefact_type.description: The artefact type. One of: actionability_judgment, channel_assignment, code_reference, commit, dismissal, note, priority_judgment, related_to, repo_selection, safety_judgment, signal_finding, source_suggestion, suggested_reviewers. Log types accumulate; status types (safety_judgment, actionability_judgment, priority_judgment, repo_selection, suggested_reviewers, channel_assignment, source_suggestion) are latest-wins — appending a new version supersedes the previous one as the report's canonical status.

claim_id.description: Active claim to attribute this work to. Must belong to the caller and report.

content.description: The artefact payload as a JSON object or array; shape depends on artefact_type and is validated against its schema.

expected_reviewers.description: Report reviewer_assignment.state read before selection began. Required when reviewer corrections are enabled.

reviewer_outcome.description:
A successful selection, a deliberate empty result, or an unavailable lookup. Defaults to selected when omitted.

* `selected` - Selected
* `no_suitable_owner` - No suitable owner
* `lookup_failed` - Lookup failed

action.description:
Add or remove only the supplied people, replace the list, or explicitly confirm it.

* `add` - Add
* `remove` - Remove
* `replace` - Replace
* `confirm` - Confirm

content.description: People to add, remove, or keep in a replacement. Send an empty list for confirmation.

expected_reviewers.description: State from the last read. Required for replacement and confirmation when corrections are enabled.

removal_note.description: Optional context for the removal, such as the area the person does not work on. Remove action only.

removal_reason.description:
Why the people in `targets` are removed. Remove action only. 'wrong_area': the work should not be on them, because it is outside their area, they moved off it, or someone else owns it. 'already_covered': another reviewer already covers the report. 'unavailable': they do not have bandwidth right now. The last two say nothing about ownership. 'other': explain in removal_note. Research and scouts read the reason when they pick reviewers for later reports.

* `wrong_area` - Not their area
* `already_covered` - Someone else is on it
* `unavailable` - No bandwidth
* `other` - Other

targets.description: Explicit add or remove targets. When supplied, content is only a fallback for older servers.

ids.description: Report ids to claim for the caller in one call (1–100). Duplicates are de-duplicated. Each id is claimed independently, so a report that cannot be claimed does not block the rest.

takeover_agent_claims.description: Take over a report that an agent or an internal task holds. A report that a person holds directly is never taken over and comes back as a conflict.

claimed_count.description: Number of reports the caller now holds.

conflict_count.description: Number of reports whose claim was refused.

not_found_count.description: Number of requested ids not visible to the caller.

results.description: One result per requested id, in request order (after de-duplication).

detail.description: Human-readable explanation for a conflict or not_found outcome.

id.description: The report id this result refers to.

outcome.description: One of: claimed, conflict, not_found. claimed: the caller holds the claim, including when it already did. conflict: the claim was refused, because someone else holds the report or its status does not allow a claim (a 409 on the single-report endpoint). not_found: no report with this id is visible to you.

corrected_repository.description: Optional, only allowed with dismissal_reason='wrong_repo'. The repository this report should have targeted, in 'owner/repo' format (case-insensitive). It is recorded with the dismissal and fed into future repository selection for this project. When the repository is connected to the project, it also becomes the report's corrected repo selection, so restoring the report re-researches against it.

dismissal_note.description: Optional free-form note explaining the dismissal. Capped at 4000 characters.

dismissal_reason.description:
Optional canonical reason code recorded with the transition. Must be one of: already_fixed, report_unclear, analysis_wrong, wrong_assignee, wrong_repo, wontfix_intentional, wontfix_irrelevant, fixed_outside_posthog, verified_manually, no_action_needed, pr_merged, other — these match the inbox UI so the rationale renders as a labelled chip rather than a raw code. When the work this report asked for is done, the honest transition is state='resolved' with 'fixed_outside_posthog' (the fix landed without a pull request), 'pr_merged' (a pull request with the fix was merged but did not resolve the report on its own), or 'already_fixed' (it was fixed before the report was filed). Use 'no_action_needed' with state='resolved' when the report was useful but needs no implementation. A report that failed in processing resolves too, so a fix that landed is recorded as a fix rather than as a dismissal. These three codes claim the issue is gone, so a later signal about the same issue starts a fresh report linked to this one. Fixed reason codes require state='suppressed' or state='resolved', not 'potential'. The dismissal codes (report_unclear, analysis_wrong, wrong_assignee, wontfix_*) go with state='suppressed' and absorb later signals silently. 'wrong_assignee' is accepted from older clients, but a report sent to the wrong person still holds work: remove the person from the report's reviewers with a removal_reason instead of suppressing it. 'wrong_repo' when the agent picked the wrong repository for this report, ideally with corrected_repository naming the right one. The report stays suppressed, but a later matching signal starts a fresh linked report with a new repository selection informed by the project's correction feedback, even when no corrected_repository was supplied. Use 'verified_manually' with state='resolved' to stop Monitoring after manual verification. It requires Monitoring to be enabled and a report with a Monitoring period, and records no automatic verification result or evidence amendment. Use 'other' together with a dismissal_note for anything that doesn't fit a code.

* `already_fixed` - Already fixed
* `report_unclear` - Report is unclear to me
* `analysis_wrong` - Agent's analysis is wrong
* `wrong_assignee` - Wrong assignee
* `wrong_repo` - Agent picked the wrong repository
* `wontfix_intentional` - Won't fix - intentional behavior
* `wontfix_irrelevant` - Not relevant to this project
* `fixed_outside_posthog` - Fixed outside PostHog
* `verified_manually` - Verified manually
* `no_action_needed` - No action needed
* `pr_merged` - PR was merged
* `other` - Something else…

ids.description: Report ids to transition to `state` in one call (1–100). Duplicates are de-duplicated; each id is processed independently so one disallowed transition does not block the rest. `dismissal_reason`, `dismissal_note`, `corrected_repository` and `snooze_for` apply to every id.

snooze_for.description: Optional, only honored when state is 'potential'. Number of additional signals the report must accumulate before it is re-promoted into the pipeline — effectively snoozing it until then. Omit to let the report re-enter the pipeline on the next matching signal.

state.description:
Target state for the report. Use 'suppressed' to dismiss the report from the inbox, 'potential' to snooze it or restore it from the archive, or 'resolved' when the report is finished. Resolving is allowed from ready, pending_input, failed, closed, or monitoring, or from a suppressed report that previously held one of those statuses or resolved. Resolving an already resolved report succeeds. Other statuses return 409 (skipped in bulk). Dismissing or resolving closes the report's open implementation PR, if it has one. Use 'monitoring' when implementation is complete and outcome verification is pending. Entry requires the organization rollout and snapshots this report's pending or active, unexpired checks. Without applicable checks the report resolves directly. Manual completion records caller attribution, stops remaining follow-up checks, and does not claim automatic verification or an evidence amendment. Use 'ready' to reopen a report in monitoring or closed. It returns to ready with its research, pull requests, and follow-up checks kept, and its Monitoring period ends. Completing implementation again starts a new period. Reopening is refused for other statuses and for refunded reports.

* `suppressed` - suppressed
* `potential` - potential
* `resolved` - resolved
* `monitoring` - monitoring
* `ready` - ready

failed_count.description: Number of reports that failed on invalid request data.

not_found_count.description: Number of requested ids not visible to the caller.

results.description: One result per requested id, in request order (after de-duplication).

skipped_count.description: Number of reports whose transition was not allowed.

transitioned_count.description: Number of reports the call accepted. A report that already had the requested state counts here too, because a repeat dismiss or resolve still records its feedback.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation for non-transitioned outcomes (skipped / failed / not_found).

id.description: The report id this result refers to.

outcome.description: One of: transitioned, skipped, failed, not_found. transitioned: the state change was applied. skipped: the transition was not allowed from the report's current status (a 409 on the single-report endpoint). failed: the request data was invalid for this report. not_found: no report with this id is visible to you.

status.description: The report's status after the transition. Present only when outcome is 'transitioned'.

config.description: What the check measures and what the result must satisfy; the shape depends on `kind`. `query` and `baseline_value` are null when you cannot read the data they describe.

consecutive_errors.description: Runs that could not be measured since the last clean one.

dispatched_at.description: When the `agent` check's scout run started, cleared as soon as a verdict is recorded. A non-null value is what tells a reader the check is running rather than waiting, because dispatch also pushes `next_run_at` out to the result window. Always null on a `metric_threshold` check, which is measured in the tick that collects it.

* `unmeasurable` - Unmeasurable
* `needs_manual_verification` - Needs Manual Verification

inbox_merge_key.description: Sort key from the ranker named by the list response's ranker field, for sort=recommended and sort=personal only. For an outcome ranker (open, action or fix), a scored report gets 1 minus its score, from 0 to 1, and a report without a usable score gets 2 plus its priority rank. The priority ranker uses the priority rank only, from 0 (P0) to 5 (no priority). For the personal ranker, a report in the stored personal ranking gets its position in that ranking from 0, and every other report gets the number of those positions plus its key from the recommended ranker. corrected_repository.description: Optional, only allowed with dismissal_reason='wrong_repo'. The repository this report should have targeted, in 'owner/repo' format (case-insensitive). It is recorded with the dismissal and fed into future repository selection for this project. When the repository is connected to the project, it also becomes the report's corrected repo selection, so restoring the report re-researches against it.

dismissal_note.description: Optional free-form note explaining the dismissal. Capped at 4000 characters.

dismissal_reason.description:
Optional canonical reason code recorded with the transition. Must be one of: already_fixed, report_unclear, analysis_wrong, wrong_assignee, wrong_repo, wontfix_intentional, wontfix_irrelevant, fixed_outside_posthog, verified_manually, no_action_needed, pr_merged, other — these match the inbox UI so the rationale renders as a labelled chip rather than a raw code. When the work this report asked for is done, the honest transition is state='resolved' with 'fixed_outside_posthog' (the fix landed without a pull request), 'pr_merged' (a pull request with the fix was merged but did not resolve the report on its own), or 'already_fixed' (it was fixed before the report was filed). Use 'no_action_needed' with state='resolved' when the report was useful but needs no implementation. A report that failed in processing resolves too, so a fix that landed is recorded as a fix rather than as a dismissal. These three codes claim the issue is gone, so a later signal about the same issue starts a fresh report linked to this one. Fixed reason codes require state='suppressed' or state='resolved', not 'potential'. The dismissal codes (report_unclear, analysis_wrong, wrong_assignee, wontfix_*) go with state='suppressed' and absorb later signals silently. 'wrong_assignee' is accepted from older clients, but a report sent to the wrong person still holds work: remove the person from the report's reviewers with a removal_reason instead of suppressing it. 'wrong_repo' when the agent picked the wrong repository for this report, ideally with corrected_repository naming the right one. The report stays suppressed, but a later matching signal starts a fresh linked report with a new repository selection informed by the project's correction feedback, even when no corrected_repository was supplied. Use 'verified_manually' with state='resolved' to stop Monitoring after manual verification. It requires Monitoring to be enabled and a report with a Monitoring period, and records no automatic verification result or evidence amendment. Use 'other' together with a dismissal_note for anything that doesn't fit a code.

* `already_fixed` - Already fixed
* `report_unclear` - Report is unclear to me
* `analysis_wrong` - Agent's analysis is wrong
* `wrong_assignee` - Wrong assignee
* `wrong_repo` - Agent picked the wrong repository
* `wontfix_intentional` - Won't fix - intentional behavior
* `wontfix_irrelevant` - Not relevant to this project
* `fixed_outside_posthog` - Fixed outside PostHog
* `verified_manually` - Verified manually
* `no_action_needed` - No action needed
* `pr_merged` - PR was merged
* `other` - Something else…

snooze_for.description: Optional, only honored when state is 'potential'. Number of additional signals the report must accumulate before it is re-promoted into the pipeline — effectively snoozing it until then. Omit to let the report re-enter the pipeline on the next matching signal.

state.description:
Target state for the report. Use 'suppressed' to dismiss the report from the inbox, 'potential' to snooze it or restore it from the archive, or 'resolved' when the report is finished. Resolving is allowed from ready, pending_input, failed, closed, or monitoring, or from a suppressed report that previously held one of those statuses or resolved. Resolving an already resolved report succeeds. Other statuses return 409 (skipped in bulk). Dismissing or resolving closes the report's open implementation PR, if it has one. Use 'monitoring' when implementation is complete and outcome verification is pending. Entry requires the organization rollout and snapshots this report's pending or active, unexpired checks. Without applicable checks the report resolves directly. Manual completion records caller attribution, stops remaining follow-up checks, and does not claim automatic verification or an evidence amendment. Use 'ready' to reopen a report in monitoring or closed. It returns to ready with its research, pull requests, and follow-up checks kept, and its Monitoring period ends. Completing implementation again starts a new period. Reopening is refused for other statuses and for refunded reports.

* `suppressed` - suppressed
* `potential` - potential
* `resolved` - resolved
* `monitoring` - monitoring
* `ready` - ready

SignalScoutConfig.description:
Read shape for a per-(team, skill) scout config.

One row per scout skill on the team. The coordinator auto-creates a row
when it discovers a scout skill; this serializer lets agents tune the row.

allowed_mcp_tools.description: Exact MCP tool names selected for this scout, excluding its built-in run context tools. Null means no tool restriction; an empty list selects no additional tools. Write access is derived from selected write tools. Clearing to null preserves the last write scopes. Send this field or tool_preset, never both. Requires the scouts-tool-access feature flag.

auto_pause_exempt.description: Whether this scout is exempt from the inactivity sweep, meaning both the `ignored` pause and the `no_output` quiet warning. Set it on watchdog scouts whose value is staying quiet. Only ever set explicitly: re-enabling a swept scout instead grants a fresh grace window before the sweep may judge it again.

consecutive_failure_count.description: How many of this scout's runs have failed in a row. Back to 0 after a successful run or any config edit. At the failure limit the scout pauses itself (`status` becomes `paused_by_system` with `pause_reason` `repeated_failures`) and retries about once a day; a successful retry resumes it, and so does setting `enabled=true`.

custom_image_id.description: ID of a project-shared custom sandbox image this scout's runs start from. Null uses the project's default scout image, or the standard image when no default is set. Only the scout's author or a project admin can change it. Setting an image requires skill-authoring authorization (the `llm_skill:write` scope and skill editor access), since the image can supply agent instructions. An image that is missing or not ready at run time falls back to the standard image.

deprecation.description: Set when PostHog is retiring this scout, and null otherwise. Carries the phase, the reason to show, what replaces the scout, and when it stops running. Only a canonical scout the project has not edited is ever marked: a project's own copy keeps running and reads as null.

description.description: Human-readable summary of what this scout investigates, sourced from the scout skill's `description` metadata. Use it for a quick steer on the scout's focus without loading the full skill body. Empty if the skill is not currently present on the team or carries no description.

display_name.description: Name shown in the UI. Does not change the skill name. Leave blank to use the default name.

effective_precheck_query.description: The pre-check query the next scheduled run uses: `precheck_query`, or the default the scout's skill ships. Null when no pre-check runs.

emit.description: Whether the scout writes findings to the inbox. False = dry-run: it runs and logs but emits nothing.

enabled.description: Whether this scout runs on its schedule. Disabled scouts are skipped by the coordinator. Derived from `status`: true for `active` and `pending_pause`, false for the paused statuses.

last_precheck_at.description: When a scheduled run last evaluated this scout's pre-check. A skipped run writes no run row, so this stays recent while `last_run_at` ages. Null if no pre-check has run.

last_precheck_outcome.description:
The outcome of the latest scheduled pre-check: `run` (the query found something new), `skip` (nothing new, so the run did not start), or `error` (the query failed and the run started). Null if no pre-check has run.

* `run` - Run
* `skip` - Skip
* `error` - Error

last_precheck_row_count.description: How many rows the latest scheduled pre-check returned, at most 50. Null if no pre-check has run.

last_run_at.description: When the coordinator last dispatched this scout. Null if it has never run.

lifecycle_locked.description: Opt-in guard on this scout's lifecycle. Off by default, so anyone with scout write access may pause, resume, switch the scout to dry run, or delete it. On, only the person the scout's runs act as or a project admin may do any of those, or change this flag. Use it on a scout whose output people depend on: `signal_scout:write` is a project-wide scope held by people and by unattended agents alike, and a resume has to pass the project's enabled-scout maximum that a pause does not, so a bulk pause is not undone in one step. The lock never stops an automatic pause, such as the inactivity sweep or the repeated-failure breaker.

managed_by.description:
Who controls this scout now. `team`: a person set it up or has changed it. `background`: PostHog runs it in the background and no person has edited it yet. Any edit through this API changes `background` to `team`.

* `team` - Team
* `background` - Background

mcp_gateway_server_ids.description: MCP gateway servers (by id) this scout's runs may use, chosen from the connections members shared to the whole team. Selection is per scout: an empty list gives the scout no MCP servers. Applies from the scout's next run.

model.description: Optional model id this scout's runs are pinned to, e.g. `claude-opus-4-5`. Must be one of the platform's agent models; an invalid id is rejected with the available ones listed. Null keeps the default model, chosen by the platform. Early access: the pin can only be set on projects enrolled in the scout model preview, and only takes effect there. Set null to clear it.

network_access.description:
What the scout's sandbox can reach over the network while it runs. `trusted` (the default) restricts runs to the platform's trusted-domain allowlist (PostHog, GitHub, common package registries). `full` lets the scout reach any site, for skills that read external sources such as documentation or papers.

* `trusted` - Trusted domains only
* `full` - Full

output_destinations.description: Destinations that receive each finding or report this scout emits. Empty when none is configured.

owners.description: Who answers for this scout, seed-creator first. Ownership is recorded on the scout's skill rather than on this config, so editing the skill or toggling the scout leaves it unchanged. Reports the scout files suggest these people as reviewers. Prefer this over `created_by`-style fields, which only say who last flipped a switch. Empty when nobody owns the scout, when the owners are no longer members with access to the project, or when the caller is a scout sandbox token: owners are member PII, and a scout reads them through the skill API instead.

pause_reason.description:
Why the system paused (or warned) this scout: `no_output` (it emitted nothing over the evaluation window), `ignored` (no person engaged with its reports — no view, rating, note, dismissal, or resolution), `repeated_failures` (consecutive failed runs), `retired` (PostHog retired the scout), or `background_removed` (the background lane stopped managing the scout). Null unless `status` is `pending_pause` or `paused_by_system`.

* `no_output` - No output
* `ignored` - Ignored
* `repeated_failures` - Repeated failures
* `trial_scout_limit` - Free trial scout limit
* `retired` - Retired
* `background_removed` - Background removed

precheck_disabled.description: True turns off the pre-check, both `precheck_query` and the default the skill ships, so every scheduled run starts. False (the default) uses `precheck_query`, or the skill default when that is null.

precheck_query.description: Optional HogQL `SELECT` a scheduled run evaluates before it starts. When it returns no rows, or one row with one false value (`false`, `0`, null or empty), the run is skipped: no sandbox, no model call, and no run row. Any other result starts the run, and the scout reads the rows. A query error also starts the run. Use `{since}` (the start of the last run that ran, or when the scout was created) and `{now}` to look only at what is new, e.g. `SELECT count() FROM events WHERE event = '$exception' AND timestamp > {since}`. To run at least once a week however quiet it is, add `OR {since} < {now} - INTERVAL 7 DAY` to the condition. Only scheduled runs evaluate it: a manual or workflow run always starts. `{interval_minutes}` is the gap between two scheduled runs, so a backstop can follow the schedule: `{since} < {now} - toIntervalMinute(greatest(1440, 2 * {interval_minutes}))` runs at least daily and never more often than every two intervals. The query stops after 10 seconds and reads at most 50 rows. Try a query with `scout-config-precheck-test` before you save it. Null or blank uses the default pre-check the scout's skill ships, if any. To turn every pre-check off, set `precheck_disabled`.

precheck_query_source.description: Where `effective_precheck_query` comes from: `config` (this scout's `precheck_query`), `skill_default` (the default its skill ships), or `off` (no pre-check runs).

repositories.description: GitHub repositories this scout clones into its sandbox, each in `organization/repo` format. Set them for a scout that reads code, so it can search the tree and run the project's own tests instead of reading files one API call at a time. Empty (the default) leaves the sandbox without a checkout. The scout's GitHub access stays read-only either way, so a repository listed here is never writable from a run. At most 10, each reachable through the project's GitHub connection. Applies from the scout's next run.

run_cron_schedule.description: Optional five-field cron expression evaluated in the project timezone, e.g. '30 9 * * *'. Takes precedence over `run_interval_minutes` when set. Null means the rolling interval schedule.

run_interval_minutes.description: Minutes between runs (30–43200). The scout runs once this interval has elapsed since its last run.

scout_origin.description: Where this scout came from: `canonical` for a scout PostHog ships and maintains (seeded from `products/signals/skills/`), or `custom` for one a team hand-authored on this project. Use it to badge built-in vs custom scouts instead of a hardcoded name list. Defaults to `custom` if the skill is not currently present on the team.

scout_role.description: What this scout is to the harness: `specialist` for one that watches a product surface, or `operational` for one PostHog ships to watch the self-driving system itself. An operational scout is exempt from the inactivity sweep and from the enabled-scout cap, and is not a scout a project should delete. Always `specialist` for a custom scout.

skill_name.description: The skill this config controls as a scout. Set at creation, not editable.

source_id.description: Id of the owning object in `source_product`, e.g. a Replay Vision scanner id.

source_product.description: The product that stood this scout up for one of its own objects. Null when a person created it.

status.description:
Lifecycle status. `active`: runs on its schedule. `pending_pause`: still running, but flagged by the system to pause soon unless something changes (any config edit clears it). `paused_by_system`: paused automatically, see `pause_reason`; set `enabled=true` to resume. `paused_by_user`: switched off by a person and never resumed automatically.

* `active` - Active
* `pending_pause` - Pending pause
* `paused_by_system` - Paused by system
* `paused_by_user` - Paused by user

status_changed_at.description: When `status` last changed. For `pending_pause` this is when the warning was issued (an `ignored` warning pauses about a week later unless someone engages with the scout's reports — opening one counts; a `no_output` warning only flags the scout); for the paused statuses it is when the scout was paused. Null if the status never changed.

status_changed_by.description: Who last moved `status`, when a person did it through this API. Null for a system transition such as an automatic pause, for a row whose status never changed, and for a caller that may not read member identities. Pair it with `status` to say who turned a scout off, instead of only when it went off.

structured_output_schema.description: Optional JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) describing ONE structured record this scout produces via `scout-record-output` — e.g. a per-report quality judgment (`{"type": "object", "properties": {"verdict": {"enum": ["good", "bad", "unsure"]}, "reason": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["verdict", "reason"]}`). The root must be `"type": "object"`. Setting a schema turns the structured-output channel on: the run prompt renders the schema and every submitted record is validated against it and recorded in the project as a `$scout_structured_output` event, queryable like any event. The channel also requires emit — a dry-run scout has nowhere to record to. Cardinality is the scout's call (one record per run, one per judged entity, ...). Null = channel off. Setting a schema requires skill-authoring authorization (the `llm_skill:write` scope and skill editor access) since the scout reads it verbatim in its prompt; clearing it needs only the config write. Records validate against the schema in force when the run was dispatched.

tags.description: Free-form labels for grouping the fleet, e.g. `["revenue", "on-call"]`. Normalized to lowercase kebab-case (`On Call` and `on_call` both become `on-call`), deduped, and stored sorted; at most 10 tags, each at most 50 characters once normalized. Pass the full desired set — a write replaces the existing tags rather than merging into them. Filter the config list with the `tags` query parameter.

tool_preset.description: Preset used to select the saved tool list, custom for an explicit list, or null when unrestricted.

updated_at.description: When this config last changed: an edit through this API, or a status change the system made such as an automatic pause. A scheduled run does not bump it — the coordinator stamps `last_run_at` with a direct write — so this reads as when the scout was last tuned rather than when it last ran.

write_scopes.description: Write access granted to this one scout, as scope strings. The grantable set is `account_note:write`, `alert:write`, `annotation:write`, `canvas:write`, `customer_task:write`, `dashboard:write`, `event_definition:write`, `experiment:write`, `hog_flow_proposal:write`, `insight:write`, `llm_skill:write`, `notebook:write`, `replay_scanner:write`, `ticket:write`, `warehouse_table:write`, `warehouse_view:write`. A new scout starts with `notebook:write` when this field is omitted. Empty means the scout reads the project and writes only its findings and its own memory. Each scope is project-wide and object-level, so a scout holding `dashboard:write` can update or delete any dashboard in the project, not only ones it made. `ticket:write` lets the scout update tickets, manage saved views, and add private notes. Scouts cannot send public replies, compose emails, change existing notes, or change customer identity fields. Ticket changes can start workflows that message customers. `event_definition:write` lets the scout change the tags on event definitions and nothing else. `account_note:write` lets the scout write and retag notes on Customer analytics accounts. Its notes are always tagged `scout` and with its skill name, and the account notes API refuses its deletes. Account notes are also notebooks, so `notebook:write` can still edit or trash one. Grant only what this scout maintains. Only the person the scout's runs act as (whoever authored it) or a project admin can set it, and a scoped API key must itself carry each scope it grants. A dry run (`emit=false`) never holds the grant, and a run that acts as a project member other than the author holds only the default scopes. Applies from the scout's next run.

SignalScoutCreate.description: Create a runnable custom scout and its config in one atomic request.

body.description: Complete markdown prompt executed on every scout run. Include any project-specific signal names, thresholds, investigation steps, and report criteria here.

config.description: Optional schedule, enablement, dry-run posture, and delivery settings. Defaults to an enabled, emitting scout on the daily interval with no external destination.

description.description: Short description of the signal or behavior this scout investigates.

display_name.description: Name shown wherever people identify this scout, written however you want it — spaces, capitalization, and acronyms are kept as typed, and two scouts may share one. At most 200 characters; blank means the scout has no name of its own and is labelled from its skill name instead.

files.description: Optional reference files bundled with the scout prompt.

name.description: Optional skill name for the scout — its permanent identifier, containing only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens. Omit it and one is generated from `display_name` (`My APM scout` becomes `my-apm-scout`), with a numeric suffix when that name is taken. Pass it to pick the identifier yourself, or to keep a client written before display names working unchanged. The `signals-scout-` prefix is optional.

suggestion_id.description: Optional id of the suggestion this scout was created from. The suggestion then stops being offered on this project. An id this project's batch does not hold is ignored.

created.description: True when this request created the missing scout skill or config; false when both already existed.

SignalScoutEmission.description:
One finding a scout run emitted to the inbox — the persisted, queryable record of
*what* the run surfaced, returned by `scout-runs-emissions-list`. The emitted text
lives in `description`; `source_id` is the join key (`run:<run_id>:finding:<finding_id>`)
back into the underlying signal store.

description.description: The emitted finding prose — the signal's `description` as surfaced to the inbox.

emitted_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the finding was emitted.

finding_id.description: Stable id the finding was emitted under; matches an entry in the run's `emitted_finding_ids`.

run_id.description: UUID of the `SignalScoutRun` that emitted this finding.

severity.description:
Optional severity tag — one of P0, P1, P2, P3, P4 — or null if the run didn't set one.

* `P0` - P0
* `P1` - P1
* `P2` - P2
* `P3` - P3
* `P4` - P4

source_id.description: Deterministic `run:<run_id>:finding:<finding_id>` — the join key into the underlying signal store.

tags.description: Slug tags the scout attached to this finding (lowercase kebab-case, e.g. `cost-spike`). Empty list when the run set none.

SignalScoutManualRun.description:
Response for an on-demand (`run now`) scout dispatch.

The run executes asynchronously on the Temporal worker, so there is no `SignalScoutRun`
row yet at response time — the bridge row is created once the run's first turn starts.
Poll the scout's runs (`scout-runs-list`) to see the resulting run and its findings.

skill_name.description: The `signals-scout-*` skill that was dispatched.

started.description: True when a new run was dispatched. The endpoint returns 409 instead when a run for this scout is already in progress.

workflow_id.description: Temporal workflow id for the dispatched run. The run executes asynchronously; poll the scout's runs to see the resulting run row, its status, and any emitted findings.

SignalScoutManualRunRequest.description:
Request body for an on-demand (`run now`) scout dispatch.

Every field is optional: a plain trigger sends no body at all.

note.description: Optional steering for this run only, such as 'focus on the checkout regression' or 'skip the staging traffic today'. The agent reads it alongside the scout's durable notes and weighs it the same way: it directs attention, it never forces a finding. Use it instead of leaving a scout note that would also steer every later scheduled run. The note is kept on the run for history and is never read by another run. Because the agent reads it verbatim while holding privileged tools, a run that carries one needs `llm_skill:write` on top of `signal_scout:write`, plus editor access to skills, the same bar as leaving a note.

inbox.description: Whether this scout's reports appear in the shared inbox. Defaults to true. Set false to keep the reports this scout authors out of the inbox and its Slack notifications, for example for a digest scout read in Slack. Reports this scout only edits are not affected. An update that omits this key keeps the stored value.

slack.description: Slack destination for each emitted scout finding or report. Null or omitted disables Slack delivery.

webhook.description: The CDP destination another product provisioned for this scout's reports. Null or omitted means no webhook. Unlike Slack, Signals does not deliver this itself: the reference lives here so the owning product can manage the destination's lifecycle.

inbox.description: Whether this scout's reports appear in the shared inbox. Defaults to true. Set false to keep the reports this scout authors out of the inbox and its Slack notifications, for example for a digest scout read in Slack. Reports this scout only edits are not affected. An update that omits this key keeps the stored value.

slack.description: Slack destination for each emitted scout finding or report. Null or omitted disables Slack delivery.

webhook.description: The CDP destination another product provisioned for this scout's reports. Null or omitted means no webhook. Unlike Slack, Signals does not deliver this itself: the reference lives here so the owning product can manage the destination's lifecycle.

acting_user.description: The member scheduled runs check the query as, when that is not you. The test runs with your access, so a table you can read can still fail on a scheduled run, and the run then starts as if there were no pre-check. Null when scheduled runs check it as you.

columns.description: The column names of the result, in order.

error.description: Why the query failed, when it failed. A syntax or schema error is given as written; other failures read as a general message. Null when the query ran.

interval_minutes.description: The value bound to `{interval_minutes}`: the scout's rolling interval, or for a cron schedule the gap in minutes between the fire times around now.

reason.description:
Why: `rows` (the query found rows), `no_rows` (it found none, so the run is skipped), `false_value` (it returned one false value, so the run is skipped), or `query_error` (the query failed, so the run starts as if there were no pre-check).

* `rows` - Rows
* `no_rows` - No Rows
* `false_value` - False Value
* `query_error` - Query Error

row_count.description: How many rows the query returned, at most 50.

rows_text.description: The rows as the scout reads them: one JSON object per line, cut before the text passes the size limit. Empty when the query returned no rows or failed.

since.description: The value bound to `{since}`: the start of the last run that ran, or when the scout was created.

would_run.description: Whether a scheduled run that started now would run the scout. False means it would skip the run.

precheck_query.description: HogQL `SELECT` to try, with the same `{since}`, `{now}` and `{interval_minutes}` placeholders a saved pre-check gets. Omit it, or pass null or blank, to try the scout's effective query: its own `precheck_query`, or the default its skill ships.

SignalScoutRunDetail.description:
Full `SignalScoutRun` projection used by `get-run`. Same shape as the summary
today; kept distinct so future detail-only extensions (linked Signal rows,
LLMA token-cost join) can land here without bloating the list response.

completed_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the TaskRun completed; null while still running.

created_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the bridge row was created — the field `date_from` / `date_to` filter and order on. Use this (not `started_at`) as the `date_to` cursor when walking past the 100-row cap, so runs created in the gap between a boundary run's TaskRun and its bridge row aren't skipped.

edited_report_ids.description: The `SignalReport` ids this run mutated via the `edit_report` channel (rewrote title/summary and/or appended a note), deduped. Distinct from `emitted_report_ids`: edit can target any inbox report, so these are generally not reports the run authored. Empty for runs that edited no report.

emitted_count.description: Number of findings this run actually emitted to the inbox. 0 for runs that investigated but surfaced nothing, or ran dry-run / before AI approval. `> 0` means the run produced at least one `Signal`.

emitted_finding_ids.description: The `finding_id`s behind `emitted_count`, in emit order. Each maps to a `Signal` with `source_id = run:<run_id>:finding:<finding_id>`. Empty for non-emitting runs.

emitted_report_ids.description: The `SignalReport` ids this run authored directly via the `emit_report` channel, in emit order. Separate from `emitted_finding_ids` (weak `emit_signal` findings) — a report-authoring scout writes a full report here instead. Empty for runs that authored no report.

error.description: Full `error_message` from the linked TaskRun, surfaced only for failed/cancelled runs (null otherwise, including on success). Use `failure_reason` for a concise scan-friendly summary.

failure_reason.description: Concise derived reason the run didn't complete cleanly — the first line of `error` (bounded), or a status-derived fallback. Null unless the run terminated failed/cancelled. Read this to see at a glance *why* a run emitted nothing without pulling full stack traces.

metadata.description: Scout-owned per-run context, in two regions. Top-level keys are stamped by the runner at run start. Always present: `harness_prompt_version` (id of the harness prompt build the run was given), `report_channel` (which report tools the run held: `none`, `emit`, `edit`, or `both`), `skill_origin` (`canonical` or `custom`), `github_guidance` (whether the run got the GitHub evidence section), and `business_knowledge_maintained` (whether the run got the business-knowledge section: the product flag is on and the team's knowledge base looks maintained) — the provenance set that says which instructions the run actually got, so runs are only compared against runs of the same shape. Present only when the run departed from a default: `model`, `runtime_adapter`, and `reasoning_effort` (routing overrode the agent-server default), `network_access` (`full` when the scout's config lifted the trusted-domain network restriction for this run), `write_scopes` (the extra write access the run's token carried, when the scout was granted any), and `triggered_by` (`manual` or `workflow` when the run was fired off-schedule; absent means the run came from the coordinator's schedule). The nested `derived` object is the harness's own map of boolean run dimensions, computed server-side at finalize: `has_emit_report`, `has_edit_report`, `has_self_improvement`, `has_chart`, `has_self_validation`, `has_structured_output`, and `has_not_in_use_closeout` (the run wrote a `not-in-use:` scratchpad entry and produced no report, finding, or structured output). Use `derived` to answer 'what kind of run was this?' instead of parsing the `summary` prose. Note the flags describe the reports the run authored as they stand now, so charts attached to someone else's report via an edit are not counted. A missing `derived` object is unknown, not all-false: the run predates the field, never finalized, or its stamp failed.

run_id.description: UUID of the bridge row.

skill_name.description: Canonical skill name the run executed (e.g. `signals-scout-general`).

skill_version.description: Skill version snapshotted at run start.

started_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the TaskRun was created.

status.description:
Status from the linked TaskRun.

* `not_started` - not_started
* `queued` - queued
* `in_progress` - in_progress
* `completed` - completed
* `failed` - failed
* `cancelled` - cancelled

summary.description: One-paragraph close-out the scout wrote at end-of-run. Empty string for runs that errored before close-out. The dedupe key for non-emitting runs.

task_id.description: UUID of the Tasks `Task` the scout span ran inside.

task_run_id.description: UUID of the Tasks `TaskRun`. Pairs with `task_id` to deep-link.

task_url.description: Relative deep-link to the Tasks UI for this run, e.g. `/project/{team_id}/tasks/{task_id}?runId={task_run_id}`.

total_spend.description: Accounted customer spend in USD cents, including fractional cents. May be partial; null for untracked runs.
